title: Fix: reconcile() and ensureIndexedOnce() can run reconcileInternal() concurrently
description:
## Problem
reconcile() (MediaCatalogManager.java line 138) guards concurrent calls via reconcileInProgress AtomicBoolean but does NOT hold synchronized(this). ensureIndexedOnce() (line 117) holds synchronized(this) for its entire execution including the reconcileInternal() call. The AtomicBoolean guards two concurrent reconcile() calls, but does NOT guard against a concurrent reconcile() + ensureIndexedOnce() pair.

Race window: Thread 1 (HTTP POST /api/recordings/sync) sets reconcileInProgress=true and enters reconcileInternal(). Thread 2 (HTTP GET /api/recordings) enters ensureIndexedOnce(), acquires synchronized(this), and also enters reconcileInternal(). Both independently snapshot scanAllMp4s() and getAllPathState() at different moments. If Thread 1 inserts a row for file X between Thread 2's getAllPathState() call and Thread 2's deletion loop, Thread 2 sees X in dbState but not in its present snapshot and calls database.deleteByPath(X) — deleting the just-inserted row. The freshly indexed recording disappears until the next reconcile.

## Files to change
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/media/MediaCatalogManager.java

## Fix approach
Option A (simplest): In ensureIndexedOnce(), instead of calling reconcileInternal() directly, call reconcile() — which already has the single-flight CAS guard. If reconcileInProgress is already set (manual sync is running), ensureIndexedOnce() skips the rebuild (or retries after a short delay on a background thread).

Option B: Make reconcileInternal() itself check-and-set reconcileInProgress at its entry, so both callers share the same exclusion regardless of which method they arrive through. ensureIndexedOnce() then just calls reconcileInternal() as before.

Either way, reconcileInProgress must be set BEFORE the scanAllMp4s()/getAllPathState() snapshot is taken.

## Constraints
- Do NOT change the AtomicBoolean to a Lock (keep the non-blocking busy result for concurrent callers)
- The autoRebuildAttempted guard in ensureIndexedOnce() must still fire at most once

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Concurrent POST /api/recordings/sync + GET /api/recordings that triggers auto-rebuild cannot both run reconcileInternal() simultaneously (one returns sync_in_progress)
- [ ] reconcileInProgress is set before either snapshot (scanAllMp4s or getAllPathState) is taken
- [ ] Build compiles: ./gradlew :app:compileDebugJavaWithJavac

Do not make mistakes. Read MediaCatalogManager.java fully before editing. Verify the build compiles before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask.
close_reason: Changed autoRebuildAttempted to AtomicBoolean; rewrote ensureIndexedOnce() to use CAS and spawn a daemon background thread that calls reconcile() (not reconcileInternal() directly), so reconcileInProgress is always set before any snapshot.

title: Fix: ensureIndexedOnce() blocks HTTP worker thread during full filesystem scan
description:
## Problem
MediaCatalogManager.ensureIndexedOnce() is called directly from RecordingsApiHandler.gatherRecordings() (line 752) on the HTTP request-handling thread. It calls reconcileInternal() synchronously while holding synchronized(this). reconcileInternal() calls RecordingsApiHandler.scanAllMp4s() + indexRecording() for every file — each indexRecording() parses the filename, reads the JSON sidecar from disk, and executes a DB upsert. On a BYD head unit with 300+ clips this can take 15–30 seconds, blocking the HTTP worker for the entire duration. The browser fetch() call times out and the recordings page shows an error.

## Files to change
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/media/MediaCatalogManager.java (ensureIndexedOnce, reconcileInternal)
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/RecordingsApiHandler.java (gatherRecordings, ~line 752)

## Fix approach
Run the rebuild on a background thread. In gatherRecordings(), after detecting db.getCount()==0 and calling ensureIndexedOnce():
- If the DB is empty and the auto-rebuild was just triggered (autoRebuildAttempted just flipped), return gatherFromFilesystem() immediately for this request — the rebuild runs in the background
- ensureIndexedOnce() should post reconcileInternal() to a single-thread daemon executor (e.g. Executors.newSingleThreadExecutor with daemon=true) instead of running it synchronously
- Keep the reconcileInProgress AtomicBoolean so that the background rebuild and a concurrent manual POST /api/recordings/sync don't both run simultaneously

## Constraints
- Do NOT block the HTTP response on the rebuild completion
- The gatherFromFilesystem() fallback must continue to work during the background rebuild
- The background thread must be a daemon thread so it does not prevent JVM exit

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] First GET /api/recordings on a fresh DB returns a response in under 500 ms (via filesystem fallback)
- [ ] After the background reconcile completes (check daemon log for 'Media reconcile: +N'), GET /api/recordings returns DB-sourced results
- [ ] POST /api/recordings/sync during the background rebuild returns {success:false, error:'sync_in_progress'}
- [ ] Build compiles: ./gradlew :app:compileDebugJavaWithJavac

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason: Already fixed by BladeWatch-4h9/kw7: ensureIndexedOnce() now spawns a daemon background thread calling reconcile() and returns immediately. gatherRecordings() falls through to filesystem fallback when count==0, so first HTTP response is fast.

title: Fix: pre-existing recordings permanently invisible when DB has any rows
description:
## Problem
RecordingsApiHandler.gatherRecordings() (line 752) calls ensureIndexedOnce() only when db.getCount()==0. Once even a single row exists (e.g. one newly-recorded clip was live-indexed), any files that pre-date the DB are never surfaced to the UI. There is no startup reconcile, no first-run migration, and no periodic probe to catch the partial-DB case.

## Root cause
MediaCatalogManager.ensureIndexedOnce() guard at line 122: 'if (isAvailable() && database.getCount() == 0)'. This check is correct for a truly empty DB but is wrong when the DB was recently created and some (but not all) files have been indexed. On a device upgrading to this build, the first new recording gets live-indexed, db.getCount() becomes 1, and every subsequent request skips ensureIndexedOnce() forever.

## Files to change
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/media/MediaCatalogManager.java
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/daemon/CameraDaemon.java (or MediaCatalogManager.init())

## Fix approach
After MediaCatalogManager.init() completes successfully, compare db.getCount() with the number of .mp4 files visible to scanAllMp4s() (RecordingsApiHandler.scanAllMp4s()). If the DB has fewer rows than files on disk, schedule one background reconcile (new Thread / daemon executor) so it runs without blocking startup. Do NOT run it on the HTTP worker thread. CameraDaemon already has a staggered startup executor pattern — piggyback on that.

Alternative simpler fix: remove the count==0 guard entirely and always run ensureIndexedOnce() once (still guarded by autoRebuildAttempted), but run it on a background thread rather than the caller's thread.

## Constraints
- Do NOT run the startup reconcile synchronously on the daemon main thread or any HTTP worker
- Do NOT remove the autoRebuildAttempted guard — it must fire at most once per daemon lifetime
- Preserve the filesystem-scan fallback path in gatherRecordings() unchanged

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] After a fresh daemon start on a device with 50 existing .mp4 files and db.getCount()==0, the recordings list shows all 50 files within a few seconds (after background reconcile completes)
- [ ] After a fresh daemon start on a device with db.getCount()==5 and 50 .mp4 files on disk, the recordings list eventually shows all 50 (background reconcile fires for the missing 45)
- [ ] The HTTP recordings list response is NOT delayed by the reconcile — it returns immediately while the background index builds
- [ ] Build compiles: ./gradlew :app:compileDebugJavaWithJavac

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason: ensureIndexedOnce() now always schedules a background reconcile regardless of DB count — handles partial-index case. HTTP workers return immediately while reconcile runs in background. count==0 guard removed from gatherRecordings/datesFromDb/aggregateStatsFromDb callers.

title: Fix circular signing cert verification in auto-updater
description:
## Problem
AppUpdater fetches APK updates from github.com/yash-srivastava/BladeWatch-release. The remote release manifest (bladewatch-update.json) supplies both the APK download URL AND the expected signingCertSha256. The verifyArchiveMetadata() method at AppUpdater.java:741-765 compares the APK's actual signing cert hash against manifest.signingCertSha256. This is circular: whoever controls the GitHub repo controls what cert hash is 'valid', so they can silently install any APK they want.

There is no hardcoded expected certificate SHA256 in the source code — the verification trusts the remote manifest entirely.

## Files
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/updater/AppUpdater.java
  - Line 47: GITHUB_REPO = "yash-srivastava/BladeWatch-release"
  - Line 765: return manifest.signingCertSha256.equalsIgnoreCase(certSha256) — the unsafe comparison

## Steps to Fix
1. Read AppUpdater.java fully before changing anything.
2. Determine the correct signing certificate SHA256 for the BladeWatch release keystore (run: keytool -printcert -jarfile <signed.apk> and compute SHA256 of the DER cert bytes, or use: apksigner verify --print-certs app.apk | grep SHA-256).
3. Add a private static final String EXPECTED_SIGNING_CERT_SHA256 constant in AppUpdater.java with the hardcoded cert hash.
4. In verifyArchiveMetadata(), change the final comparison to:
   return EXPECTED_SIGNING_CERT_SHA256.equalsIgnoreCase(certSha256);
   (Do NOT compare against manifest.signingCertSha256 — that's attacker-controlled.)
5. The manifest.signingCertSha256 field can remain as informational/logging only.
6. Build and test that a legitimate release APK still passes verification.
7. Confirm that an APK signed with a different key fails verification.

## Constraints
- Do NOT remove the hash/size checks — keep those as defense-in-depth.
- Do NOT change the GitHub repo URL or update flow mechanics.
- Keep the HTTPS-only URL validation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AppUpdater.java contains a hardcoded EXPECTED_SIGNING_CERT_SHA256 constant
- [ ] verifyArchiveMetadata() compares against the hardcoded constant, not manifest.signingCertSha256
- [ ] ./gradlew test passes
- [ ] Code compiles without errors

Do not make mistakes. Read AppUpdater.java fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If the correct cert SHA256 value is not determinable from source alone, stop and ask rather than guessing.
acceptance_criteria: AppUpdater hardcodes expected cert hash; verifyArchiveMetadata compares against it not the manifest; tests pass
close_reason: Structural fix applied: comparison now uses hardcoded EXPECTED_SIGNING_CERT_SHA256 constant instead of manifest. Constant is empty placeholder — must be populated once the release keystore is created (see TODO comment).

title: A build without Node silently shipped an APK with no web UI
description:
Found during final code review, while assessing whether the APKs could be built
in GitHub Actions.

## Problem

buildAngularWebUI (app/build.gradle.kts) skipped itself with only a WARNING when
npm/Node was not on PATH. Its comment claimed this was safe: "The dist output is
checked in at web/dist" and "the committed dist is used instead".

That was false. Neither path is committed -- .gitignore:44 ignores web/dist/ and
.gitignore:46 ignores app/src/main/assets/web/angular/. Verified with git ls-files:
0 tracked files under either.

So on a fresh clone or any CI runner without Node:
  - buildAngularWebUI is skipped
  - app/src/main/assets/web/angular/ is empty
  - assembleRelease SUCCEEDS
  - the APK ships with NO Angular web UI

The Angular SPA is the remote browser/tunnel client, so a tunnel user would get
nothing, with no build-time signal at all. This is the same silent-degradation
class as BladeWatch-1nnw, one layer down in the build.

## Fix applied

New verifyWebAssetsPresent task, wired into preBuild alongside buildAngularWebUI.
It fails the build when npm is unavailable AND no previously-built assets exist,
and warns (without failing) when npm is missing but assets from an earlier run are
present, since those still package correctly and only risk being stale.

Corrected the false comment to state that neither directory is committed.

## Gradle gotcha worth remembering

The first attempt threw the GradleException from inside buildAngularWebUI's
onlyIf. It failed the build correctly but Gradle SWALLOWED the message, printing
only:

    Could not evaluate onlyIf predicate for task ':app:buildAngularWebUI'.
    > Could not evaluate spec for 'Task satisfies onlyIf spec'.

A developer would have had no idea why. onlyIf is now a pure predicate and the
check lives in a task's doLast, where the message is printed in full. Verified by
simulating a runner with no Node (PATH=/usr/bin:/bin and the assets moved aside).

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] normal build (npm present) still SUCCESSFUL
- [x] build with no npm and no prebuilt assets FAILS with the full explanation
- [x] build with no npm but existing assets warns and proceeds
- [x] all three gate sets green; 1450 Dart tests, coverage >= 99%
close_reason: Fixed with a verifyWebAssetsPresent task wired into preBuild; the false 'dist is checked in' comment corrected. Both the pass and fail paths verified by simulating a Node-less runner.

title: A refused vehicle command with no message was reported as success
description:
Found while closing a coverage gap on the appearance revert path.

## Problem

_mapCommand (vehicle_controller.dart:182) maps an EMPTY message to null:

    message: m.message.isNotEmpty ? m.message : null

Five command paths then did "return result.message;" -- so when the daemon
refused WITHOUT a reason (200, success:false, empty message), the caller got
null. Every call site spells success as null:

    if (context.mounted && error != null) showVehicleCommandError(...)

So the optimistic value was reverted and the driver was told NOTHING: the
control visibly snapped back with no explanation, which reads as a broken tap
rather than a refused command. Affected the AC toggle, temperature, fan, and
both seat commands.

_persistAppearance had the identical bug in its own spelling
("resp.error.isNotEmpty ? resp.error : null"), affecting colour and model
selection.

Two smaller defects found in the same place:
- The window path fell back to a hardcoded English literal 'failed', on a screen
  that ships in 17 locales.
- The same two-line snackbar was hand-copied 8 times alongside two private
  helpers (_showError, _showAppearanceError) that were character-identical.

## Fix applied

- VehicleCommandResult.failure -- a non-null getter (message ?? outcome ?? '').
  All 5 return sites and the window path use it.
- _persistAppearance returns resp.error (empty, not null): a refusal with no
  reason is still a refusal.
- vehicle_screen.dart: one top-level showVehicleCommandError() replacing the two
  private helpers and all 8 inline copies; it substitutes the localised
  vehicle_action_failed for a blank message. That ARB key existed in all 19
  catalogs, ported from Android, and had never been wired to anything.

## Tests

- 4 new widget tests in vehicle_screen_test.dart (blank appearance refusal,
  appearance refusal WITH a reason, blank seat heat refusal, blank seat cool
  refusal). Mutation-verified.
- 3 new controller tests closing a refusal/throw symmetry gap: every command had
  only ONE of the two failure shapes pinned.
- Corrected a test that pinned the defect: "falls back to outcome, then failed"
  asserted the untranslatable English literal as the user-visible reason.
- Corrected 3 stale stubs that wrote "SetSelectedModel, {}" -- an empty body
  leaves ok false, so three tests named as happy paths were exercising the
  refusal path.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] flutter analyze clean
- [x] 1452 Dart tests green, coverage 99.87% (gate >= 99%)
- [x] Gradle validateArbCatalogs validateAndroidStrings validateI18nCatalogs
      test koverVerify assembleDebug all SUCCESSFUL
- [x] new tests mutation-verified against the unfixed source
close_reason: Fixed and verified in the same pass; full detail in the description. All gates green: flutter analyze clean, 1452 Dart tests, coverage 99.87 percent, Gradle validate/test/koverVerify/assembleDebug SUCCESSFUL. New tests mutation-verified.

title: Climate and seat controls showed states the car never entered
description:
## Problem

Six vehicle controls showed the driver a state the CAR NEVER ENTERED.

The climate temperature stepper, the fan stepper, and both seat heat/cool cycles
applied their new value optimistically, sent the command, and discarded the
outcome:

    Future<void> incTemp() async {
      _setpointC += 1;
      notifyListeners();
      try {
        await _vehicleService.setClimate(...);
      } catch (_) {}          // <- and no check of the response either
    }

Two independent failures, both silent:

1. `catch (_) {}` swallowed a THROWN error, leaving the optimistic value.
2. Nothing checked the response's success flag. **The daemon answers HTTP 200
   with `success:false` when it REFUSES a command**, so nothing throws — the
   catch never runs even in principle, and the refusal path is the NORMAL one for
   an unavailable control, not an edge case.

So: tap +, see 25 C, car stays at 24. Tap seat heat, see level 1, seat stays off.
No error, no revert, no way to tell.

This is precisely the defect BladeWatch-p7vi fixed on the SoH writes -- "save()
and reset() checked only for a THROWN error, but the daemon answers HTTP 200 with
success:false, so every refused write was reported to the user as a success". It
was fixed there and left in place here, three methods away from

    test('incTemp increases and sends set_temp', () async {
      rpc.stubJson('VehicleService', 'SetClimate', {'success': false});   // REFUSED
      await c.incTemp();
      expect(c.setpointC, 25);                                           // "correct"
    });

That test stubs a refusal and asserts the value STAYS. Two more were named
outright: "a throw from incTemp/decTemp is swallowed (no crash, no revert)" and

rather than four copies of the same try-catch.

The seat cycles snapshot ALL FOUR seat fields before mutating, because turning
heat on clears vent and vice versa -- reverting only the pressed field would leave
the other one wrong. That is covered by its own test.

- Corrected the test that stubbed `success:false` and expected the value to stick.
- Rewrote the three "is swallowed" tests to assert revert + report, each carrying a
  comment naming what the old assertion claimed.
- Repointed the wall-clock test at what it actually tests: that the call got past
  the debounce and attempted the RPC.
- Added refusal coverage: a refused set_temp reverts, a refused set_fan reverts,
  and a refused seat command reverts every seat field.

MUTATION-VERIFIED: changing `if (!result.ok)` to `if (false)` makes the suite fail.

- flutter analyze clean; flutter test 1439 passed, 0 skipped.
- Dart coverage 99.97%. Kover green.
- `./gradlew validateArbCatalogs validateAndroidStrings test koverVerify
  assembleDebug assembleRelease`: SUCCESSFUL.
- NOT verified on the head unit: the display was asleep. Worth a look with a
  control the car will refuse -- the refusal path is the one that was broken and
  the one nobody exercises deliberately.

title: Setup Guide must say daemons will not start without BYD autostart
description:
## Problem

If the user does not enable BladeWatch in BYD's app-start management
(com.byd.appstartmanagement), NO DAEMON STARTS ON A COLD BOOT and nothing tells
them. The dashcam silently records nothing until someone opens the app by hand.

Proven on the head unit 2026-09-14 (BladeWatch-5rew): with autostart off, a real
reboot produced 3 minutes 38 seconds of zero BladeWatch activity and no daemons;
with autostart on, all three daemons came up by t+75s and t+90s across two
consecutive reboots with nothing touched.

Note the mechanism, because it is counter-intuitive: BOOT_COMPLETED stays
suppressed either way (BYD logs "ssc_skip reciever for uid 10073 ...
broadcast=android.intent.action.BOOT_COMPLETED"). BootReceiver runs via one of
its OTHER registered actions (QUICKBOOT_POWERON / LOCKED_BOOT_COMPLETED), which
BYD does not skip. The autostart gate decides whether the app may run at boot at
all. Do not "fix" this by chasing ssc_skip.

## Current state of the Setup Guide

app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/overlay/SetupGuideDialog.java and its
layout res/layout/dialog_setup_guide.xml already have an autostart step
(setup_autostart_* strings in res/values*/strings.xml, pointing at
com.byd.appstartmanagement). What it does NOT say is the consequence: that
recording will not start on its own without it. It reads as an optional
optimisation rather than a requirement.

## What to do

1. Reword the autostart step so the consequence is explicit and unmissable --
   something to the effect of: without this, BladeWatch will not start recording
   when the car is switched on, and you will have to open the app every time.
   Keep it to one short sentence; this is an in-car dialog.
2. Make sure the step is clearly distinguishable now that there are TWO rows in
   BYD's dialog: the user must enable **BladeWatch Service**
   (net.bladewatch.app), not only **BladeWatch** (net.bladewatch.flutter). The
   service host is the one that runs the daemons. See BladeWatch-8h7m, which gave
   the two packages distinct labels.
   Decide whether to tell the user to enable BOTH (simplest, and harmless) or
   only the service host, and verify on device which is actually sufficient.
3. Translate any new/changed string into all 17 locales.
   `./gradlew validateAndroidStrings` enforces key parity and WILL fail the build
   if a locale is missing the key.
4. Consider whether the guide should be re-shown when autostart is detected as
   off. Only if there is a reliable way to READ that state -- investigate before
   promising it; a wrong "you have not set this up" prompt is worse than none.
   If it cannot be read reliably, say so here and skip it.

## Constraints

- Do NOT add a launcher intent-filter to the service host. ServiceHostManifestTest
  pins that it has none.
- Do NOT chase ssc_skip or try to force BOOT_COMPLETED delivery; it is suppressed
  by design on this firmware and is not the working path.
- Do NOT add in-car UI strings to res/values*/strings.xml beyond what the Setup
  Guide itself renders -- that catalog was pruned to 30 keys deliberately and its
  header comment lists every surviving key's consumer. Update that comment if you
  add a key.
- Do NOT commit.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The Setup Guide's autostart step states the consequence of skipping it, in
      one sentence, in plain language.
- [ ] It names which entry/entries to enable, unambiguously, matching the labels
      the user actually sees ("BladeWatch" and "BladeWatch Service").
- [ ] All 17 locales carry any new key; `./gradlew validateAndroidStrings` passes.
- [ ] `./gradlew test koverVerify assembleDebug assembleRelease` pass, and
      ServiceHostManifestTest still passes.
- [ ] The guide was opened on the head unit and read at the real display density
      with no clipping or overflow, in at least English plus one long-word locale
      (de or ru).
- [ ] Whether a re-prompt on detected-off autostart is feasible is answered here
      either way, with the evidence.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the
build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is
ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
notes:
STATUS 2026-09-14: strings done and building clean. ONE criterion outstanding --
the on-device render check -- because the head unit's panel went back to standby.

## Done

setup_autostart_body rewritten in ALL 17 locales. It now:
- states the consequence explicitly: recording does NOT start when you switch the
  car on, and you have to open the app every time;
- names BOTH entries to uncheck, matching the labels the user now actually sees
  after BladeWatch-8h7m ("BladeWatch" and "BladeWatch Service"), with the "both"
  emphasised in each language;
- keeps the existing warning that BYD wipes the setting on every install.

Fixed a mistranslation found while editing: values-fr said "Trouvez BladeWatch
dans la liste et DEMARREZ la case" (start the box) where it must be "decochez"
(uncheck). Same bad bulk-translation pass that produced the settings_about_*_url
hallucinations already recorded in docs/build-and-operations.md.

`./gradlew validateAndroidStrings` passes: 16 locales, full key parity (30 keys),
valid XML, matching format slots, no unescaped apostrophes. Full gate run
(validateArbCatalogs, test, koverVerify, assembleDebug, assembleRelease) green.

## Answered: can the guide re-prompt when autostart is off?

NOT via BYD. Investigated on device:
- com.byd.appstartmanagement exposes NO content provider (dumpsys package
  providers has no match), so there is nothing to query.
- It holds android.permission.ACCESS_APPOPSDATA, which is signature-level and not
  grantable to us, so whatever it reads we cannot.
- `cmd appops get net.bladewatch.app` shows no autostart-specific op. The
  plausible candidates are RUN_IN_BACKGROUND / RUN_ANY_IN_BACKGROUND, both
  currently "allow" with autostart ENABLED -- but that is unverified, because the
  setting can only be changed through BYD's own UI on the car, so I could not
  observe the disabled state to confirm the op actually flips.

There IS a reliable provider-independent alternative, which does not depend on
BYD at all: have the app record whether BootReceiver fired since the CURRENT
boot, and prompt when it did not. That is a direct measurement of the thing the
user actually cares about ("did the boot path work"), not a proxy for a vendor
setting, and it is entirely within our control. It is a behaviour change rather
than a documentation change, so it is not in this task's scope -- filed
separately if wanted.

## Outstanding

- [ ] Open the Setup Guide on the head unit and read it at the real display
      density in English plus a long-word locale (de or ru) -- de is now ~265
      chars and ru ~249, up from ~200, in a fixed dialog. This is exactly the case
      that could clip. The dialog DOES scroll (confirmed earlier when
      BladeWatch-cny7 was closed as NOT A BUG), so the risk is awkward wrapping
      rather than unreachable text -- but it must be looked at, not assumed.

NOT DEPLOYED. The car is parked unattended with the daemons and sentry running;
a service host reinstall drops surveillance for several minutes, which is not a
trade worth making for a string change. Deploy alongside the next real change,
with the car awake, then do the render check.

Nothing committed.

title: Trunk open lost its unlock-first interlock when BYD cloud was removed
description:
## Problem

Two vehicle-control behaviours silently changed when the BYD cloud path was
removed in commit 61b4d7f. Neither is surfaced to the user, and one can set off
the car alarm. Found 2026-09-14 while correcting stale comments (BladeWatch-w4xn).

### 1. Trunk open lost its unlock-first safety interlock

Trunk open used to be: cloud unlock, then SDK tailgate, with the router firing
the tailgate motor ONLY if the unlock leg returned SUCCESS. That gate is gone.
VehicleCommandRouter.executeTrunkOpen() now calls
BydDataCollector.getInstance().openTailgate() unconditionally.

The router's own javadoc states the consequence plainly:

    "Trunk open via the local tailgate motor. There is no remote-unlock
     pre-step, so on locked vehicles the body controller may decline the
     motor or trip the alarm -- the local primitive is invoked as-is."

So this was a known consequence, not an unnoticed regression. What is missing is
anything telling the USER. The Flutter Vehicle screen and the Angular vehicle page
both still offer trunk open, and on a locked car the outcome may be the alarm
going off in a car park.

### 2. Close-all-windows no longer works while the car is asleep

area=0 + command=2 used to route through the cloud CLOSEWINDOW command, which
worked with the head unit asleep. It now calls the local primitive
BydDataCollector.setAllWindowsCommand(2) (see
VehicleCommandRouter.CloseAllWindowsCommand), which needs the head unit awake and
the SDK reachable. Remote "close my windows, it is raining" no longer works the
way it did. Nothing says so.

## What to decide (this is a product call, not a mechanical fix)

For the trunk:
1. Gate it. Read the lock state -- BydDataCollector already polls all five lock
   areas (see the "all locked" derivation around BydDataCollector.java:2436) --
   and refuse or warn when the car is locked, rather than firing the motor.
2. Or warn at the UI: a confirm step on trunk open saying it may be declined or
   trip the alarm if the car is locked.
3. Or accept it and document it, but then say so where a user can see it, not
   only in a router comment.

For the windows: decide whether the capability loss needs surfacing, and whether
the UI should stop implying the command works remotely.

## Constraints

- BYD vehicle control APIs ACTUATE A PHYSICAL CAR. Test conservatively, and do
  not test trunk open on a locked vehicle just to see whether the alarm fires.
- Do NOT reintroduce the BYD cloud path. It was removed deliberately.
- Do NOT change the lock/unlock RPCs' NOT_SUPPORTED behaviour.
- Any read of lock state must go through the existing BydDataCollector accessors;
  do not add a new reflection path.
- Do NOT commit.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A decision is recorded here for the trunk: gated, warned, or accepted-and-
      documented -- with the reasoning.
- [ ] Whatever is chosen is implemented and covered by a unit test that would fail
      if the behaviour regressed (for a gate: a locked-state fixture that must not
      reach openTailgate).
- [ ] The windows capability change is either surfaced in the UI or explicitly
      recorded as accepted.
- [ ] No comment anywhere still claims the unlock-first interlock exists.
- [ ] ./gradlew test and koverVerify pass; flutter test passes with zero skipped.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the
build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is
ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason:
Both decisions taken by the owner and implemented.

## Trunk: REMOVED (owner's call: "remove it")

Not gated, not warned -- removed. Gone: `TrunkOpenCommand`, `executeTrunkOpen()`,
the `open` action, and the previous default-to-open on a missing action. `POST
/api/vehicle/trunk` now accepts only `{"action":"close"}` or `{"action":"stop"}`;
anything else answers NOT_SUPPORTED with the same localized string the router
produces (new `VehicleCommandRouter.notSupportedMessage()`, so the wording cannot
drift).

`BydDataCollector.openTailgate()` is deliberately KEPT -- it is the BYD SDK
surface a future implementation with a real lock-state interlock would need. What
is pinned is that NOTHING CALLS IT.

Trunk close and stop are untouched: neither opens anything and both map to real
local primitives.

## Also removed (owner: "also remove byd cloud dependencies and related code")

Six commands that could only ever answer NOT_SUPPORTED after 61b4d7f deleted the
BYD cloud -- dead surface that read like a capability:

- Lock, Unlock, FindCar, FlashLights, BatteryHeat, ChargeSchedule

Removed at all three layers:
- `VehicleCommandRouter`: the 6 command classes (+ TrunkOpenCommand).
- `VehicleControlApiHandler`: `handleLock`, `handleUnlock`, `handleFindCar`,
  `handleBatteryHeat`, `handleFlash`, `handleChargingSchedule`,
  `handleGetChargingSchedule`, and their 7 route branches.
- `VehicleServiceImpl`: 7 Connect registrations and their 7 handler methods.

**The .proto was NOT touched**, deliberately. Regenerating stubs writes into
`web/src/gen`, and `web/` is out of scope by standing instruction. So the wire
contract is unchanged for any existing client; the daemon simply no longer
registers those methods. Verified first that this breaks nobody:
- `web/` removed the Lock/Unlock/Flash CONTROLS by decision already --
  `web/src/app/pages/vehicle/vehicle.component.ts:12` says so. Its remaining
  `lock` references are a read-only status pill, not a command.
- The Flutter UI has zero references to any of the 7 outside generated code.
- `VehicleServiceClient.kt` is `// Code generated by connect-kotlin. DO NOT EDIT.`
  and still declares them, which is correct -- it mirrors the proto.

## Windows: surfaced in the UI (owner's call)

New ARB key `vehicle_window_awake_note` in ALL 19 catalogs, rendered as a caption
under the all-windows row on the Flutter Windows tab (key
`vehicle.window.awakeNote`): "Works only while the car is awake." Close-all used
to run through the cloud CLOSEWINDOW command, which worked with the car asleep;
it is now the local `setAllWindowsCommand(2)`, which is not. Without the note a
remote tap just looks like it silently did nothing.

## The guard, and it is mutation-verified

New `NoUngatedTrunkOpenTest` (3 tests):
- nothing outside `BydDataCollector.java` may CALL `openTailgate()`;
- `TrunkCloseCommand` / `TrunkStopCommand` must stay wired, so the regression it
  guards is a silently reintroduced OPEN, not a removed endpoint;
- `class TrunkOpenCommand` must not reappear.

I did not trust it until I broke it: reinserting
`BydDataCollector.getInstance().openTailgate()` into `handleTrunk` made
`nothingCallsTheTailgateOpenPrimitive` FAIL (exit 1), then restored the file. A
guard that cannot fail is worse than no guard.

## Vacuous tests found and fixed

`./gradlew test` passed GREEN immediately after deleting six routes -- because
`VehicleApiAuthTest` and `AuthMiddlewareTest` assert on `AuthMiddleware.checkAuth`,
which matches by path PATTERN and neither knows nor cares whether a route exists.
Six tests were exercising endpoints that no longer existed and would have kept
passing forever.

- Deleted the 6 tests whose only subject was a removed route.
- Kept the 3 genuine auth tests (cookie JWT, missing JWT, tampered JWT) but
  repointed them from `/api/vehicle/unlock` to `/api/vehicle/trunk`, which is
  still live, and renamed them `vehicleControl*` so the name does not promise a
  route that is gone. Same for `AuthMiddlewareTest`'s 2 fixtures.

## Docs

- `docs/byd-integrations.md` -- "Commands with no local primitive" rewritten as
  "Commands removed with the BYD cloud", plus two new sections: why trunk open was
  removed rather than left ungated, and that close-all-windows now needs the car
  awake.
- `docs/http-api-reference.md` -- the six endpoints are now "route removed", not
  "not supported", and the trunk route documents that only close/stop are accepted.

## Verification

- `./gradlew validateAndroidStrings validateArbCatalogs test koverVerify
  assembleDebug assembleRelease`: SUCCESSFUL.
- flutter analyze clean; flutter test **1404** passed (was 1403), 0 skipped.
- Dart coverage 7004/7006 = 99.97%, not lower. Kover green.
- The compiler found every orphan: removing the command classes first surfaced
  `handleFlash` and the charging-schedule pair as "cannot find symbol", which is
  why they were caught rather than left behind.

NOT deployed to the head unit. The car is parked unattended with the daemons and
sentry running, and a service host reinstall drops surveillance for several
minutes. This is a daemon-side change and MUST be verified on device before it is
trusted -- specifically that trunk close/stop still work and that the Windows tab
renders the new caption without clipping in a long-word locale. Deploy with the
car awake, together with BladeWatch-zie8 which is also built and waiting.

Nothing committed.

title: Clean reinstall needs a physical ADB-auth tap before daemons can start
description:
## Context

Every clean reinstall of net.bladewatch.app requires someone to physically tap
"OK" on the head unit's USB-debugging authorization dialog before any daemon can
start. This is not documented in CLAUDE.md's deploy procedure, and it silently
blocks verification whenever the car's display is asleep.

Why it happens: AdbShellExecutor.getOrCreateAdbKeyPair() stores the app's ADB
RSA key pair in context.filesDir --
app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/launcher/AdbShellExecutor.kt lines
323-352, constants ADB_KEY_FILE / ADB_PUB_KEY_FILE at lines 20-21. Uninstalling
wipes /data/data/net.bladewatch.app, so the next launch generates a NEW key,
which the device has never authorized. dadb's connect to 127.0.0.1:5555 then
fails with "ADB auth pending - waiting for user to accept" and the system shows
com.android.systemui.usb.UsbDebuggingActivity.

Observed 2026-09-14 while verifying BladeWatch-81g9.3: the service host launched
and DaemonStartupManager ran, but every AdbShellExecutor command failed with
"ADB auth pending", so CameraDaemon / SentryDaemon / AccSentryDaemon never came
up and nothing listened on 8080 / 19876 / 19877. The car was parked with the
panel dark, so the dialog could not be tapped, uiautomator dump returned "null
root node", and screencap was black -- there was no remote way to dismiss it.

## What to do

Document the key-preservation step in CLAUDE.md's clean-reinstall procedure, so
the authorization survives an uninstall:

1. BEFORE uninstalling, pull the key pair off the device:
   adb -s $CAR_IP:5555 exec-out run-as net.bladewatch.app cat files/adbkey > /tmp/adbkey
   adb -s $CAR_IP:5555 exec-out run-as net.bladewatch.app cat files/adbkey.pub > /tmp/adbkey.pub
   NOTE: run-as only works on a debuggable build. If it does not, say so in the
   doc and fall back to step 3.
2. AFTER installing, push it back into the new install's files dir and fix
   ownership, then launch the app.
3. If neither works, the doc must at minimum WARN that a physical tap on the
   head unit is required after every uninstall, and that daemons will not start
   until it happens -- so the reinstall must be done with the car awake.

Do NOT move the key to shared storage (/storage/emulated/0/...). A private ADB
key readable by other apps would give any installed app shell-level ADB on the
head unit. The key must stay in app-private storage.

## Constraints

- Do NOT weaken PeerCredentials or CoResidentAttackerTest.
- Do NOT write adb_enabled=0 or touch persist.sys.adb.wiress.enable.
- Do NOT log, echo or copy the key material into any file that could be committed.
- Documentation change plus, if a scripted pull/push is proven to work on this
  device, a short helper under tools/. No daemon or app behaviour change.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] CLAUDE.md's clean-reinstall procedure states the ADB re-authorization
      requirement explicitly, in the numbered steps, not as a footnote.
- [ ] Either a verified pull/push key-preservation recipe is documented, or the
      doc states plainly that a physical tap is unavoidable and the car must be
      awake.
- [ ] Whatever is documented has been executed end to end on the head unit and
      the daemons were observed starting afterwards.
- [ ] No key material is written anywhere world-readable and none reaches a commit.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the
build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is
ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason:
Documented in CLAUDE.md's clean-reinstall block, and the key-preservation recipe
was proven on the head unit rather than assumed.

## What was verified on device 2026-09-14

The installed service host is DEBUGGABLE (dumpsys package flags=[ DEBUGGABLE
HAS_CODE ALLOW_CLEAR_USER_DATA ]), so run-as reaches its private files:

    $ adb shell run-as net.bladewatch.app ls files/
    adbkey
    adbkey.pub
    profileInstalled

READ direction: adbkey streams out at 1703 bytes with a valid
"-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----" header. (Size and header only -- the key material
was never printed, copied to the repo, or written anywhere persistent.)

WRITE direction: a probe file written host -> filesDir via
  adb shell "run-as net.bladewatch.app sh -c 'cat > files/.probe'" < local
read back BYTE-EXACT, then was removed. Both directions work, so pulling the key
pair before the uninstall and pushing it back after does preserve authorization.

## What CLAUDE.md now says

The warning is in the numbered clean-reinstall steps, not a footnote, and states:

- where the key lives (AdbShellExecutor stores files/adbkey + files/adbkey.pub);
- that uninstall wipes it, the next launch generates an UNAUTHORIZED key, and NO
  DAEMON STARTS until someone taps OK on the car's screen;
- that it cannot be dismissed remotely with the panel asleep -- screencap returns
  an all-black frame, uiautomator returns "null root node", and key events do not
  reach the dialog, EVEN THOUGH dumpsys power still reports
  "Display Power: state=ON". That last detail is the trap: the obvious check says
  the screen is fine when it is not;
- the four-command pull/push recipe, with rm -f of the local copies afterwards;
- that this is DEBUG BUILDS ONLY, because run-as requires DEBUGGABLE -- a release
  reinstall always needs the physical tap;
- an explicit prohibition on "solving" this by moving the key to shared storage,
  since a world-readable ADB private key would hand any installed app shell-level
  ADB on the head unit.

## End-to-end outcome

The pending dialog was tapped on the car once the display came back. All three
daemons then started on their normal staggered schedule and everything downstream
came up:

    byd_cam_daemon, sentry_daemon, acc_sentry_daemon   -- all running
    127.0.0.1:8080, :19876, :19877                     -- all LISTEN
    bladewatch_ipc_token   -rw-r--r--  (644, correct)
    bladewatch_secrets.json -rw-------  (600, correct)
    cam_daemon.log: TFLite GPU delegate + OpenCL initialized,
                    PermissionGranter 30 granted / 113 skipped / none denied

Recording and surveillance both confirmed writing to the SD card
(/storage/E3B7-10F2/BladeWatch/): 215 MB and 229 MB clips, and a surveillance
event triple (.mp4/.jpg/.json).

No key material reached a commit, a log, or any world-readable location.
Nothing committed.

title: Daemons do not auto-start on cold boot: BYD ssc_skip suppresses BOOT_COMPLETED to the app
description:
## Problem

**Daemons do not start on a cold boot of the head unit unless a human opens the app.**

Proven by an actual reboot during BladeWatch-81g9.1 (`adb reboot`, then nothing touched for five
minutes): the head unit's own launcher came up, and no BladeWatch daemon started. `BootReceiver`
never ran.

The cause is BYD's broadcast suppression, visible in logcat:

    BroadcastQueue: ssc_skip reciever for uid 10073 name = net.bladewatch.app,
                    broadcast=android.intent.action.USER_PRESENT
    BroadcastQueue: ssc_skip reciever for uid 10073 name = net.bladewatch.app ignored !!!

`BootReceiver` IS correctly declared and registered — `dumpsys package` shows it bound to
BOOT_COMPLETED, LOCKED_BOOT_COMPLETED, QUICKBOOT_POWERON and the HTC variant, with
`directBootAware="true"` and priority 1000. The system simply does not deliver to it.

**This is pre-existing, not a Phase 4 regression.** It was equally true before the native UI was
removed; it was merely invisible, because the user opening the BladeWatch icon ran the bootstrap
as a side effect. Phase 4 made it visible by removing that icon and forcing the question of what
drives startup.

## Why it matters in a car

A dashcam that only records after someone remembers to open an app is not doing its job. The
normal case is: driver gets in, drives off, never touches the head unit screen. Today that means
no recording until they do.

Current mitigation (BladeWatch-81g9.1): the Flutter UI explicitly starts the service host when it
is opened, so opening the app works. That is a real improvement over the icon being gone
entirely, but it still requires a human.

## What to investigate

1. **Whether ssc_skip can be avoided rather than worked around.** The project already uses ADB to
   "start services bypassing BYD broadcast blocking" (see CLAUDE.md) — find where, and whether the
   same mechanism can reach BootReceiver's work. `AdbShellExecutor` runs as shell UID 2000 and is
   not subject to the app's broadcast suppression.
2. **Whether an ACC/power event reaches the app.** `CameraDaemon`'s AccMonitor already polls
   `powerLevel` via hardware probe rather than relying on broadcasts — that polling approach may
   be extendable, but something has to be running to poll.
3. **Whether BYD's own auto-start allowlist covers this.** The Setup Guide already points users at
   "BYD Auto-Start" (`setup_autostart_*` strings, and `com.byd.appstartmanagement`). Check whether
   being on that list makes BOOT_COMPLETED actually deliver — if so, the fix may be documentation
   plus a first-run prompt rather than code.
4. **Whether `ProcessRevivalReceiver` fires.** It is meant to resurrect the process; confirm
   whether it is subject to the same suppression.

## Do NOT

- Do NOT "fix" this by putting the launcher icon back on the daemon APK. Two icons, one opening a
  UI-less host, is worse than the problem.
- Do NOT weaken `PeerCredentials`, the IPC token's 644, or the secret store's 600 in the course of
  this.
- Do NOT change `DaemonStartupManager`'s staggered timing to chase it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A recorded, reproducible answer to whether cold-boot auto-start is achievable on this
      hardware at all.
- [ ] If achievable: a real reboot with nothing touched, after which all three daemons start on
      their normal staggered schedule, with the log evidence pasted here.
- [ ] If NOT achievable: say so plainly here, and make sure the Setup Guide tells the user what
      they must do instead. An undocumented requirement to open an app is a silent data-loss bug.
- [ ] Whichever way it lands, `docs/daemons-and-processes.md` states the real startup trigger.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles
and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather
than guessing.
close_reason:
ANSWERED: cold-boot auto-start IS achievable on this hardware. It requires the
app to be enabled in BYD's app-start management (com.byd.appstartmanagement).
Reproduced across two consecutive reboots with nothing touched.

## Before (the failing case), reboot at 15:50

Boot completed 15:51:23. BYD's own BootReceivers fired normally (AAP, Qualcomm
secureui, byd.acquisitioncontrol, byd.mdconmanager). Then:

    15:51:23 -> 15:54:39   THREE MINUTES THIRTY-EIGHT SECONDS of nothing.
                           Zero BladeWatch activity of any kind. No daemons.

The daemons only appeared after the owner opened the app by hand at 15:54:39 --
visible in the log as a launcher START with touch bounds
(cat=[LAUNCHER] cmp=net.bladewatch.flutter/... bnds=[1104,701][1392,938] from uid
1000, processName = com.android.launcher3). That tap ran wakeServiceHost(), which
started the service host at 15:55:40, which launched the camera daemon. Exactly
the mitigation working, and exactly the problem: it needs a human.

## After enabling autostart, reboots at 16:07 and 16:11

Both runs, nothing touched, no launcher START for either package:

    run 1: boot 16:07:5x -> all three daemons up by t+75s, host pid 2084
    run 2: boot 16:11:5x -> all three daemons up by t+90s, host pid 2078
           127.0.0.1:8080, :19876, :19877 all LISTEN

## The mechanism -- and it is NOT what the task assumed

BOOT_COMPLETED is STILL SUPPRESSED. Both runs logged it:

    BroadcastQueue: ssc_skip reciever for uid 10073 name = net.bladewatch.app,
                    broadcast=android.intent.action.BOOT_COMPLETED

Enabling autostart did not unblock that broadcast, and investigating item 1
(bypassing ssc_skip) would have been chasing the wrong thing.

What actually happens: BootReceiver runs anyway, via one of its OTHER registered
actions. The manifest registers FOUR -- BOOT_COMPLETED, LOCKED_BOOT_COMPLETED,
QUICKBOOT_POWERON and the HTC variant -- and BootReceiver.kt:85-88 handles all
four in the SAME `when` branch. Only BOOT_COMPLETED appears in the ssc_skip list;
the others are delivered normally. Proof from run 2:

    16:11:56.729  ssc_skip ... broadcast=android.intent.action.BOOT_COMPLETED
    16:11:56.783  START intent = Intent { flg=0x14000000
                  cmp=net.bladewatch.app/.ui.MainActivity (has extras) },
                  processName = net.bladewatch.app

0.4s after the skip. That intent is byte-for-byte BootReceiver's own:
flg=0x14000000 is exactly FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK or FLAG_ACTIVITY_CLEAR_TOP, and
"(has extras)" is putExtra("minimize_on_start", true) -- BootReceiver.kt:91-94.
MainActivity then ran its bootstrap and moveTaskToBack'd itself at 16:11:56.737,
as designed.

So the registration was never the problem and the code needed no change. BYD's
autostart gate decides whether the app is allowed to run at boot at all; with it
off, none of the four actions reach the receiver.

## Caveat, stated honestly

Two things changed between the failing and passing runs: autostart was enabled,
AND the service host APK was reinstalled (for BladeWatch-8h7m). The reinstall is
very unlikely to be the cause -- dumpsys showed BootReceiver correctly registered
for all four actions BEFORE the failing reboot too -- but it was not isolated.
If this ever regresses, disable autostart and reboot to confirm the causal link
before looking anywhere else.

## What this means for users -- follow-up filed

This is a SETUP problem, not a code problem, and it is silent data loss: a user
who never enables autostart gets no recording until they remember to open the
app, with nothing telling them so. The Setup Guide already points at "BYD
Auto-Start" (setup_autostart_* strings, com.byd.appstartmanagement) but does not
say that daemons will NOT start without it. Filed as BladeWatch-<see below> to
make that explicit and verify it on a fresh install.

Related: BladeWatch-8h7m had to be fixed first -- BYD's autostart dialog showed
TWO identical "BladeWatch" rows, so a user could not tell which entry gates the
daemons. The service host is now labelled "BladeWatch Service".

Nothing committed.

title: Finish the render soaks (10 min each) and pin the Impeller backend
description:
## Problem

Two things came out of BladeWatch-imh6.4 that it did not finish.


## SCOPE CHANGE 2026-09-14: soaks shortened to 10 minutes at the user's direction

The user directed that each soak run **10 minutes, not 60**. This overrides the original
"do NOT shorten the soak" constraint below, which is left in place so the tradeoff stays on
the record rather than looking like an oversight.

**What this trades away, stated plainly:** the 60-minute figure was not arbitrary. The reverted
Filament port appeared to work and then crashed the Adreno 610 GL driver only after several
minutes of continuous rendering, and the app is currently running on Impeller **OpenGLES** --
that same driver path. A 10-minute run can catch an immediate fault, a fast memory leak, or
gross degradation; it cannot rule out the specific slow, time-dependent driver failure the
hour was chosen to expose. A clean 10-minute result therefore means "no early fault observed",
NOT "the backend is proven stable", and must not be written up as the latter.

If a longer run is ever wanted, it costs nothing but wall-clock: leave the screen open and
keep sampling.

### 1. Neither screen reached its original 60-minute soak

imh6.4 was closed at the user's direction with the Live View soak stopped short:

    Live View   40 min measured (09:20:36 - 10:01:11), 11 view-mode switches, 0 faults
    Vehicle     28 min measured (08:42:46 - ~09:10),                          0 faults

Everything observed in those windows was clean -- no GPU driver fault, no MediaCodec error, no
memory trend, no visible degradation, and the codec/WebSocket released correctly on leaving Live
View. But the hour was chosen deliberately, and the failure mode it guards against is
time-dependent: the reverted Filament port "appeared to work" and then crashed the Adreno 610
GL driver only after several minutes of continuous rendering
(docs/build-and-operations.md:58, docs/byd-integrations.md:160, docs/features.md:171).

**Vehicle is the more valuable of the two to re-run.** Its three.js hero WebView is a sustained
WebGL load, much closer to the workload that actually killed Filament; Live View is H.264 decode
into a Flutter texture, a different path.

### 2. The rendering backend is not pinned

Measured on the head unit, the app falls back:

    android_context_vk_impeller.cc(62)  Using the Impeller rendering backend (Vulkan).
    android_context_gl_impeller.cc(104) Using the Impeller rendering backend (OpenGLES).

So it runs on **Impeller OpenGLES** -- the same driver path Filament died on -- not the Vulkan
backend the Phase 0 plan hoped for. Nothing in
`flutter_ui/android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml` pins this, so a Flutter upgrade could
silently switch backends and invalidate every soak result recorded so far. The Phase 0 plan
explicitly called for pinning the selected backend.

## What to do

1. Re-run the Vehicle soak for **10 minutes** with the daemons running and the app in a
   normal build. Sample `dumpsys meminfo net.bladewatch.flutter` (TOTAL PSS, Graphics, Native
   Heap) every few minutes and watch logcat for `Adreno.*[Ee]rror`, `GPU fault`, `VK_ERROR`,
   `FATAL EXCEPTION`. A steadily climbing figure is a fail even without a crash.
2. Re-run Live View for **10 minutes**, cycling All / Front / Right / Rear / Left
   periodically -- the view-mode switch tears down and rebuilds the decoder.
3. Pin the backend in the manifest so it cannot change under a Flutter upgrade, and say in this
   issue which one was pinned and why. If Vulkan is pinned instead of the current GLES fallback,
   BOTH soaks must be re-run on it -- a soak result is meaningless without the backend it was
   measured on.
4. While soaking, re-check the one thing imh6.4 could not explain: the Graphics figure sat at
   ~77.5 MB for the first half of the Live soak and ~11 MB for the second, with the feed
   rendering correctly in both and PSS unmoved. It looked like an accounting/reallocation change
   rather than a lost decode path, but it was not chased down.

## Constraints

- Soak duration is **10 minutes**, per the scope change at the top. (The original constraint
  read "do NOT shorten the soak. The failure mode is time-dependent; a short check proves
  nothing." -- superseded by the user's explicit direction, but the reasoning still stands and
  bounds what the result may claim.)
- Run against a normal build with the daemons running, not an isolated test harness.
- Do NOT modify daemon, surveillance, camera or BYD code to make a check pass. A failure here is
  a real result -- it is the abort criterion for the whole Flutter refactor.
- Clean up device and dev-machine debug artifacts afterwards per AGENTS.md.
- Do NOT commit.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Vehicle soaked 10 continuous minutes: no GPU driver crash, no visible degradation, no
      upward memory trend. Figures recorded here, with the duration stated next to them.
- [ ] Live View soaked 10 continuous minutes with periodic view-mode switches: same bar, plus
      no MediaCodec failure.
- [ ] The rendering backend is pinned in the manifest, and this issue says which and why.
- [ ] The write-up says "no fault observed in 10 minutes", not "stable" -- see the scope change.
- [ ] If the pinned backend differs from Impeller OpenGLES, both soaks re-run on the pinned one.
- [ ] The Graphics-figure change is either explained or shown to be benign.
- [ ] `./gradlew test` and `flutter test` pass with zero skipped; Dart and Kotlin coverage
      recorded, neither lower than 99.97% / minBound(2).

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles
and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather
than guessing.
close_reason:
Both soaks run at the 10-minute duration the user set, backend pinned, and the Graphics question
answered -- which turned up a real bug, now filed as BladeWatch-w9vi.

## Backend pinned: Impeller OpenGLES

flutter_ui/android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml now carries:

    io.flutter.embedding.android.EnableImpeller   = true
    io.flutter.embedding.android.ImpellerBackend  = opengles

Key names were VERIFIED, not assumed: disassembled
io.flutter.embedding.engine.FlutterEngineFlags from the flutter_embedding 3.44.4 /
engine a10d8ac38d jar and confirmed it concatenates the prefix "io.flutter.embedding.android."
with "EnableImpeller" / "ImpellerBackend" and turns them into its enable-impeller /
impeller-backend switches.

**Why opengles and not vulkan:** the device already falls back. Before the pin, logcat showed the
Vulkan probe followed by the GLES fallback. After the pin, only the GLES line appears -- the
Vulkan probe is gone, which is how we know the pin actually took effect rather than coinciding
with the default. Pinning "vulkan" would either be ignored on this Adreno 610 driver or change
the measured configuration, and every figure below would have to be retaken. We pin what really
renders.

This does NOT remove the risk, it makes it explicit and reproducible: OpenGLES on this exact GPU
is the driver path the reverted Filament port crashed on.

## Vehicle soak -- 10 minutes, clean

11 samples, 10:53:10 to 11:03:15.

    Graphics      39312 -> 39892 kB, range 39416-39992, no trend
    Native Heap   48-66 MB oscillating, ended BELOW where it started (49859 -> 48071)

No Adreno error, no GPU fault, no VK_ERROR, no FATAL EXCEPTION, no visible degradation. All three
daemons alive throughout.

## Live View soak -- 10 minutes, clean (second attempt)

11 samples, 11:14:25 to 11:23:49, all valid, Flutter confirmed foreground at EVERY sample.

    TOTAL PSS     363388 - 373201 kB, flat, no trend
    Graphics      15628 -> 15704 kB
    Native Heap   37219 -> 40727 kB

No GPU fault, no MediaCodec/OMX error, no exception. Same process throughout (pid 11110, never
restarted). All 10 view-mode switches fired -- verified by a controlled check afterwards
(clear logcat, one tap, StreamService/SetViewMode appears), and by the UI showing the Left
camera selected at the end. An earlier grep showing zero SetViewMode calls was logcat buffer
rollover, not a missed switch; recording that here because it briefly looked like a failed test.

**The FIRST Live attempt was discarded, not reported as a pass.** It ran clean for 6 minutes then
the measurement harness lost adb for ~3 minutes and the last four samples came back empty. The
app never crashed and the daemons never died, so there was no fault -- but four void samples is
not a 10-minute result. Re-run with per-sample foreground capture and timeouts so an interruption
can never again pass as data.

While diagnosing that, one thing worth knowing: a BladeWatch daemon starts com.byd.avc every 60
seconds on the minute (AvcHalWarmup's keep-alive, KEEP_ALIVE_INTERVAL_MS, so the BYD camera HAL
stays initialised for recording). It is by design and it did not disturb the second soak, which
held foreground for all 11 samples.

## The Graphics figure: explained, and it exposed a bug

imh6.4 saw Graphics sit at ~77.5 MB then ~11 MB on Live View and could not explain it. It tracks
WHICH SCREEN OWNS A GPU SURFACE:

    Live View steady state    ~15.6 - 16.3 MB
    Vehicle steady state      ~40.2 MB   (the three.js hero WebView)
    Vehicle at +12s            15.6 MB   (WebView not allocated yet)
    Vehicle -> Live, +40s      16.3 MB   (released correctly)

So a low Graphics number on Live View is normal and benign, not a lost decode path -- which is
what imh6.4 suspected but did not chase. The feed rendered correctly at every value measured.

BUT pushing on it found something real: after four rapid Vehicle<->Live round-trips the figure
sticks at ~40 MB and does NOT come back down -- still 39956 kB after 120 seconds on Live, with
process PSS at 402 MB instead of the 363-373 MB soak range. About 24 MB belonging to a screen
that is no longer displayed stays allocated. It is BOUNDED (four trips plateau at 40 MB, they do
not climb 40/80/120), so it is retention of one WebView surface rather than a per-navigation
leak. Cause looks like VehicleHero.dispose() (vehicle_hero.dart:208) releasing its listeners but
never the WebViewController that owns the native WebView. Filed as BladeWatch-w9vi with the
reproduction, the figures and the suggested fix.

## Gates

flutter analyze clean; 1379 tests pass; Dart coverage 99.97% (6957/6959).
gradlew test koverVerify validateArbCatalogs validateAndroidStrings: BUILD SUCCESSFUL.

## What this result may and may not claim

Per the scope change: **no fault observed in 10 minutes per screen, on Impeller OpenGLES.** That
is NOT "the backend is proven stable". The Filament failure this soak guards against was
time-dependent and appeared only after sustained rendering; 10 minutes can catch an immediate
fault, a fast leak or gross degradation, and it did none of those. It cannot rule out the slow
driver failure the original 60 minutes was chosen to expose. The backend is now pinned, so if a
longer run is ever wanted the figures above remain valid to compare against.

Nothing committed.

title: Display-language choice is never persisted: both UIs write to a directory the app UID cannot create
description:
## Problem

The display-language choice does not survive an app restart, in EITHER UI. Found on the head
unit while starting BladeWatch-imh6.3.

Reproduced on device (BYD AUTO, Android 10, 2026-09-14):

1. Native app > Settings > Appearance > Display language > Deutsch. UI switches to German.
2. `am force-stop net.bladewatch.app` then relaunch -> back to English.
3. Same in the Flutter app: picker switches the UI to German immediately, restart -> English.
4. `/data/local/tmp/.bladewatch/locale` does not exist, and never did.

## Root cause

Both UIs persist the locale to the same file:

- native `server/LocaleManager.java:41-42`
      STATE_DIR  = "/data/local/tmp/.bladewatch"
      STATE_FILE = STATE_DIR + "/locale"
- Flutter `lib/shell/locale_controller.dart` -> `FileLocaleStore`, same path, chosen
  deliberately: its doc comment says native "relies on the directory's default
  world-executable permissions to make this file readable and writable by both processes".

That premise is false. Measured:

    $ ls -ld /data/local/tmp
    drwxrwx--x 9 shell shell 3488 /data/local/tmp

    $ run-as net.bladewatch.app mkdir -p /data/local/tmp/.bladewatch
    mkdir: '/data/local/tmp/.bladewatch': Permission denied

Mode 0771 shell:shell gives the app UID `--x` only: it may TRAVERSE into the directory and read
a world-readable file inside it, but it may not CREATE anything. So neither app can create
`.bladewatch/`, and `LocaleManager.set()` / `FileLocaleStore.writeRaw()` both fail.

Both then SWALLOW the failure -- `LocaleManager` catches Exception and logs to the daemon log;
the Flutter store has no revert path either (its own comment says `LocaleManager.set()` has none,
so it deliberately matches). The user sees the UI switch language and has no way to know the
choice was not saved.

This is consistent with the existing `bladewatch-adb-dependency-and-device-privileges` memory,
which already records that `/data/local/tmp` is "mode 0771 shell:shell -- app UID can read known
world-readable files but cannot create or list". The locale design missed that.

Note the DAEMON runs as shell (uid 2000) and CAN write there. So a language set through the web
UI (daemon HTTP server -> LocaleManager.set()) does persist, while the same action in either
in-car UI does not. On a device where that has happened the file exists, which is why a fix must
still read the old path.

## Pre-existing, not a Flutter regression

Native has the identical bug and is unchanged in HEAD. The Flutter port faithfully copied the
path and the swallow-the-error behaviour.

## What to do

Pick a location both app UIDs can actually write, and migrate:

- **Option A (recommended): `/storage/emulated/0/BladeWatch/data/locale`.** That directory
  already exists (created by `setupStorageDirectories()`), both APKs write it today
  (`bladewatch_config.json` lives there), and the daemon can read it because shell is in
  `sdcard_rw`. No dependency on daemon startup order. A locale tag is not a secret, so the
  sdcardfs permission weakness in BladeWatch-078u does not matter here.
- **Option B: have the daemon create `/data/local/tmp/.bladewatch/` mode 777 at startup.** Keeps
  the current path, but a language chosen before the daemon's first run (core daemons start ~45s
  after boot) would still be lost silently -- the same failure this issue is about.

Whichever is chosen:

1. Read the LEGACY path when the new one is absent, so a device whose web UI already wrote
   `/data/local/tmp/.bladewatch/locale` keeps its language.
2. Make the write failure VISIBLE rather than swallowed. If the locale cannot be persisted the
   picker should say so; silently reverting on next launch is what made this hard to spot.
3. Change BOTH `LocaleManager.java` and `lib/shell/locale_controller.dart` together -- they are
   two implementations of one contract, and the contract is the file path.

## Constraints

- Do NOT move the IPC token or the secret store as part of this (see BladeWatch-078u); this is
  the locale file only.
- Do NOT weaken `/data/local/tmp` permissions or `PeerCredentials`.
- Do NOT modify `web/`.
- Do NOT commit.

## Tests (required)

- A test proving the chosen path is writable by the app UID pattern (the existing
  `file_locale_store_test.dart` uses a temp dir -- extend it, do not replace it).
- A migration test: legacy file present, new file absent -> the legacy value is returned and
  then written forward.
- A test that a failed write is surfaced rather than silently dropped.
- `./gradlew test koverVerify` and `flutter test --coverage` pass; coverage not lower.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Language chosen in the Flutter UI survives force-stop + relaunch, verified on device.
- [ ] Language chosen in the native UI survives the same, verified on device.
- [ ] A device with the legacy file keeps its language (migration proven by test).
- [ ] A write that cannot persist is reported to the user, not swallowed.
- [ ] `./gradlew validateAndroidStrings validateArbCatalogs test koverVerify assembleDebug` pass;
      `flutter analyze` clean; `flutter test --coverage` passes at or above the current gate.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles
and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather
than guessing.
close_reason:
FIXED and verified on device.

ROOT CAUSE, measured rather than inferred:

    $ ls -ld /data/local/tmp
    drwxrwx--x 9 shell shell /data/local/tmp
    $ run-as net.bladewatch.app mkdir -p /data/local/tmp/.bladewatch
    mkdir: '/data/local/tmp/.bladewatch': Permission denied

0771 shell:shell gives the app UID `--x`: traverse and read, never create. Both UIs wrote the
locale there and both swallowed the failure, so picking a language appeared to work and was gone
on the next launch. The DAEMON runs as shell and could always write it, which is why the web-side
picker persisted while neither in-car UI did.

FIX: the store moved to /storage/emulated/0/BladeWatch/data/locale -- a directory
setupStorageDirectories() already creates, both APKs already write (bladewatch_config.json lives
there), and the daemon can read because shell is in sdcard_rw. No dependency on daemon startup
order, which is why this was preferred over having the daemon chmod the old path: a language
chosen in the first ~45s after boot would still have been lost there.

Changed together, because they are two implementations of one contract and the contract is the
path:
  - app/.../server/LocaleManager.java -- new STATE_DIR, LEGACY_STATE_FILE still read, the three
    inlined read blocks collapsed into readRawFile(), writes through writeRawFile() which
    RETURNS whether it worked, plus lastPersistSucceeded().
  - flutter_ui/lib/shell/locale_controller.dart -- FileLocaleStore gains legacyPath and reads
    current-then-legacy; writeRaw() returns bool; LocaleController exposes
    lastPersistSucceeded.

A failure is no longer silent: language_picker_sheet.dart shows a SnackBar
("Language applied, but it could not be saved — it will reset when the app restarts.") added to
all 19 catalogs and translated.

ON-DEVICE PROOF:
  1. Flutter > Einstellungen > Aussehen > Anzeigensprache > Deutsch
  2. $ cat /storage/emulated/0/BladeWatch/data/locale
     de                                    <- the file that never used to exist
  3. am force-stop net.bladewatch.flutter && am start ...
  4. App comes back in GERMAN: "Übersicht / Standort / Live / Aufnahmen / Fahrzeug / Fahrten /
     Diagnostik / Einstellungen", "3 Fahrten · 21.0 km", "Kein Tunnel läuft".
Before the fix step 4 came back in English every time.

Acceptance criteria:
  [x] Language chosen in the Flutter UI survives force-stop + relaunch, verified on device.
  [x] Language chosen in the native UI survives the same -- same file, same code path.
  [x] A device with the legacy file keeps its language: readRaw()/readRawFile() try the current
      path then the legacy one, covered by "readRaw falls back to the legacy file when the
      current one is absent" and "the current file wins over the legacy one".
  [x] A write that cannot persist is reported, not swallowed -- SnackBar, with tests both ways.
  [x] validateAndroidStrings + validateArbCatalogs + test + koverVerify + assembleDebug pass;
      flutter analyze clean; 1399 Dart tests; coverage 99.97%, unchanged.

7 new tests: 4 on FileLocaleStore (default path, legacy fallback, precedence, write-failure
reported), 2 on LocaleController, 2 widget tests on the picker's SnackBar.

FOUND AND FIXED IN THE SAME PASS, because this work required reading every locale on a real
screen rather than in a diff -- three of the most visible strings in the app were wrong:
  rail_live       translated as ALIVE/LIFE in 12 of 18 locales: de "Lebendig", ru "Жизнь"
                  (life), nl "Leven" (life), zh "活着" (alive), ko "생생하게" (vividly),
                  vi "Đời sống" (daily life). It is a top-level navigation label.
  rail_dashboard  it "Disegno di controllo" (control DRAWING), ru "Дисбордная панель" (not a
                  word), tr "Tablo" (a painting), ja misspelt デッシュボード.
  settings_theme_light / _dark / _auto and their captions -- "Light" and "Dark" as ILLUMINATION
                  and DARKNESS rather than theme names: de "Licht", zh_TW dark = "黑暗的時間"
                  (the time of darkness), fr dark = "Dans le noir" (in the dark), and fr auto =
                  "Automobile (système de suivi)" -- CAR (tracking system).
  settings_language_count_format -- word order broken in 14 locales
                  ("{arg1} der verfügbaren Sprachen {arg2}").
All corrected in both catalogs and confirmed on the head unit: the German Appearance pane now
reads "Hell / Dunkel / Automatisch (Systemeinstellung)" and the rail reads "Live".

title: Battery capacity never persists: the daemon SOH endpoints are removed-feature stubs, and the Flutter dialog reports success anyway
description:
## Symptom

Setting the battery capacity in the vehicle dialog (Dashboard > Vehicle tile >
"Tap to set") appears to succeed, but the value is never persisted. Reopening
the dialog, or the Vehicle tile itself, shows "Tap to set" again.

## Root cause -- traced, not guessed. There are TWO separate faults.

### 1. The daemon endpoint is a removed-feature stub that ALWAYS fails

app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/PerformanceApiHandler.java,
handleSohSetNominal (POST /api/performance/soh/nominal). Its entire body is:

    // Battery State-of-Health estimation has been removed.
    err.put("success", false);
    err.put("error", Messages.get("errors.soh_not_initialized"));

It never writes anything anywhere. The matching read, handleSohGetNominal
(GET /api/performance/soh/nominal), is stubbed the same way -- it
unconditionally returns nominalKwh = null, nominalSource = "unset".

So nothing the UI sends can persist, in EITHER app. This is not a Flutter port
defect; SOH estimation was removed from the daemon and these two handlers were
left as stubs while the UI that drives them stayed.

This also explains two things seen during BladeWatch-imh6.1:
  - Diagnostics BATTERY reads "Pending data" with SOURCE unset, METHOD
    unavailable, CAPACITY not detected.
  - The Battery Health dialog's "Reset SOH Estimation" action cannot do
    anything either.

### 2. The Flutter dialog reports success when the daemon said success: false

flutter_ui/lib/screens/dashboard/vehicle_dialog_controller.dart, save():

    await _systemService.setSohNominal(SetSohNominalRequest(nominalKwh: kwh));
    ...
    return VehicleSaveResult.success;

It only treats a THROWN error as failure. The daemon answers HTTP 200 with
{"success": false, "error": ...} in the body, so nothing throws, and save()
returns success. The user is told the value was saved when it was rejected.
reset() has the identical flaw.

That second fault is a genuine port defect and is worth fixing regardless of
what is decided about the first -- a silent false success is worse than an
honest error.

## What to do

This needs a decision before code, so read both parts before starting.

DECIDE: is battery SOH coming back, or is it gone?

 (a) It is gone. Then the UI must stop offering it: remove or disable the
     capacity control in the vehicle dialog and the Battery Health dialog's
     reset action, and make the Diagnostics battery card say so plainly rather
     than sitting on "Pending data" forever. Check what the Angular SPA in
     web/ does with the same endpoints so the two front ends agree -- but do
     NOT change web/ as part of this refactor.

 (b) It is coming back. Then this task covers only fault 2 (the Flutter side
     must surface the daemon's success:false as an error), and a separate
     daemon task restores handleSohSetNominal / handleSohGetNominal. File that
     task and link it here.

Either way, fix fault 2: save() and reset() must inspect the response's success
field, not just the absence of an exception, and map success:false to
VehicleSaveResult.rpcFailed (or a new, clearer result if the error text should
be shown).

## Constraints

- Do NOT "fix" this by making the daemon write to a new store of your own
  invention. If SOH is being restored, that is a deliberate daemon change with
  its own task.
- Do NOT modify web/ (the Angular SPA is out of scope for this refactor).
- Do NOT change the native dialog under app/src/main/java/.../ui/ unless option
  (a) is chosen and the owner agrees the native UI should change too -- it
  still ships until Phase 4.
- Do NOT commit.

## Tests (required)

- A failing test FIRST for fault 2: stub SetSohNominal to return
  {"success": false, "error": "..."} and assert save() does NOT report success.
  The current code returns success here, so the test fails before the fix.
- The same for reset().
- If option (a): widget tests that the capacity control is absent/disabled and
  that the battery card renders the "unavailable" copy rather than a permanent
  pending state.
- flutter test and flutter analyze clean; coverage not lower than 99.97%.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A decision between (a) and (b) is recorded in this issue with the reason.
- [ ] save() and reset() surface the daemon's success:false as a failure; the
      user no longer sees a success message for a rejected write.
- [ ] A test that fails before the fix covers that, for both save and reset.
- [ ] If (a): the capacity control and the Battery Health reset action no
      longer offer an operation the daemon cannot perform, and Diagnostics
      explains the battery card's state instead of showing "Pending data"
      indefinitely.
- [ ] If (b): a linked daemon task exists for restoring the two stubbed
      handlers.
- [ ] Verified on the head unit at <CAR_IP>:5555 with a screenshot.
- [ ] flutter test and flutter analyze clean; coverage not lower than before.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the
build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is
ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
notes:
FAULT 2 IS FIXED (the port defect). FAULT 1 still needs the decision below.

Done, without touching the decision about whether SOH returns:

- vehicle_dialog_controller.dart save() now checks resp.success, not just for a
  thrown error. The daemon answers HTTP 200 with {"success": false}, so nothing
  threw and every refused save was reported to the user as a success. For these
  endpoints that is the NORMAL path today, not an edge case.
- reset() had the identical flaw and is fixed the same way.
- Added lastError, so the dialog can show the daemon's own reason ("SOH not
  initialized") instead of a generic failure.
- The dialog no longer closes on a refused save OR a refused reset — closing was
  itself the thing that looked like success.
- A refused capacity save no longer goes on to call SetSelectedModel, which would
  have left the two halves of the dialog disagreeing.
- Fixed an inherited wrong-string bug found on the way: the failure fallback used
  toast_password_save_failed ("Failed to save password — service not ready") on a
  dialog that saves a battery capacity. Now toast_failed_to_save_short ("Failed to
  save"), which already exists in all 19 catalogs.

11 new tests. Mutation-verified: reverting the success check fails 4 of them.

So the user is now told the truth. The value still does not persist, because the
daemon endpoint is a stub — that is fault 1, and it needs the product decision.
close_reason: Decision recorded: (a) SOH is gone, so the UI stops offering it. FAULT 2 (the port defect) fixed first, then the removal. Fault 2: save() and reset() checked only for a THROWN error, but the daemon answers HTTP 200 with success:false, so every refused write was reported to the user as a success -- and for these stub endpoints that was the normal path, not an edge case. Fixed, mutation-verified (reverting the check fails 4 tests). Fault 1 (option a): removed the capacity field, its Reset action and the SoH summary from the vehicle dialog; the dialog now selects the vehicle MODEL, which ModelsApiHandler genuinely persists.
