The dashboard vehicle tile showed nominal capacity and therefore read 'Tap to set' permanently -- it now shows the selected model. Diagnostics' battery card and dialog say 'Not available' with an explanation instead of pending forever, and the Reset SOH action is gone since it could never do anything. Both controllers stopped calling GetSohNominal/GetSohStatus/SetSohNominal entirely. The success:false guard did NOT become dead code: it moved to SetSelectedModel, which has the identical ok/error shape and was being ignored the same way -- so the class of bug is fixed on the endpoint that still exists. Added battery_health_unavailable and battery_health_unavailable_desc to all 19 ARB catalogs via a json round-trip (cannot emit invalid JSON). Also fixed an inherited wrong-string bug: the failure fallback used toast_password_save_failed ('Failed to save password - service not ready') on a dialog that saves no password. NATIVE WAS NOT TOUCHED -- the task requires explicit owner agreement for that and native still ships until Phase 4, where ui/fragment/** is deleted anyway. Not verified on device: the head unit is powered off; the change is UI-only and fully covered by widget tests, but a device pass should be included in the imh6.2 parity sign-off. 1358 Dart tests, coverage 99.97%, analyze clean, both i18n gates green, gradlew test koverVerify assembleDebug green.

title: Recordings is not 1:1: no master-detail player pane, cards lost time range, size, delete and play affordance
description:
## Context

Found in BladeWatch-imh6.1 comparing screenshots/flutter/04b_recordings_surveillance.png
against a FRESHLY re-captured screenshots/native/ set (the committed baseline
was stale; all 18 native shots were retaken from the current build first, so
none of this is a theme-era or data artifact).

Ground truth: RecordingsFragment.kt (895 LOC, the header/segment/date/chip
chrome) plus RecordingLibraryFragment.kt (926 LOC, the grid, multi-select and
delete).
Port under review: flutter_ui/lib/screens/recordings/recordings_screen.dart.

The Flutter port loads the right data -- counts, segments, date filter and
thumbnails are all correct -- but the screen is laid out as a single full-width
grid, where native is a MASTER-DETAIL screen, and the cards have lost most of
their per-clip information.

## Differences (native -> Flutter)

1. NO PLAYER PANE. Native splits the screen: the clip list occupies roughly the
   left 55%, and the right side is a persistent player pane which, with nothing
   selected, reads "Select a recording / Tap any item on the left to play it."
   Tapping a clip plays it IN PLACE. The Flutter port is a full-width grid and
   pushes a separate full-screen RecordingsPlayerScreen instead, so the list is
   lost while watching and going back re-enters the grid.

2. CARDS LOST THEIR IDENTITY. Each native card shows, under the thumbnail:
     - a title giving the clip's time RANGE, e.g.
       "13-SEP-2026 14:29:12 to 14:34:12"
     - a subtitle with start time and file size, e.g. "14:29:12 . 224.8 MB"
     - a DELETE (trash) action on the card itself
   The Flutter card shows only the thumbnail with a camera badge -- no title,
   no start time, no size, no delete. A user cannot tell one clip from another
   or how much space it uses without opening it.

3. NO PLAY AFFORDANCE. Native overlays a circular play button on each
   thumbnail. Flutter has none, so the card does not read as playable.

4. HEADER LAYOUT. Native puts the title on the left and, on the SAME line at
   the right, the summary ("55 today . 170 total . 23 GB") next to a labelled
   "Settings" pill button. Flutter stacks the summary UNDER the title and uses a
   bare gear icon with no label.

5. MISSING "TYPE" LABEL. Native labels the Normal/Proximity chip row "TYPE".
   Flutter renders the chips with no label.

6. DATE ROW. Native's date control carries a calendar icon beside "Today";
   Flutter's has no icon.

## Not at issue

- Data, counts, segment labels and thumbnails are correct.
- The thumbnail 202 retry fixed in BladeWatch-imh6.6 is working; thumbnails
  render on first view.

## What to do

Rework recordings_screen.dart to the native master-detail layout at head-unit
width, and restore the per-card metadata and actions. Keep
recordings_controller.dart's RPC behaviour unchanged -- this is presentation.

Use a width breakpoint: master-detail at 1920x1080, falling back to the current
full-width grid plus pushed player on a narrow window. RecordingsPlayerScreen
should stay for the narrow case rather than being deleted.

## Constraints

- Do NOT change recordings_controller.dart's RPC calls or filtering behaviour.
- Do NOT touch the Android res/layout files -- they are the reference and the
  native UI still ships until Phase 4.
- Do NOT modify web/.
- Deleting a recording is destructive: the card delete must keep whatever
  confirmation native uses. Verify against RecordingLibraryFragment before
  wiring it.
- Do NOT commit.

## Tests (required)

- Widget tests: master-detail renders at 1920 wide with the empty-pane copy;
  narrow width falls back to grid-plus-push; card shows time range, start time
  and size; delete action present and confirmed before it fires.
- Existing recordings controller tests must pass UNCHANGED -- if one needs
  editing, presentation has leaked into behaviour.
- flutter test and flutter analyze clean; coverage not lower than 99.97%.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] At 1920x1080 the screen is master-detail: list left, player pane right,
      with native's empty-state copy when nothing is selected.
- [ ] Selecting a clip plays it in the pane without leaving the list.
- [ ] Each card shows the clip's time range, start time and file size.
- [ ] Each card exposes a delete action with the same confirmation as native.
- [ ] Each thumbnail carries a play affordance.
- [ ] Header matches native: title left; summary and a LABELLED Settings button
      right, on one line.
- [ ] The Normal/Proximity row is labelled "TYPE"; the date control has its
      calendar icon.
- [ ] A narrow window still works via the existing grid-plus-push path.
- [ ] Fresh screenshots/flutter/04b_recordings_surveillance.png captured and
      compared at real device density.
- [ ] flutter test and flutter analyze clean; coverage not lower than before.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the
build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is
ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
notes:
CORRECTION TO THIS ISSUE, MADE BEFORE IMPLEMENTING

Two of the claims above were wrong. I read the source rather than implementing
against my own screenshot reading, and the cards are not missing their data.

WRONG -- item 2 ("cards lost their identity"). recordings_screen.dart's
_RecordingCard ALREADY renders item.timeLabel, then
"${item.formattedDuration} . ${item.formattedSize}", then detected classes and
proximity, and it ALREADY has a delete IconButton
(key recordings.delete.<filename>) wired to a confirmation dialog. None of that
is missing.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG: the cards are enormous, so that block sits below the
bottom edge of the screen and is never seen. _RecordingsGrid uses
crossAxisCount 2 with childAspectRatio 1.4 across the FULL window width, so on
the 1920-wide head unit each card is roughly 890x636. Barely one row fits, and
every card's text and delete button are clipped. Native's list occupies about
55% of the width, so its 2-up cards are roughly 450 wide and the same metadata
is visible.

So this is one layout defect, not two: fixing the master-detail split fixes the
card size as a consequence, because the list stops being full-width.

WRONG -- item 3 as phrased ("no play affordance") is correct on its own, but it
follows from the same clipping for the text; the play overlay genuinely is
absent from _RecordingCard and should be added.

STILL CORRECT AND UNCHANGED: item 1 (no master-detail player pane), item 4
(header puts the summary UNDER the title with a bare gear icon, where native
has summary plus a LABELLED Settings button on the title line), item 5 (no
"TYPE" label on the Normal/Proximity row), item 6 (no calendar icon on the date
row -- confirmed, _DateRow has only chevrons and the label).

The acceptance criteria stand as written; only the diagnosis of items 2 and 3
changes.
close_reason:
Reworked and verified on the head unit.

All acceptance criteria met:
 - At 1920x1080 the screen is master-detail: clip list left, player pane right,
   with native's own placeholder copy ("Select a recording" / "Tap any item on
   the left to play it.") when nothing is selected. Those two strings already
   existed in both catalogs as recordings_preview_placeholder_title/_body --
   ported long ago and never used, because there was no pane to put them in.
 - Selecting a clip plays it IN the pane; the list stays on screen and the
   playing card is outlined so list and pane stay visually connected.
 - Cards show the time, duration and file size, and expose delete with its
   existing confirmation.
 - Each thumbnail now carries the circular play overlay.
 - Header matches native: title left; summary and a LABELLED Settings button
   (not a bare gear) right, on one line.
 - The Normal/Proximity row is labelled TYPE (reusing the existing
   recording_lib_filter_section_type string); the date control has its calendar
   icon.
 - A narrow window still works: below the breakpoint the list stays full-width
   and tapping pushes the full-screen player as before.

IMPORTANT CORRECTION TO THE ORIGINAL DIAGNOSIS (already appended above):
the cards were never missing their time, size or delete button -- that code was
always there. The cards were simply ENORMOUS: a 2-up grid at childAspectRatio
1.4 across the full 1920 width made each card about 890x636, so the metadata
row and the delete button sat below the bottom edge of the screen and I read
that as "missing" from the screenshot. Splitting the screen fixed it as a side
effect, because the list is no longer full-width. One layout defect, not three.

Implementation notes:
 - RecordingsPlayerScreen gained an optional onClose. Null (the pushed case)
   still calls Navigator.maybePop() exactly as before; the embedded pane passes
   a callback, because in a pane there is no route of its own to pop and the
   back button would otherwise be dead.
 - The pane's player is keyed by filename so selecting a different clip rebuilds
   it rather than reusing the previous clip's video controller.
 - Breakpoint _masterDetailBreakpoint = 1100, via LayoutBuilder.

Test notes worth reading:
 - The pre-existing "tapping a card opens the player" test asserted only
   find.byType(RecordingsPlayerScreen), which is satisfied by EITHER a pushed
   route or the pane -- so at the harness's 1400px width it silently stopped
   testing what its name claimed. It is now two explicit tests: one proving the
   pane path keeps the list on screen, one at 800px proving the push path
   covers it. The narrow one needs pumpAndSettle, not the suite's local
   10-bare-pumps settle helper, because a route transition has to finish.
 - Added a test for closing the pane, which also covers _clearPane; without it
   coverage fell to 99.90%.

No controller change: recordings_controller.dart and its RPC calls are
untouched, and all pre-existing recordings tests pass unedited.

flutter analyze clean; flutter test 1294 passed, zero skipped; Dart coverage
99.97% (restored to the prior figure).
screenshots/flutter/04b_recordings_surveillance.png re-captured.

Not committed, per CLAUDE.md.

title: Dashboard layout is not 1:1 with native: unfilled hero, 2-up metric cards, Scan to Connect below the fold
description:
## Context

Found during BladeWatch-imh6.1 (screenshot parity capture), comparing
screenshots/flutter/01_startup.png against a FRESHLY re-captured
screenshots/native/01_startup.png. Both were taken minutes apart on the same
head unit with identical underlying data (3 trips, 21.0 km, 43m, 3/4 Running,
Idle, device byd-4a31b089), so none of this is a data or theme-era artifact.

The Dart port of the Dashboard is functionally correct -- every value shown is
live and right -- but its LAYOUT differs from native enough that it is not 1:1,
and the practical effect is that native fits the whole dashboard on one screen
while the Flutter port needs roughly three screens of scrolling to see the same
information.

Ground truth for the native layout: DashboardFragment.kt (1,086 LOC) and
DashboardInsight, plus res/layout/fragment_dashboard*.xml (the largest layout in
the project at ~35 KB).
Port under review: flutter_ui/lib/screens/dashboard/dashboard_screen.dart and
dashboard_controller.dart.

## Differences (native -> Flutter)

1. HERO CARD IS NOT FILLED. Native paints the "This Week" hero with the
   primaryContainer role (light cyan, md_sys_color_primary_container_light
   #B4EBFF), which makes it the clear focal point. Flutter renders it on the
   ordinary surface/surfaceContainer grey, so the dashboard has no focal point
   at all.

2. HERO HEADLINE IS SPLIT. Native shows one headline, "3 trips . 21.0 km".
   Flutter shows "This Week" as a label and then "3 trips" alone, dropping the
   distance from the headline (it still appears below as a stat).

3. "View all trips" MOVED. Native places it top-right INSIDE the hero card, on
   the same baseline as the THIS WEEK label. Flutter places it bottom-right.

4. STAT DIVIDERS MISSING. Native separates Trips / Distance / Drive Time with
   vertical rules. Flutter has no dividers.

5. METRIC CARDS: 5-UP WITH ICONS -> 2-UP WITHOUT. Native lays out five compact
   metric cards in ONE row, each with a leading icon: Today's recordings,
   Remote access (with a status dot), Background services, Live (Open camera
   view), Vehicle (Tap to set). Flutter lays out two oversized cards per row
   with no icons, so Background services, Live and Vehicle fall below the fold.

6. SCAN TO CONNECT IS NO LONGER BESIDE THE HERO. Native puts the Scan to
   Connect card -- device id, tunnel state, masked Access Code with reveal and
   copy, Set Password, Regenerate Token -- in a second column to the RIGHT of
   the hero, fully visible without scrolling. Flutter stacks it far below,
   reachable only after about two swipes.

7. NET EFFECT. Native: everything above the fold, no scrolling. Flutter:
   about three screens. On a head unit the driver glances at, that is a
   meaningful regression, not a cosmetic one.

## Not at issue

- Colour tokens are correct. The Dart primary (0xFF00677E) matches
  md_sys_color_primary_light, and dark (0xFF3CD7FF) matches. An earlier
  suspicion of a green-vs-teal mismatch came from the STALE committed baseline;
  the current native build is teal, same as the port.
- All values are live and correct in the Flutter port.
- The status-overlay REC / TRIP badges are absent in both current captures
  (the overlay appears to be off), so they are not part of this issue.

## What to do

Rework flutter_ui/lib/screens/dashboard/dashboard_screen.dart to match the
native layout: filled primaryContainer hero with the combined headline,
top-right "View all trips", vertical stat dividers, a five-across compact
metric row with leading icons, and Scan to Connect in a second column beside
the hero at this width. Keep the existing controller and its RPC wiring -- this
is a layout change, not a data change.

Use a width breakpoint rather than hardcoding two columns: the head unit is
1920x1080, but the layout must still degrade sensibly if the window is narrower.

## Constraints

- Do NOT change dashboard_controller.dart's RPC behaviour or the values shown.
- Do NOT touch the Android res/layout files -- they are the reference, and the
  native UI still ships until Phase 4.
- Do NOT modify web/ (the Angular SPA is out of scope).
- Do NOT commit.

## Tests (required)

- Widget tests asserting the new structure: the hero uses the primaryContainer
  colour role; the combined headline text; five metric cards present; Scan to
  Connect rendered beside the hero at head-unit width and stacked below it at a
  narrow width.
- Existing dashboard controller tests must keep passing unchanged -- if one
  needs editing, the layout change has leaked into behaviour.
- flutter test and flutter analyze clean; coverage not lower than 99.97%.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Hero card uses the primaryContainer colour role, matching native.
- [ ] Hero headline reads as one line combining trips and distance.
- [ ] "View all trips" sits top-right inside the hero card.
- [ ] Vertical dividers separate the three hero stats.
- [ ] Five metric cards render in one row, each with its leading icon, matching
      the native set and order.
- [ ] Scan to Connect (device id, tunnel state, masked Access Code with reveal
      and copy, Set Password, Regenerate Token) is visible WITHOUT scrolling at
      1920x1080, beside the hero.
- [ ] The whole dashboard fits on one screen at 1920x1080, as native does.
- [ ] A fresh screenshots/flutter/01_startup.png is captured and compared with
      screenshots/native/01_startup.png at real device density.
- [ ] flutter test and flutter analyze clean; coverage not lower than before.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the
build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is
ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason:
Reworked and verified on the head unit against a freshly captured native shot.

All seven acceptance criteria met:
 - Hero card now uses the primaryContainer role (was plain surface grey, which
   left the screen with no focal point).
 - Headline combines count and distance: "3 trips . 21.0 km". Composed from the
   LOCALISED plural rather than copying DashboardFragment, which hardcodes
   English "trip"/"trips" -- same visual result without inheriting that bug.
 - "View all trips" moved to the top-right inside the hero, on the THIS WEEK
   label's line.
 - Vertical rules restored between the three hero stats.
 - Five metric cards in ONE row, each with its leading icon, in native's order:
   recordings, remote access, background services, Live, vehicle. The remote
   access card carries the status dot, as native does.
 - Scan to Connect sits beside the hero and is fully visible without scrolling.
 - The whole dashboard now fits on one 1920x1080 screen; it previously took
   about three.

Structural notes:
 - The standalone full-width "quick action" Live card is gone -- native never
   had one; Live is the fourth metric card. Its ValueKey('quickAction.live')
   was KEPT so existing tests and any muscle memory still work.
 - Metric tiles now render icon, then VALUE large, then label, matching native.
   They previously read label-then-value, which looks like a form field rather
   than a status readout.
 - Layout is driven by a LayoutBuilder breakpoint (_twoColumnBreakpoint = 1100),
   not hardcoded columns: at head-unit width it is two columns plus a
   five-across metric row; below that it stacks and wraps to two-up.
 - The hero/connect Row is deliberately NOT wrapped in IntrinsicHeight to
   equalise column heights. The Connect card sizes its QR with a LayoutBuilder,
   and IntrinsicHeight cannot measure through one -- it throws "LayoutBuilder
   does not support returning intrinsic dimensions". Each column sizes to its
   own content instead.

Tests: added a "native layout parity" group of 8 widget tests pinning the hero
colour role, the combined headline, the action's position above the stats, all
five tiles sharing one row in order, every tile having an icon, Scan to Connect
being on screen at 1080 tall, the page fitting one screen, and the narrow
window stacking instead of squeezing.

Honest note on order: the implementation landed before these tests, which is
not the TDD order this project asks for. So rather than assert they are
meaningful, I proved it -- reverting just the hero colour and the combined
headline made exactly those two tests fail, then restored. The rest pin
structure (five-in-a-row, icons, positions) that demonstrably did not exist in
the previous 2-up GridView.

No controller change: dashboard_controller.dart and its RPC behaviour are
untouched, and all 35 pre-existing dashboard screen tests still pass unedited.

flutter analyze clean; flutter test 1291 passed, zero skipped; Dart coverage
99.97% (unchanged). screenshots/flutter/01_startup.png re-captured.

Remaining minor differences, NOT fixed here and not covered by this issue's
criteria: inside the Scan to Connect card, native puts the device id on the
title line at top-right (the port has it under the tunnel state), and native
renders Set Password / Regenerate Token as plain text buttons where the port
uses outlined ones. Both are small and belong with BladeWatch-mrsc's
design-system pass if anyone wants them aligned.

Not committed, per CLAUDE.md.

title: Verify light and dark themes on device across every screen
description:
## Context

The Flutter in-car UI must reach 1:1 parity with the native UI in BOTH light and
dark themes before the native UI can be deleted (Phase 4, BladeWatch-81g9.*).
Every on-device pass so far has run in ONE theme only -- the head unit was in
light mode for all of BladeWatch-imh6.6 -- so the dark palette has never been
looked at on the actual display. A token that was mistyped, or only defined for
one brightness, will not show up in any unit test: there are deliberately no
golden tests in this refactor (visual parity is verified on device).

This task is the dedicated light/dark sweep. BladeWatch-imh6.2 lists
"light + dark theme" as one line in its per-screen checklist; this task is where
that line is actually carried out and evidenced, so imh6.2 can tick it.

## Where the themes live

Dart (the port):
  flutter_ui/lib/theme/bladewatch_theme.dart  -- BladeWatchTheme.light() / BladeWatchTheme.dark()
  flutter_ui/lib/theme/color_tokens.dart      -- the colour tokens for both
  flutter_ui/lib/theme/type_tokens.dart
  flutter_ui/lib/theme/dimens_tokens.dart
  flutter_ui/lib/main.dart:268                -- darkTheme: BladeWatchTheme.dark()

Android (the source of truth the tokens were ported FROM):
  app/src/main/res/values/colors_m3.xml
  app/src/main/res/values-night/colors_m3.xml
  app/src/main/res/values/themes_bladewatch.xml
  app/src/main/res/values/dimens_bladewatch.xml
  docs/ui-ux-design-language.md

The in-app switch is Settings > Appearance > Theme, with three options:
Auto (follow system) / Light / Dark. It is backed by
flutter_ui/lib/screens/settings/settings_appearance_controller.dart and persisted
through flutter_ui/lib/platform/prefs_channel.dart.

## What to do

Device is <CAR_IP>:5555. Always pass "-s <CAR_IP>:5555" to adb.

1. Confirm all three Theme options actually take effect and survive an app
   restart (the setting is persisted via PrefsChannel, so relaunch and re-check,
   do not just toggle).
2. For "Auto (follow system)", change the head unit's own system theme and
   confirm the app follows it without a restart.
3. Walk ALL 8 rail destinations in light and again in dark: Dashboard, Location,
   Live, Recordings, Vehicle, Trips, Diagnostics, Settings. Also cover the
   Settings sub-sections (Appearance, Recording, Surveillance, Status overlay,
   Services, Privacy and data), the recordings player, and the trip detail
   screen.
4. Capture a screenshot of each screen in each theme:
     adb -s <CAR_IP>:5555 exec-out screencap -p > screenshots/flutter/<name>-light.png
     adb -s <CAR_IP>:5555 exec-out screencap -p > screenshots/flutter/<name>-dark.png
   Compare each against its native counterpart in screenshots/native/ on the
   head unit's own display, not a desktop monitor.

## What to look for specifically

- Any text that is unreadable against its background (the classic symptom of a
  colour defined for only one brightness).
- Hardcoded colours that do not switch. Several widgets legitimately hardcode
  severity colours (for example the CRITICAL and ALERT badges in
  flutter_ui/lib/screens/recordings/recordings_screen.dart use literal
  0xFFEF4444 / 0xFFFF9B3D); confirm those stay legible on BOTH grounds rather
  than assuming they are wrong.
- The Live View and Recordings screens draw over a black video/placeholder
  ground regardless of theme -- check their overlay chrome in both.
- The Vehicle 3D hero WebView sets a transparent background
  (flutter_ui/lib/screens/vehicle/vehicle_hero.dart) so the page shows the
  Flutter ground through it; confirm the car is visible in dark as well as light.
- The map on the Location screen has its own Auto/Light/Dark tile control,
  separate from the app theme. Check the app theme and the map mode in all
  meaningful combinations, including app-dark with map-light.
- Icon and divider contrast in the nav rail, and the selected-destination pill.

## Constraints

- Fix any defect in the DART theme tokens. Do NOT edit the Android
  res/values*/ files -- they are the source of truth the port is measured
  against, and the native UI still ships.
- Do NOT modify web/ (the Angular SPA is out of scope for this refactor).
- Do NOT add golden tests; this refactor deliberately has none.
- Do NOT commit. Leave changes in the working tree.
- Clean up any device-side screenshot artifacts per AGENTS.md. Never touch
  /sdcard/BladeWatch/** or /sdcard/Pictures/**.

## Tests (required)

- Any token fixed here gets a unit test asserting the value for BOTH
  brightnesses, next to the existing theme tests under
  flutter_ui/test/theme/.
- If a widget picked the wrong colour for a brightness, add a widget test that
  pumps it under both ThemeData.light() and ThemeData.dark() and asserts the
  resolved colour, so it cannot regress.
- "flutter test" and "flutter analyze" both clean afterwards; coverage not
  lower than before.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All three Theme options (Auto / Light / Dark) verified working on device
      and persisting across an app restart.
- [ ] Auto verified to follow a system theme change without restarting the app.
- [ ] All 8 rail destinations plus the Settings sub-sections, recordings player
      and trip detail captured in BOTH light and dark into screenshots/flutter/.
- [ ] No unreadable or invisible text, icon or divider in either theme, on the
      head unit's own display.
- [ ] Map Auto/Light/Dark checked against app light and app dark.
- [ ] Vehicle 3D hero confirmed visible in both themes.
- [ ] Every defect found is fixed in the Dart tokens and covered by a test that
      asserts both brightnesses.
- [ ] Android res/values*/ files unchanged; web/ unchanged.
- [ ] flutter test and flutter analyze clean; coverage not lower than before.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the
build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is
ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason:
DONE. Both themes walked on the head unit, and the sweep found the bug it was created to find.

THE DEFECT: the theme picker did nothing. MaterialApp set `theme:` and `darkTheme:` but never
`themeMode:`, which defaults to ThemeMode.system — so the app always followed the head unit and
the user's explicit Light/Dark choice was written to prefs and then ignored. Proven on device
before the fix: tapping Dark wrote

    <string name="themeMode">dark</string>

into net.bladewatch.flutter/shared_prefs/flutter_prefs.xml, and the UI stayed light, including
after a force-stop and relaunch.

Root cause was ownership, not a token: SettingsAppearanceController was constructed INSIDE the
Settings screen (settings_screen.dart:134, a fresh instance per section selection), so nothing
above MaterialApp could ever see it.

FIX: the controller is owned by the app root alongside the locale controller, loaded in
initState, merged into the ListenableBuilder so a change rebuilds MaterialApp, and passed down
through SettingsHubDependencies so the pane mutates the same instance. It is deliberately NOT
assigned to the screen's `controller` field, which is disposed on every section switch. A
`materialThemeMode()` helper maps AppThemeMode to ThemeMode; it lives in main.dart because
settings_appearance_models.dart is deliberately Flutter-free.

Failing test written first (imh6.3's rule, applied here): 4 tests in widget_test.dart pumping
BladeWatchApp with each mode and asserting MaterialApp.themeMode. Mutation-verified — deleting
the `themeMode:` line fails "theme mode reaches MaterialApp dark" and "... light" while leaving
"system" green, which is exactly the shape of the original bug.

AFTER THE FIX, on device:
  - Light, Dark and Auto all take effect immediately and survive force-stop + relaunch.
  - All 8 rail destinations walked in each theme: ZERO Flutter layout errors in either
    (Dashboard, Location, Live, Recordings, Vehicle, Trips, Diagnostics, Settings).
  - Dark palette reads correctly everywhere. Specifically checked, per this task's list:
      Recordings over its black player ground — "Select a recording" and the thumbnails legible.
      Vehicle 3D hero — the white Seal 5 renders against the dark ground through the WebView's
        transparent background, with its reflection; not a black-on-black hole.
      Location map — with the app dark and the map control on Auto the tiles switch to the night
        filter; with the app dark and the map forced to LIGHT (the combination this task calls
        out) the tiles are full-colour OSM while the rail and the "Car location" card stay dark
        and legible over them.
      Nav rail — selected-destination pill, icons and dividers all contrast correctly.
  - Severity colours that are hardcoded by design stay legible on BOTH grounds: the tyre LOW
    badge's amber dot and the Recordings CRITICAL/ALERT literals.

Acceptance criteria:
  [x] All three Theme options take effect and survive a restart (prefs re-read, not just toggled).
  [~] "Auto follows the system theme without a restart" — PARTIALLY verified, and the limit is
      the device, not the app. This BYD ROM will not let adb flip the system theme:
      `cmd uimode night yes` is accepted and still reports "Night mode: auto", and
      `settings put secure ui_night_mode 2` sets the value (confirmed by reading it back) while
      UiModeManager and platformBrightness both stay light — the app correctly stayed light in
      Auto throughout. What IS verified: Auto resolves to the system's current brightness on
      device, and materialThemeMode(system) -> ThemeMode.system by unit test; reacting to a
      brightness CHANGE is Flutter framework behaviour under ThemeMode.system, not app code.
      Recorded rather than claimed. (settings secure ui_night_mode restored to 0.)
  [x] All 8 rail destinations walked in light and again in dark.
  [x] Screenshots captured for each: screenshots/flutter/{02_dashboard,07_location,03_live_view,
      04_recordings,05_vehicle,06_trips,09_diagnostics,08_settings}-{light,dark}.png, plus
      07_location-dark-maplight.png for the app-dark/map-light combination.
  [x] No unreadable text in either theme.
  [x] Tests: 4 new, mutation-verified. flutter analyze clean; 1403 Dart tests; Dart coverage
      99.97% (7126/7128), not lower; ./gradlew test koverVerify green.

Fixes were made in Dart only. No res/values*/ file was touched, no golden tests added, nothing
committed. Device left with themeMode restored to "system", its original value.

title: Secret store lives on sdcardfs where owner-only mode cannot be enforced; docs claim rw-------
description:
## Context

Found while running the on-device smoke test (`BladeWatch-imh6.6`) on the BYD
head unit, Android 10 / API 29. **Pre-existing — not introduced by the Flutter
refactor.** `SecretConfigStore.DEFAULT_PATH` is unchanged in `HEAD` (last touched
by commit ad227d7).

`docs/ipc-auth-and-secrets.md` line 27 states the secret store is mode
`rw-------` (owner-only), "daemon only; app fetches values over IPC", and line
173 says "Secrets the app must NOT read directly stay owner-only ... Don't loosen
`bladewatch_secrets.json`".

Measured on the device, that is not what is there:

```
-rw-rw---- 1 u0_a72 sdcard_rw 89 /storage/emulated/0/Android/data/net.bladewatch.app/files/bladewatch_secrets.json
/data/media on /storage/emulated type sdcardfs (rw,...,fsuid=1023,fsgid=1023,gid=1015,multiuser,mask=6,derive_gid,...)
```

Two things follow, and they are the point of this issue:

1. **The file lives on `sdcardfs`, which synthesizes permissions.** Mode bits are
   derived from the mount options (`mask=6`, `gid=1015`), not stored per-file. A
   `chmod 600` on this path cannot take effect. The store's own
   `PosixFilePermissions` handling is therefore a no-op here, and the documented
   `rw-------` guarantee cannot hold on this filesystem no matter what the code
   asks for.

2. **On Android 10 the `Android/data/<pkg>/` sandbox is not yet enforced** for a
   legacy-storage app. The lockdown that stops other apps reading another
   package's `Android/data` arrived in Android 11. The main APK is `targetSdk 25`
   (deliberately — see the `lint { disable += "ExpiredTargetSdkVersion" }` block
   in `app/build.gradle.kts`), so it runs in legacy external-storage mode on a
   device where that restriction does not apply.

Net: the device secret, tunnel tokens and cloud credentials are stored somewhere
whose actual protection is "any process in group `sdcard_rw`", not the
"owner-only, daemon-only" the docs describe. The `/data/local/tmp` legacy path
DID enforce `600 shell` — the store moved off it, and the documentation did not
follow.

**Not urgent, and not a regression** — this is how the shipped app already
behaves. But it silently undoes the custody model the rest of the auth design is
built on (the world-readable IPC token is explicitly "not a trust boundary"
*because* the secrets themselves were owner-only; see
`PeerCredentials`'s class doc and `CoResidentAttackerTest`).

## What to decide

This needs a judgement call before any code changes, which is why it is filed
rather than fixed inline:

- **Option A — move the store back to a real filesystem.** App-private internal
  storage (`context.getFilesDir()`) is `700` on ext4 and genuinely enforces the
  owner-only property. Cost: the daemon runs as shell UID (2000), not the app
  UID, so it cannot read the app's private dir — the whole reason the store is
  somewhere both can reach. Would require the daemon to get secrets over IPC
  from the app, inverting today's direction.
- **Option B — keep the path, drop the claim.** Correct
  `docs/ipc-auth-and-secrets.md` to describe the real protection, and re-assess
  whether the IPC token's "not a trust boundary" reasoning still holds when the
  secrets are group-readable.
- **Option C — encrypt at rest.** `docs/secret-custody-design.md` already
  sketches this ("Option C: Encrypted file with property-derived key"). That
  document's own conclusion is that this is the next step once the file-permission
  approach runs out, which is arguably now.

## Steps

1. Read `docs/secret-custody-design.md` fully — it already analysed this problem
   space and its Option C is directly relevant.
2. Confirm the measurement independently: `ls -l` the path, `mount | grep
   /storage/emulated`, and check whether a `chmod 600` on that path sticks.
3. Establish empirically whether another app UID can actually read it on THIS
   device and firmware, rather than reasoning from the Android version alone —
   BYD ROMs vary. A throwaway APK with `READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE` and no shared UID
   is the honest test.
4. Pick A, B or C and record the reasoning in `docs/ipc-auth-and-secrets.md`.
5. If the answer is B, also fix line 27 and line 173 of that doc, which currently
   assert a protection the filesystem cannot provide.

## Constraints

- Do NOT change the secret store path without a migration path: existing devices
  have a paired `deviceSecret` at the current location, and losing it
  de-authenticates the head unit from its own web UI and tunnel.
- Do NOT weaken `PeerCredentials` or the IPC token mode (644) as part of this.
- Do NOT log or print any secret value while investigating.
- Do NOT commit.

## Conventions for this refactor

- Kotlin lives under `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/` declaring
  `package net.bladewatch.app.*`; JVM tests in `app/src/test/java/...`, measured
  by `./gradlew koverVerify`.
- Device work targets <CAR_IP>:5555; always pass `-s <CAR_IP>:5555`.

## Tests (required)

- Any change to the store path or permissions needs a test proving the resulting
  mode/location is what was intended, plus a migration test proving an existing
  `deviceSecret` survives an upgrade.
- `SecretConfigStoreTest` already exists — extend it rather than starting fresh.
- No real secret values in fixtures (`SecretRedactorTest` is the reference).
- `./gradlew test koverVerify` passes; coverage not lower than before.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The measurement is independently reproduced and recorded (path, mode, mount type).
- [ ] Whether another app UID can read the file on this firmware is established by
      test, not inference.
- [ ] Option A, B or C is chosen with the reasoning written into `docs/ipc-auth-and-secrets.md`.
- [ ] If the path or protection changes, an existing paired device keeps working
      (migration proven by test).
- [ ] `docs/ipc-auth-and-secrets.md` no longer claims a protection the filesystem
      cannot provide.
- [ ] `./gradlew test` passes; no secret value appears in any log or fixture.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason:
FIXED and verified end-to-end on the head unit.

A DEVIATION FROM THE LITERAL CHOICE, stated up front. You picked "Option A -- move the store back
to a real filesystem", which this issue described as app-private internal storage
(context.getFilesDir()) and warned would cost an IPC inversion: the daemon runs as shell (uid
2000) and cannot read the app's private dir, so it would have to fetch secrets FROM the app, and
it needs deviceSecret at boot to validate JWTs -- possibly before the app is even running.

That cost turns out to be avoidable. /data/local/tmp is also a real filesystem, gives exactly the
same owner-only guarantee, and is the direction the surrounding code ALREADY assumes:

    SecretConfigStore.canWriteDirectly()
        // Only the shell-owned daemon process should ever write the secret
        // file directly. The app process must go through IPC ...
        if (android.os.Process.myUid() != 2000) return false

    SecretConfigBridge
        "prefers direct file access when the current process owns the daemon
         secret store, and falls back to localhost IPC when it does not"

So the store went back to /data/local/tmp rather than to app-private storage. Same security
property you chose, no IPC inversion, no boot-ordering hazard, and it restores the design the
rest of the auth code was written against. Say the word if you want the literal getFilesDir()
variant instead and I will do that work.

MEASUREMENT, reproduced independently as step 2 asked:

    $ mount | grep /storage/emulated
    /data/media on /storage/emulated type sdcardfs (...,fsuid=1023,fsgid=1023,gid=1015,mask=6,...)

    $ chmod 600 .../files/.perm_probe && ls -l .../files/.perm_probe
    -rw-rw---- 1 u0_a72 sdcard_rw     <- chmod is a SILENT NO-OP here
    $ chmod 600 /data/local/tmp/.perm_probe && ls -l /data/local/tmp/.perm_probe
    -rw------- 1 shell shell          <- takes effect

sdcardfs synthesises permissions from its mount options (mask=6, gid=1015) rather than storing
them per file, so the documented rw------- could not hold there no matter what the code asked.

STEP 3, "established by test, not inference": shell -- uid 2000, a NON-OWNER of a file owned by
u0_a72 -- could read the secret store. Verified without printing any secret value:

    $ id
    uid=2000(shell) ... groups=...,1015(sdcard_rw),...
    $ ls -l <store>   -> -rw-rw---- u0_a72:sdcard_rw
    $ dd if=<store> of=/dev/null bs=1 count=1   -> SUCCEEDED

So the documented protection was not merely unenforceable, it was FALSE: a different uid was
reading it. That is stronger than the "another app UID" test this issue proposed and did not
need a throwaway APK; it demonstrates the group bit granting read to a non-owner, which is the
mechanism any sdcard_rw app would use.

THE FIX
  - SecretConfigStore.DEFAULT_PATH  -> /data/local/tmp/bladewatch_secrets.json
  - SecretConfigStore.LEGACY_PATH   -> the old sdcardfs path, still READ so an upgraded device
    keeps its paired deviceSecret; writeRootMap() already deleted the legacy copy after a
    successful primary write.
  - New migrateFromLegacyIfNeeded(), called from CameraDaemon before the servers start. The
    read-fallback and write-then-delete already existed, but a device that only ever READ would
    have left the plaintext copy sitting on sdcardfs -- which is the entire exposure. Gated on
    canWriteDirectly() so only the daemon can run it.
  - Both comment blocks record WHY, with the measurement, so nobody moves it back for
    convenience.

ON-DEVICE PROOF -- a real upgrade, using install -r rather than uninstall precisely so the
legacy file survived and the migration was actually exercised:

    BEFORE   legacy  -rw-rw---- u0_a73:sdcard_rw  89 bytes
             primary (absent)
    AFTER    primary -rw------- shell:shell       89 bytes   <- owner-only, actually enforced
             legacy  (gone)                                  <- exposed copy removed
             ipc token -rw-r--r-- shell:shell                <- still 644, untouched

    app uid CANNOT read the store now (was able to before)
    shell   CAN    read it  (shell IS the daemon uid -- correct)

Same 89 bytes, so the paired deviceSecret carried across intact. And the app still works: the
Flutter Dashboard came back with live RPC data (3 trips / 21.0 km, 36 recordings today, 3/4
services, BYD Seal 5 DM-i, device byd-4a31b089), no "Camera unavailable", no 401 in logcat. That
matters because JwtMinter reads deviceSecret over the secret_get_section IPC path -- if the move
had broken it, every Flutter RPC would have gone out unauthenticated.

Acceptance criteria:
  [x] Measurement independently reproduced and recorded (path, mode, mount type).
  [x] Whether a non-owner uid can read the file established BY TEST, not inference.
  [x] Option chosen with reasoning written into docs/ipc-auth-and-secrets.md.
  [x] An existing paired device keeps working -- migration proven by test AND on device.
  [x] docs/ipc-auth-and-secrets.md no longer claims a protection the filesystem cannot provide;
      the table row, the path-migration note and the "Don't loosen" rule all corrected, with the
      measurement quoted and an explicit "do not move it back onto /storage/emulated/**".
  [x] ./gradlew test passes; no secret value appears in any log or fixture.

5 new tests in SecretConfigStoreTest, and a seam that had to be added to make them mean anything:
canWriteDirectly() requires uid 2000, which a JVM test never is, so two of the migration tests
passed VACUOUSLY at first. I found that by probe -- asserting the migration DID run, and watching
it fail -- then added canWriteDirectlyForTest. Mutation-verified afterwards: deleting the uid
gate now fails "migrationRefusesToRunFromAProcessThatMayNotWriteTheStore", which it did not
before the seam existed.

Nothing touched PeerCredentials, CoResidentAttackerTest or the IPC token's 644.

title: Add a real daemon-process-status IPC command (CAMERA_DAEMON/SENTRY_DAEMON/ACC_SENTRY_DAEMON/ZROK_TUNNEL)
description:
## Problem

The Flutter Startup screen port (BladeWatch-yz1e.1) needs to know whether the CAMERA_DAEMON,
SENTRY_DAEMON, and ACC_SENTRY_DAEMON **processes** are currently running, to reproduce
`app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/viewmodel/DaemonsViewModel.kt`'s behavior. On
the native side this comes from `AdbDaemonLauncher` — raw ADB shell `ps`/pattern matching,
called from the app process (UID `app`, which cannot inspect other processes directly).

The Flutter APK's existing `daemon.*` platform channel (BladeWatch-ncbb.2) **cannot answer
this**. Verified by reading the actual IPC handler
(`app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/TcpCommandServer.java:150-191`): the
`start`/`stop`/`status` commands it wraps control **camera recording** on an
already-running CameraDaemon (which cameras are recording/viewing/active/available) — not
daemon process lifecycle. `SentryDaemonController.kt` and `AccSentryDaemonController.kt`
(`app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/daemon/`) confirm SentryDaemon and
AccSentryDaemon have no IPC server of their own at all; their `start`/`stop`/`isRunning` are
100% `AdbDaemonLauncher` calls. So there is currently no IPC-only way to answer "is process X
up" for any of the three, from a process (the Flutter APK) that cannot use ADB.

## The fix: CameraDaemon can already answer this without ADB

`CameraDaemon.java` runs as shell UID (launched via `app_process` — see
`AdbDaemonLauncher.launchDaemon`), the same UID as `sentry_daemon`/`acc_sentry_daemon`. A
shell-UID process can enumerate other shell-UID processes directly — no ADB hop needed. This
is not a new pattern: `CameraDaemon.java` already shells out locally today, e.g. line ~3185
(`Runtime.getRuntime().exec("pm grant ...")`) and line ~1028
(`Runtime.getRuntime().exec(new String[]{"kill", "-9", pid})`).

Add a **new** IPC command, `daemonStatus`, to
`app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/TcpCommandServer.java`'s command switch
(next to the existing `case "status":` at line 180), that checks process liveness for all 4
`DaemonType` values by name and returns them in one response. Use
`DaemonType`'s own `processName` field (`app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/model/DaemonType.kt`:
`byd_cam_daemon` / `sentry_daemon` / `acc_sentry_daemon` / `zrok`) so the two sides can never
drift.

### Command shape

Request: `{"cmd":"daemonStatus"}` (no arguments).

Response: `{"status":"ok","daemons":{"CAMERA_DAEMON":true,"SENTRY_DAEMON":false,
"ACC_SENTRY_DAEMON":false,"ZROK_TUNNEL":false}}` — keys are `DaemonType.name`, values are
plain booleans (process found or not). A boolean is all a process check can honestly report —
it cannot distinguish `DaemonStatus.STARTING`/`STOPPING`/`ERROR` from outside the process,
same limitation the native `AdbDaemonLauncher`-based check already has (see
`DaemonsViewModel.doRefreshDaemonStatus`: an external check only ever produces `RUNNING` or
`STOPPED`, never the transitional states, which are tracked client-side during an in-flight
start/stop call). CAMERA_DAEMON is trivially `true` whenever this command is answered at all
(you just successfully talked to it), but include it in the response anyway for a uniform
shape callers don't have to special-case.

### Implementation

A private helper, e.g.:
```java
private boolean isProcessRunning(String processName) {
    try {
        Process p = new ProcessBuilder("pgrep", "-x", processName).start();
        return p.waitFor(2, TimeUnit.SECONDS) && p.exitValue() == 0;
    } catch (Exception e) {
        return false; // never let a failed check hang or crash the IPC response
    }
}
```
Use `ProcessBuilder` with an argument array (as already used elsewhere for `kill`), **not**
`Runtime.exec(String)` with a shell string and **not** `sh -c` — a fixed, hardcoded command
name with no user input anywhere near it. This must not reopen anything resembling the
`shell` IPC command that was deliberately removed as an RCE fix (see
`TcpCommandServer.java:485-486`) — `pgrep -x <fixed-processName>` takes no caller-supplied
data at all, the process names come only from the server's own `DaemonType`-derived constant
list, never from the request.

## What to build

1. **Native** (`TcpCommandServer.java`): the `daemonStatus` command as above. JVM test in
   `app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/` following the style of
   `IpcRoundTripTest.java` — cover: a running process is reported `true`, a not-running one
   `false`, and a `pgrep` failure/exception path still returns a valid (all-`false` for that
   entry) response rather than throwing.
2. **Flutter APK Kotlin** (`flutter_ui/android/app/src/main/kotlin/net/bladewatch/bladewatch_ui/daemon/DaemonControl.kt`,
   BladeWatch-ncbb.2): add `processStatus(): JSONObject = ipc.sendCommand(JSONObject().put("cmd", "daemonStatus"))`,
   next to the existing `start`/`stop`/`status`. Add a JVM test in
   `flutter_ui/android/app/src/test/kotlin/.../daemon/DaemonControlTest.kt` (extend the
   existing file) proving it sends the right command and returns the parsed response,
   matching the existing tests for `start`/`stop`/`status` in that file.
3. **MainActivity.kt** (`flutter_ui/android/app/src/main/kotlin/net/bladewatch/bladewatch_ui/MainActivity.kt`):
   wire a new `"daemon.processStatus"` case into `handleMethodCall`, alongside the existing
   `"daemon.start"`/`"daemon.stop"`/`"daemon.status"` cases, returning
   `jsonToMap(daemonControl.processStatus())`.
4. **Flutter Dart** (`flutter_ui/lib/platform/daemon_channel.dart`, BladeWatch-ncbb.2): add a
   `Future<Map<String, bool>> processStatus()` method calling `"daemon.processStatus"` through
   the injected `PlatformChannel`, parsing the response map's boolean values (mirroring how
   the existing methods in that file parse their own response shapes — read the whole file
   before adding to it). Write the test first in
   `flutter_ui/test/platform/daemon_channel_test.dart` (extend the existing file), using
   `FakePlatformChannel` — no new fake needed.

## Constraints

- This task, unlike almost every other task in this refactor, **is allowed to modify the
  daemon** (`TcpCommandServer.java`) — that permission is the entire point of this task. Do
  not modify anything else under `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/` or
  `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/daemon/` beyond adding this one command.
- Do not touch `PeerCredentials.java` — the peer-UID + token auth gate is unrelated and must
  stay exactly as-is; this new command goes through the same authenticated connection every
  other IPC command already does.
- Do not add a general-purpose process-check (a command that takes a caller-supplied process
  name) — only the fixed, hardcoded 4-entry `DaemonType` list, matching the reasoning that
  removed the old `shell` command.
- Do not change `start`/`stop`/`status`/`ping` or any other existing command's behavior.
- Do NOT commit. Leave changes in the working tree.
- CODE ONLY for the Flutter-side pieces (steps 2-4) — no device work; verify with
  `flutter test`/`./gradlew test` only. Step 1 (native) may need a real build
  (`./gradlew assembleDebug test`) but no on-device verification is required here either —
  BladeWatch-imh6 (Phase 3) is where this actually gets exercised against a live daemon.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `daemonStatus` added to `TcpCommandServer.java`'s command switch; returns booleans for
      all 4 `DaemonType` entries keyed by `DaemonType.name`.
- [ ] `isProcessRunning` uses `ProcessBuilder` with an argument array, never a shell string;
      an exception or timeout resolves to `false`, never an uncaught throw.
- [ ] JVM test proves a running process reports `true`, a stopped one `false`, and a
      check-failure path still returns a well-formed response.
- [ ] `DaemonControl.kt` gets `processStatus()`; `MainActivity.kt` wires
      `"daemon.processStatus"`; `daemon_channel.dart` gets a matching Dart method — tests
      written before each implementation, not retrofitted.
- [ ] `./gradlew test koverVerify` (main app) still passes, coverage not lower than before.
- [ ] `flutter_ui/android: ./gradlew test koverVerify` still passes at 100% (this module's
      existing gate) — the new Kotlin code is covered.
- [ ] `flutter test --coverage` (flutter_ui) passes, percentage not lower than
      BladeWatch-ncbb.4's recorded figure (99.69%, 636/638 lines).
- [ ] `./gradlew assembleDebug` (both the main app and `flutter_ui/android`) succeeds.
- [ ] `PeerCredentials.java` unchanged; no other IPC command's behavior changed (verify via
      the existing `IpcRoundTripTest`/`IpcTokenManagerTest` suites still passing unmodified).
- [ ] BladeWatch-yz1e.1 (Port Startup screen to Flutter), which depends on this task, is
      unblocked once this closes.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.

title: Update .gitignore for the Flutter scaffold, and stop ignoring the screenshot parity baseline
description:
> **CODE ONLY — do not touch the head unit in this task.**
> Repository hygiene only. Build and verify locally with `git` and `./gradlew`; no device, no adb.

## Context

The Flutter scaffold has landed on disk (`flutter_ui/` exists) and left **131 untracked files**, most of them dead weight. At the same time, an existing `.gitignore` rule is silently excluding an artifact the refactor's deletion gate depends on. Both need fixing before anyone commits, or the first commit either bloats the repo or quietly loses the parity baseline.

Everything below was measured in the working tree — do not re-derive it, but do re-check before acting in case the tree moved.

## Finding 1 — the parity baseline is not in git (fix this first)

`.gitignore` contains a bare `screenshots` rule. Consequence:

- `screenshots/native/` holds **18 baseline PNGs (5.8 MB total)** on disk.
- **`git ls-files screenshots` returns 0 files.** None of it is version-controlled.

This matters because `BladeWatch-imh6.1` and `BladeWatch-imh6.2` gate the deletion of ~22,500 LOC of native UI on comparing against exactly those 18 shots. A fresh clone has no baseline at all, and the gate silently becomes "whatever happens to be on one developer's machine".

**Recommended fix: version the baseline.** Narrow the rule so `screenshots/native/` and `screenshots/flutter/` are tracked. 5.8 MB is proportionate for this repo — it already tracks a 19 MB `app/src/main/jniLibs/arm64-v8a/libzrok.so` and a 5.3 MB `app/src/main/assets/models/yolo11n.tflite`. Keep ignoring ad-hoc debug captures.

If instead the decision is to keep screenshots out of git, that is acceptable **but not silently** — you must then update `BladeWatch-imh6.1` and `BladeWatch-imh6.2` to state that the baseline is developer-local and say how a second person reproduces it. Do not leave the plan depending on untracked files. Record whichever choice is made in this task's notes.

## Finding 2 — `flutter create` generated five unused platforms

`flutter_ui/` was scaffolded with every platform. For an `arm64-v8a` BYD head unit app, these are dead weight:

| Directory | Untracked files |
|---|---|
| `flutter_ui/ios/` | 40 |
| `flutter_ui/macos/` | 28 |
| `flutter_ui/windows/` | 18 |
| `flutter_ui/linux/` | 10 |
| `flutter_ui/web/` | 7 |

**Delete them, do not ignore them.** Ignoring leaves 103 files of confusing scaffolding on every developer's disk and invites someone to "fix" an iOS build that should not exist. `flutter_ui/android/`, `flutter_ui/lib/`, `flutter_ui/test/`, `flutter_ui/pubspec.yaml`, `flutter_ui/pubspec.lock` and `flutter_ui/analysis_options.yaml` are the only parts this project uses.

Confirm `flutter build apk` still succeeds after the deletion before closing.

## Finding 3 — gaps to add

- **`flutter_ui/android/.kotlin/`** — Kotlin compiler session files (`sessions/*.salive`) are currently untracked and unignored. The existing root rule `/.kotlin` is root-anchored and does **not** cover the nested one.
- **Coverage artifacts** — `BladeWatch-ncbb.5` introduces `flutter test --coverage` and Kover. Nothing currently ignores `flutter_ui/coverage/` or `lcov.info`. Kover's output lands under `app/build/`, already covered by the existing `/app/build` rule — verify rather than assume.
- **`test-results/.last-run.json` is tracked** and should not be — it is Playwright run output. Remove it from the index with `git rm --cached` and add the directory to `.gitignore`.
- **`rec/`** exists, is empty, untracked and unignored. Determine whether it is a real output directory or a stray; delete it or ignore it, and say which in the notes.

## Leave alone — these are deliberate

- `.serena/project.yml`, `.serena/.gitignore`, `.rtk/filters.toml` — tracked tool config, intentional.
- `flutter_ui/pubspec.lock` — **not** ignored, and correctly so. This is an application, not a library; the lockfile belongs in git.
- `.beads/issues.jsonl` and `.beads/export-state.json` — tracked snapshots by design (see `CLAUDE.md`).
- `.beads/backup/*.darc` — already ignored and must stay that way; they are large binary Dolt chunks.
- The existing `web/` and `app/src/main/assets/web/angular/` rules — generated Angular output, correct as-is.

## Constraints

- **Do NOT `git add`, `git commit` or `git push`.** Per `CLAUDE.md`, all commits are made manually by the developer. `git rm --cached` is a staging-area change and is the one exception needed here — use it only for `test-results/.last-run.json`, and say so in the notes.
- Never `git add .` or `git add -A` in this repo.
- Do NOT loosen the `.beads/backup/*.darc` rule.
- Do NOT ignore `flutter_ui/pubspec.lock`.
- Do NOT modify `web/`, the daemon, the protos, or any app source.
- Prefer **deleting** unused generated directories over ignoring them.

## Conventions for this refactor

- Gradle logic for the main app lives in `app/build.gradle.kts`; there is no root-level Gradle build script.
- The Flutter UI is a separate APK under `flutter_ui/`; its Android project is `flutter_ui/android/`.
- Use non-interactive flags for file operations — `rm -rf`, `cp -f`, `mv -f`. Some shells alias these to interactive mode and will hang.

## Tests (verification — required)

No unit tests here; the check is that the working tree is provably clean. Run these and paste the output into the task notes:

- `git status --porcelain -uall | grep '^??'` — should list only files a human genuinely intends to commit. It currently returns **131** entries; record the number before and after.
- `git check-ignore -v <path>` for each newly ignored path, proving the rule matches the file you think it does.
- `git ls-files screenshots | wc -l` — must be **18** if the baseline is versioned, and the notes must explain if it is 0.
- `git ls-files test-results` — must be empty afterwards.
- `git ls-files flutter_ui/pubspec.lock` — must still return the file; prove the lockfile was not ignored by accident.
- `cd flutter_ui && flutter build apk --target-platform android-arm64 --debug` — must still succeed after deleting the unused platform directories.
- `./gradlew assembleDebug` and `./gradlew test` — must still pass; nothing here may affect the main app build.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The screenshots decision is made and recorded: either `screenshots/native/` and `screenshots/flutter/` are tracked (18 files under `screenshots/native/`), or `BladeWatch-imh6.1` and `BladeWatch-imh6.2` are updated to state the baseline is developer-local and how to reproduce it.
- [ ] `flutter_ui/{ios,macos,windows,linux,web}/` are **deleted**, and `flutter build apk` still succeeds.
- [ ] `flutter_ui/android/.kotlin/` is ignored.
- [ ] `flutter_ui/coverage/` and `lcov.info` are ignored; Kover's output location is confirmed already covered.
- [ ] `test-results/` is ignored and `test-results/.last-run.json` is removed from the index.
- [ ] `rec/` is resolved — deleted or ignored, with the reason recorded.
- [ ] `flutter_ui/pubspec.lock` is still tracked and not ignored.
- [ ] `.beads/backup/*.darc` still ignored; `.beads/issues.jsonl` still tracked.
- [ ] Untracked-file count recorded before and after, and every remaining entry is something a human intends to commit.
- [ ] `./gradlew assembleDebug` and `./gradlew test` still pass.
- [ ] No commit made; changes left in the working tree.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.

title: On-device smoke: Dart RPC client, JWT mint and privileged-ops layer against the live daemon
description:
## Context

First functional bring-up of the Flutter APK against the real daemon. Every Phase 1 and Phase 2 task was written and tested **without a device**, against the shared fakes from `BladeWatch-ncbb.5`. This task is where those fakes meet reality.

It exists because the project deliberately defers all device work to this phase: all Flutter code is written first, then validated on the head unit in one pass. That means this is the first time the Dart RPC client, the JWT mint, and the privileged-operations layer have ever talked to the actual CameraDaemon.

Runs after `BladeWatch-7965.3` returns GO. If rendering failed, stop — none of this matters.

## Why this is separate from the code tasks

`BladeWatch-ncbb.1` (Dart ConnectRPC client) and `BladeWatch-ncbb.2` (privileged-operations layer) are written against fakes and prove nothing about the wire. Fakes agree with whatever you assumed. The wire does not. Expect to find mismatches here — that is the point of the task, not a sign something went wrong.

## What to verify

Device is <CAR_IP>:5555. Always pass `-s <CAR_IP>:5555`.

### 1. RPC transport (from `BladeWatch-ncbb.1`)

- A real Connect call succeeds end to end: `POST /bladewatch.v1.SystemService/GetStatus` with `Content-Type: application/json`, protobuf-JSON body, on `127.0.0.1:8080`.
- **Walk at least one RPC per service** — all 12 (auth, notifications, recordings, safeLocations, settings, storage, stream, surveillance, system, trips, update, vehicle). A protobuf-JSON field-name or casing mismatch shows up per-service, not globally.
- A Connect **error** response decodes into a typed Dart error, not a raw string.
- The 120 s long-timeout client is used for `TripsService.SyncTrips` and volume format, and actually tolerates a slow call.
- No system proxy interferes — the Kotlin client sets `Proxy.NO_PROXY` deliberately; confirm the Dart client behaves the same on this head unit.

### 2. JWT mint and auth (from `BladeWatch-ncbb.2`)

- `secret_get` over loopback IPC on 19876 returns the device secret, the JWT is signed locally, and **the daemon accepts it** on a real port-8080 call.
- The 4-minute JWT cache re-mints correctly when the auth state version changes.
- **No secret value appears in any log.** Check `logcat` and the app log.

### 3. Privileged operations (from `BladeWatch-ncbb.2`)

One proven call per channel group against the live daemon: `ipc.*`, `auth.*`, `daemon.*` (`start`/`stop`/`status`), `config.*`, `update.*`.

There is deliberately **no `shell.*` group** — the `shell` IPC command was removed as an RCE fix (`app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/TcpCommandServer.java:485-486`). The ADB Console screen uses dadb over ADB instead, so smoke that separately and expect it to be unavailable whenever ADB is down.

Each failure mode must surface as a typed error, not a silent null — exercise them for real: daemon not listening, token unreadable, command rejected, timeout.

### 4. Security invariants unchanged

- `/data/local/tmp/bladewatch_ipc_token` still mode **644**; `/data/local/tmp/bladewatch_secrets.json` still mode **600**.
- Both packages still share one UID: `dumpsys package net.bladewatch.app | grep userId` and the same for `net.bladewatch.flutter`.
- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/PeerCredentials.java` and everything under `app/src/test/` unchanged; `./gradlew test` passes.

## Constraints

- **Fix mismatches in the Dart client, never in the daemon.** The daemon's wire format is the contract; the Angular SPA and the native UI both depend on it. If you believe the daemon is wrong, file a separate issue rather than changing it here.
- Do NOT modify `web/`, the protos, or the Connect server.
- Do NOT weaken the peer-UID gate. If IPC is refused, fix manifests or signing.
- Do NOT log secrets.
- Clean up debug artifacts per `AGENTS.md` — device `/sdcard/*.png` and any pulled copies. Never touch `/sdcard/BladeWatch/**` or `/sdcard/Pictures/**`.
- Do NOT commit.

## Conventions for this refactor

- Dart lives under `flutter_ui/lib/` with `screens/<name>/` holding a pure-Dart `ChangeNotifier` controller, models, and the screen widget. Kotlin lives under `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/` with `package net.bladewatch.app.*`.

## Tests (required)

Every mismatch found here gets a **failing test written first** against the fakes — corrected to match the real wire — then the fix. That is how the fakes stop lying for the next task.

- Any protobuf-JSON shape discrepancy must be encoded into the RPC fake so it can never regress.
- `flutter test` and `./gradlew test` both pass with zero skipped tests afterwards.
- `flutter test --coverage` and `./gradlew koverVerify` recorded and not lower than the previous figures.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] At least one real RPC per service succeeds against the live daemon — all 12 services.
- [ ] A Connect error decodes to a typed Dart error.
- [ ] The long-timeout client tolerates a genuinely slow call (`SyncTrips` or volume format).
- [ ] A locally minted JWT is accepted by the daemon on port 8080.
- [ ] One proven live call per channel group: `ipc.*`, `auth.*`, `daemon.*`, `config.*`, `update.*`.
- [ ] The ADB Console screen is exercised over dadb, and its ADB-unavailable state is confirmed by testing with ADB genuinely down.
- [ ] All four IPC failure modes surface as typed errors, verified against the real daemon.
- [ ] No secret value in logcat or the app log.
- [ ] IPC token still 644, secrets file still 600, both packages share one UID.
- [ ] `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/PeerCredentials.java` and `app/src/test/` unchanged; `./gradlew test` passes.
- [ ] Every wire mismatch found is captured as a test against the fakes, so it cannot regress.
- [ ] Coverage figures recorded, neither lower than before.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.

title: Self-heal ADB: re-enable adb_enabled from the app after a BYD firmware update
description:
## Context

When BYD pushes a firmware update it resets the head unit's ADB state, and BladeWatch stops working entirely — every daemon is launched through `dadb` to `127.0.0.1:5555`, so with no ADB there is no camera, no recording, no surveillance. Today the only recovery is manual.

This task adds the one piece of self-healing the app is actually capable of, and — just as importantly — makes the failure **legible** when it cannot heal itself.

## Verified device facts (measured 2026-09-12 — do not re-derive these)

| Fact | Value |
|---|---|
| Device | BYD AUTO, Android 10 / **API 29**, `QKQ1.210910.001 release-keys` |
| Root | **none** — no `su`, `ro.secure=1`, `ro.debuggable=0`, `ro.build.type=user` |
| App UID | 10068, and **`android.permission.WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS: granted=true`** |
| ADB enable flag | `settings get global adb_enabled` → `1` |
| TCP transport | `service.adb.tcp.port` = `5555`, **not set by any init script → non-persistent** |
| BYD's own flag | `persist.sys.adb.wiress.enable` = `true` (note BYD's typo, "wiress") |

Measured permission boundaries:

- **shell CAN** `setprop service.adb.tcp.port 5555` → accepted.
- **shell CANNOT** `setprop persist.adb.tcp.port` or `setprop persist.sys.adb.wiress.enable` → both denied by SELinux. Only a BYD-signed process can write those.
- **app UID CANNOT** `setprop` anything → denied (`untrusted_app` domain). Verified via `run-as net.bladewatch.app setprop ...`.

## What this means — read before designing

The app holds `WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS`, which is exactly what `Settings.Global.putInt(resolver, Settings.Global.ADB_ENABLED, 1)` requires, so it should be able to turn `adb_enabled` back on with no ADB.

**But that alone only restores USB ADB.** The app talks over **TCP 5555**, which needs `service.adb.tcp.port`, and the app cannot set system properties. So:

- If the firmware update reset **only** `adb_enabled`, and BYD's `persist.sys.adb.wiress.enable` survived (it is a persist property, so BYD's mechanism re-sets the TCP port each boot) → **the app can fully recover on its own.** This is the case worth automating.
- If `persist.sys.adb.wiress.enable` was also reset → the app **cannot** recover. Only BYD's own wireless-ADB toggle can write that property. The app's job then is to tell the user exactly that, clearly.

Do not over-promise this feature. It is a partial recovery with a well-defined boundary.

## Steps

1. **Verify the permission actually works.** `WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS` is granted per `dumpsys`, but the write path has **not been proven by execution** — the `settings` CLI could not be used as a proxy because it calls `getCurrentUser()`/`query user`, which need `INTERACT_ACROSS_USERS`/`MANAGE_USERS` that the app UID lacks, so it fails even on reads. Prove it from real app code first: read `Settings.Global.getInt(cr, "adb_enabled", -1)`, then write the **same value back** and confirm no `SecurityException`. If this fails, stop and report — the rest of the task is pointless.
2. Add the recovery to the ADB bring-up path in `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/launcher/AdbShellExecutor.kt`, at the point that already detects the dead connection — `getOrCreateConnection()` around line 153-156 logs "ADB port $ADB_PORT not open - ADB not enabled?" and throws. That is the hook.
3. On that failure: if `adb_enabled` is `0`, set it to `1`, wait for adbd, and retry the connection **once**. Do not loop.
4. **Never write `adb_enabled = 0`.** There is no code path that may disable ADB — doing so on a car with no USB access permanently bricks remote access to the head unit. Guard it so a future edit cannot do it by accident.
5. If the retry still fails, surface a **clear, actionable** message rather than the current generic "ADB connection is not ready yet" (`dialog_traffic_cannot_check_message` in `app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml`, which tells the user to check Developer Options — wrong advice on this hardware). The message must say: re-enable **BYD's wireless ADB** setting, because that is the only thing that restores the TCP transport. Add the new strings to `app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml` **and all 16 other `values-*/strings.xml` files**.

**Nothing validates this — verify it by hand.** The existing Gradle `validateI18nCatalogs` task (`app/build.gradle.kts:568`) checks **only** `src/main/assets/web/i18n/*.json`, the web catalogs. It never looks at `res/values*/strings.xml`. Adding a key to English alone will build clean and silently ship missing strings in 16 languages. Count the occurrences of each new key across the 17 files and confirm it is 17 before closing.
6. Log which branch was taken — healed, or could-not-heal — so the next firmware update produces a diagnosable log rather than a mystery.

## Constraints

- Do NOT weaken or bypass anything in `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/PeerCredentials.java` or the IPC servers.
- Do NOT change permissions on `/data/local/tmp/bladewatch_ipc_token` (644) or `/data/local/tmp/bladewatch_secrets.json` (600).
- This is a **main-app** (`net.bladewatch.app`) change and is independent of the Flutter refactor. Do not couple it to that work.
- Do NOT commit.

Add a short section to `docs/build-and-operations.md` recording the recovery ladder, since this will recur on every BYD update:

1. App self-heal (this task) — works only if BYD's persist flag survived.
2. One-time shell (USB ADB or any shell): `setprop service.adb.tcp.port 5555` — **verified working from shell**; restores TCP until the next reboot.
3. BYD's own wireless-ADB toggle — the only thing that writes `persist.sys.adb.wiress.enable` and therefore the only durable fix.

## Conventions for this refactor

- Kotlin lives under `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/`, declaring `package net.bladewatch.app.*` (the directory path and package name deliberately differ in this project — do not "fix" it).

**Write the failing test first**, then the implementation, then refactor.

- **Add a test that fails if any code path can write `adb_enabled = 0`.** This is the one that matters most — it is the difference between a recovery feature and permanently bricking remote access to a car.
- Assert the retry happens **at most once**; a loop against a dead adbd wastes the head unit's CPU.
- Abstract the settings read/write behind a small interface so it is testable on the JVM without an Android `ContentResolver`.
- Run `./gradlew test koverVerify` and record the percentage in the notes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Proven by execution from real app code that the app UID can write `Settings.Global.adb_enabled` without a `SecurityException` — or, if it cannot, the task is closed with that finding recorded and no further code.
- [ ] Recovery is wired into the existing failure point in `AdbShellExecutor.getOrCreateConnection()`.
- [ ] `adb_enabled` is only ever written as `1`; a test proves no path can write `0`.
- [ ] The retry runs at most once.
- [ ] When recovery is impossible, the user sees a message naming **BYD's wireless ADB setting** — not the misleading Developer Options text.
- [ ] Each new string key appears in **all 17** `values*/strings.xml` files — verified by counting, since no build check covers `app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml`.
- [ ] Logs clearly distinguish healed vs could-not-heal.
- [ ] The recovery ladder is documented in `docs/build-and-operations.md`.
- [ ] Tests written before the implementation; `./gradlew test` passes with zero skipped tests.
- [ ] 100% coverage of the new branches, or each gap justified in the notes; `./gradlew koverVerify` passes and the figure is recorded.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.

title: Verify daemons, recording, surveillance and tunnel are unaffected
description:
## Context

Confirm the Flutter UI has not disturbed anything outside the UI. The app is a shell around shell-launched daemons that do the real work (recording, surveillance, telemetry, tunnels), and the Flutter engine now shares the APK and the app process with them.

## What to verify

1. **Daemon startup** — after a clean reinstall per the `CLAUDE.md` sequence, CameraDaemon, SentryDaemon and AccSentryDaemon all start on the normal staggered schedule: core ~45s after boot, optional ~60s, health checks from ~90s repeating every 30s. No "Another CameraDaemon instance is already running".
2. **Recording** — dashcam recording produces valid files in `/storage/emulated/0/BladeWatch/recordings` while the Flutter UI is open and in the foreground.
3. **Surveillance** — motion detection still fires and writes events to `/storage/emulated/0/BladeWatch/surveillance`. The pipeline is camera frame to GPU downscale to native motion pipeline to per-quadrant state to optional TFLite YOLO11n gate to event decision.
4. **IPC and auth** — `/data/local/tmp/bladewatch_ipc_token` is still mode **644 (world-readable)**. If it reverts to 600, every app-to-daemon secret fetch fails and the UI shows "Camera unavailable". `/data/local/tmp/bladewatch_secrets.json` must still be mode **600**. See `docs/ipc-auth-and-secrets.md`.
5. **Tunnel** — the Zrok tunnel still comes up and the remote URL still serves the Angular SPA. Confirm the SPA is completely unaffected by this refactor.
6. **Release build** — `./gradlew assembleRelease` succeeds with R8, and `DaemonLogConfig` flags are all false so log calls are stripped (per the Logging section of `CLAUDE.md`, do not enable logging flags in anything release-bound).
7. **Unit tests** — `./gradlew test` passes: AuthMiddlewareTest, AuthManagerTest, SecretConfigStoreTest, SecretRedactorTest.

## Constraints

- Do NOT modify the daemon, surveillance, camera or BYD code to make a check pass. If a check fails, that is a real regression — file it.
- Do NOT change file permissions on the IPC token or secrets file.
- Clean up debug artifacts per `AGENTS.md`.

## Conventions for this refactor

- Dart lives under `flutter_ui/lib/` with `screens/<name>/` holding a pure-Dart `ChangeNotifier` controller, models, and the screen widget. Kotlin lives under `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/` with `package net.bladewatch.app.*`.
- Coverage gates: `flutter test --coverage` (Dart, `lib/gen` excluded) and `./gradlew koverVerify` (Kotlin). Both thresholds ratchet upward and may never be lowered.
- **No golden tests.** Visual parity is verified on the device against `screenshots/native/`.
- Verification happens on the head unit at <CAR_IP>:5555. Always pass `-s <CAR_IP>:5555` to every adb command.

## Tests (regression — required)

This task adds no features, so the bar is regression rather than TDD:

- `./gradlew test` passes with zero skipped tests.
- `cd flutter_ui && flutter test` passes with zero skipped tests.
- `flutter test --coverage` and `./gradlew koverVerify` both run, both figures recorded, **neither lower** than the previous recorded figure.
- If a test had to be deleted because the code under test was deleted, say which, and confirm the behaviour it covered either no longer exists or is now covered by a Dart test.
- Any bug found while verifying gets a **failing test written first**, then the fix — never a fix without a test that would have caught it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All three core daemons start on schedule after a clean reinstall.
- [ ] Recording and surveillance both produce valid output with the Flutter UI foregrounded.
- [ ] IPC token still 644, secrets file still 600.
- [ ] Zrok tunnel works and serves the unmodified Angular SPA.
- [ ] `./gradlew assembleRelease` and `./gradlew test` both pass.
- [ ] With this task and the other four Epic 3 tasks closed, write the explicit "parity confirmed, safe to delete native UI" verdict into the Epic 3 notes.
- [ ] `./gradlew test` and `flutter test` both pass with zero skipped tests.
- [ ] Dart and Kotlin coverage figures recorded, neither lower than the previous figure.
- [ ] Any bug found got a failing test written first, then the fix.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.

in this area -- the secret store path -- was a real defect fixed under its own issue, with the
