title: One-hour sustained-render soak on Live View and Vehicle
description:
## Context

Long-duration stability test. This is the task most likely to catch a fatal problem, and the one most likely to be skipped because everything "looks fine".

## Why

The BYD head unit's Adreno 610 GL driver **crashes only after several minutes of continuous rendering**. A native Filament port was integrated, appeared to work, and then had to be reverted for exactly this reason — see `docs/build-and-operations.md:58`, `docs/byd-integrations.md:160`, `docs/features.md:171`. The device is **Android 10 / API 29 with Vulkan 1.1** (measured), so Impeller most likely runs its **Vulkan** backend — a different driver path from the GL one that crashed Filament. Soak whichever backend `BladeWatch-7965.3` selected and pinned, and say which one in your notes: a soak result is meaningless without naming the backend it was measured on.

Epic 0 soaked a synthetic screen for 10 minutes. This soaks the two REAL sustained-render screens for an hour.

## Steps

Device <CAR_IP>:5555. Always pass `-s <CAR_IP>:5555`.

1. **Live View soak — at least 1 hour.** Continuous H.264 decode into the Flutter texture. Watch `adb logcat` throughout for GPU/driver faults, MediaCodec errors and OOM. Switch camera view modes periodically (All / Front / Right / Rear / Left) — the view-mode switch tears down and rebuilds the decoder, which is where a leak would show.
2. **Vehicle soak — at least 1 hour.** The three.js hero WebView renders continuously. This is the exact workload that killed Filament.
3. Monitor memory across the soak; a steadily climbing figure is a fail even without a crash.
4. Confirm the codec and WebSocket are actually released when leaving Live View — a leaked MediaCodec on this device is unrecoverable without restarting the daemon.

## Constraints

- Do NOT shorten the soak. The failure mode is time-dependent; a 5-minute check proves nothing.
- Run against a normal build with the daemons running, not an isolated test harness.
- Clean up device and dev-machine debug artifacts afterwards per `AGENTS.md`.

## Conventions for this refactor

- Dart lives under `flutter_ui/lib/` with `screens/<name>/` holding a pure-Dart `ChangeNotifier` controller, models, and the screen widget. Kotlin lives under `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/` with `package net.bladewatch.app.*`.
- Coverage gates: `flutter test --coverage` (Dart, `lib/gen` excluded) and `./gradlew koverVerify` (Kotlin). Both thresholds ratchet upward and may never be lowered.
- **No golden tests.** Visual parity is verified on the device against `screenshots/native/`.
- Verification happens on the head unit at <CAR_IP>:5555. Always pass `-s <CAR_IP>:5555` to every adb command.

## Tests (regression — required)

This task adds no features, so the bar is regression rather than TDD:

- `./gradlew test` passes with zero skipped tests.
- `cd flutter_ui && flutter test` passes with zero skipped tests.
- `flutter test --coverage` and `./gradlew koverVerify` both run, both figures recorded, **neither lower** than the previous recorded figure.
- If a test had to be deleted because the code under test was deleted, say which, and confirm the behaviour it covered either no longer exists or is now covered by a Dart test.
- Any bug found while verifying gets a **failing test written first**, then the fix — never a fix without a test that would have caught it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Live View soaked 60+ minutes with no GPU driver crash, no MediaCodec failure, no visible degradation.
- [ ] Vehicle hero soaked 60+ minutes with no crash.
- [ ] Memory flat, not climbing, across both soaks.
- [ ] Codec and WebSocket confirmed released on screen exit.
- [ ] Logcat output for both soaks summarised in the task notes, including any non-fatal warnings.
- [ ] `./gradlew test` and `flutter test` both pass with zero skipped tests.
- [ ] Dart and Kotlin coverage figures recorded, neither lower than the previous figure.
- [ ] Any bug found got a failing test written first, then the fix.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason:
CLOSED AT THE USER'S DIRECTION with the Live View soak stopped short of 60 minutes. Recording
what was actually measured rather than what the task asked for, so the record is not misleading.

BACKEND, which this task requires be named: Impeller **OpenGLES**. Flutter probed Vulkan first
and fell back:

    android_context_vk_impeller.cc(62)  Using the Impeller rendering backend (Vulkan).
    android_context_gl_impeller.cc(104) Using the Impeller rendering backend (OpenGLES).

That matters: GLES is the same driver path the reverted Filament port died on, so this soak was
measured on the risky backend, not the hoped-for one. NOTE the backend is NOT pinned in
flutter_ui/android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml -- the Phase 0 plan called for pinning the
selected backend so a Flutter upgrade cannot silently switch it, and nothing pins it today.
Filed separately.

WHAT WAS MEASURED

Live View -- 40 minutes of controlled measurement (09:20:36 to 10:01:11), on top of roughly
10 further minutes on the screen beforehand that were not under a clock.
  - 11 camera view-mode switches (All / Front / Right / Rear / Left), each tearing down and
    rebuilding the decoder -- the specific place a leak would show.
  - GPU driver faults: 0.  MediaCodec / OMX errors: 0.  FATAL EXCEPTION: 0.  ANR: 0.
  - PSS 385-468 MB across the run with no upward trend; it oscillated and returned.
  - No visible degradation: the 4-camera panoramic feed was still rendering correctly at the end
    (screenshot at 09:56).

Vehicle (three.js hero WebView) -- 28 minutes (08:42:46 to ~09:10), then the app moved to Live
View on its own and the Vehicle clock stopped. Over that window: 0 faults, PSS 391-414 MB flat,
Graphics flat at ~39.5 MB. The 3D car rendered correctly against the dark ground.

Codec / socket release on leaving Live View (this task's step 4) -- PASSES. Immediately after
navigating away, port 8080 showed:
    0 x ESTABLISHED, 22 x TIME_WAIT (draining), 1 x LISTEN
so the live-stream connection was released rather than leaked. A leaked MediaCodec on this
device is unrecoverable without restarting the daemon; the daemon stayed healthy.

Daemons were unaffected throughout: recording kept rolling the whole time (19 -> 36 segments
written today, 5-minute segments, 106 -> 110+ files on the SD card), and the Services pane
stayed at 3/4 running.

ONE THING I CANNOT EXPLAIN, recorded rather than smoothed over. The Graphics figure sat at
~77.5 MB for the first half of the Live soak and ~11 MB for the second half, with the feed
visibly rendering correctly in both. No fault or codec error accompanied the change and PSS did
not move with it, so it looks like an accounting/reallocation change rather than a loss of the
decode path -- but I did not chase it to a root cause.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, honestly marked:
  [ ] Live View soaked 60+ minutes -- NOT MET. 40 minutes measured, stopped at the user's
      direction. Everything observed in those 40 minutes was clean.
  [ ] Vehicle soaked 60+ minutes -- NOT MET. 28 minutes measured, also clean.
  [x] No GPU driver crash, no MediaCodec failure, no visible degradation in what WAS run.
  [x] Memory monitored across the soak; no steadily climbing figure.
  [x] Codec and WebSocket released when leaving Live View.
  [x] Run against a normal build with the daemons running, not an isolated harness.
  [x] gradlew test and flutter test pass with zero skipped; Dart coverage 99.97% (7126/7128),
      Kotlin koverVerify green at minBound(2). Neither lower.

WHY THE FULL HOUR STILL MATTERS, for whoever picks this up. The failure this task exists to
catch is time-dependent: the Filament port "appeared to work" and then crashed the Adreno 610
GL driver after several minutes of continuous rendering. 40 and 28 minutes are both well past
"several minutes", which is genuine evidence -- but the hour was chosen deliberately and neither
screen reached it. The Vehicle screen is the more valuable of the two to re-run, because its
sustained WebGL load is closer to the workload that actually killed Filament; Live View is
H.264 decode into a texture, a different path.

Follow-up filed for the remaining soak time and for pinning the backend.

title: Verify all 17 locales render correctly in the Flutter UI
description:
## Context

Verify all 17 locales render correctly in the Flutter UI. This project has shipped i18n breakage twice, so this gets its own gate.

## Prior failures worth knowing about

- Locale catalogs were served with a 24-hour cache under UNHASHED URLs, so after an app update the browser kept a stale catalog and the whole SPA rendered RAW KEYS.
- LLM edits introduced invalid JSON into `app/src/main/assets/web/i18n/de.json` and `app/src/main/assets/web/i18n/zh-CN.json` via typographic smart-quote delimiters (U+201C/U+201D) and unescaped quotes inside CJK values. Nothing validated it, so it shipped. The Gradle `validateI18nCatalogs` task was added because of this.
- A component-mounting test suite did NOT catch it, because mounting is not key resolution.

The ARB port in Epic 1 has the same exposure.

**Screen groups walked (8)**
- **Dashboard** — hero, chips and all five tiles match. The Vehicle tile difference is deliberate
  and documented (BladeWatch-p7vi): native's is permanently stuck on "Tap to set" because
  GetSohNominal is a removed-feature stub, Flutter shows the real model.
- **Trips** — exact parity. Same chips, all six summary metrics identical, same three trips with
  identical scores, same tab row.
- **Recordings + Video Player** — parity, and **HTTP-Range seeking verified**: tapping the
  timeline moved 0:37 -> 1:01 AND the video's burned-in timestamp advanced 11:52:46 -> 11:53:09,
  so the seek reached the daemon and returned real frames.
- **Location** — parity; found and fixed a doubled "© ©" attribution in both map screens.
- **Diagnostics** — found two unwired sources (BladeWatch-i2wv), both fixed. Storage tile
  difference resolved in Flutter's favour: native reads empty internal storage while the data
  lives on the SD card.
- **Vehicle** — **capability gating verified against native**, the highest-risk item on the list.
  Flutter defines three tabs and renders two because this car reports no seat capability; native
  withholds the same tab. Identical tyre/charge data, "Max Cooling" dimmed in both. Nothing was
  actuated.
- **Settings** — Appearance, Services and Privacy & data walked.
- **Dialogs** — 4 of 8: battery health, camera selection, reset data, language picker. Reset
  Data's destructive-action design is good and worth recording as a pass: red warning, nothing
  pre-checked, action disabled until a box is ticked.

## Bugs found here and FIXED

- Doubled `© ©` OSM attribution, both map screens.
- **BladeWatch-0kru** — toolbar pill hardcoded "Connecting…" on EVERY screen, where native hides
  it entirely with no tunnel.
- **BladeWatch-i2wv** — Diagnostics camera tile stuck on "Probing…"; Diagnostics tunnel line
  hardcoded offline. Fixed with a read/write split on the daemon's IPC allowlist rather than
  widening the write gate.
- **BladeWatch-8sig** — the destructive "Regenerate Token" led the safer "Set Password".
- **BladeWatch-1ovy** — Battery tile said "Not available" while Vehicle showed the charge.
- **BladeWatch-uuo6** — Reset Data offered to recalibrate a removed feature; Battery dialog
  blamed the car for a product-wide removal.

One filed in error and closed as such: **BladeWatch-cny7**. I called a dialog's text clipped from
a screenshot; it scrolls fine. A still shows one scroll offset, not the reachable content.

## NOT VERIFIED — what Phase 4 inherits

**1. The error-state row is unchecked on EVERY screen.** Every observation above was made with all
three daemons healthy. I could not hold a daemon-down state: killing `byd_cam_daemon` gets it
relaunched within ~30s by DaemonStartup's health check, and force-stopping the host app first did
not prevent it either. That is a good resilience result in its own right, but it means the
"daemon not running" / "Camera unavailable" paths are untested on device.
During the brief window the camera daemon WAS down, Live View kept showing a frame with no error
indication. Worth a closer look.
The controllers all take injected RPC clients and the suite already has 271 error-related
assertions across 45 screen test files, so the LOGIC is covered — the PRESENTATION is not.

**2. The Startup screen is not observable.** With healthy daemons the Flutter app completes
startup before its first frame renders; six rapid captures immediately after launch caught only
the splash. So the Startup screen and its "Continue anyway" escape hatch are unexercised. Same
root cause as (1): the supervisor will not let the daemons stay down.

**3. Three screen groups unwalked**
- Live View as a parity checklist (it was exercised heavily for RENDERING during BladeWatch-x3vw's
  soak, but never walked control-by-control against native)
- Settings: Recording, Status overlay and About panes
- Performance, and ADB Console (its unavailable state was separately closed as not-needed,
  BladeWatch-imh6.8)

**4. Four dialogs unwalked** — setup guide, update progress, vehicle capacity, zrok token. The
last two are low value now: zrok is slated for removal and update progress needs a real update in
flight.

**5. The 17-locale sweep was not redone** after this session's catalog changes. Russian was
checked directly; the other 16 rest on the gates.

## Gates at close

flutter analyze clean; 1403 Dart tests pass, zero skipped; Dart coverage 99.97% (7004/7006);
`./gradlew test koverVerify assembleDebug validateArbCatalogs validateAndroidStrings` all green.

Device left healthy: three daemons running, IPC token 644, secret store 600, recording rolling,
locale restored to auto, no test artefacts.

Nothing committed.

title: Capture Flutter screenshot set matching the 18-shot native baseline
description:
## Context

Capture the Flutter screenshot set that mirrors the existing native baseline, so parity can be reviewed side by side.

## The existing baseline

`screenshots/native/` already contains 18 shots, captured from the native UI:

01_startup, 03_live_view, 04b_recordings_surveillance, 05_vehicle, 05b_vehicle_windows, 06_trips, 06b_trips_stats, 06c_trips_storage, 07b_diagnostics_scrolled, 07c_diagnostics_adb_console, 07d_diagnostics_battery_health, 07e_diagnostics_performance, 08_settings, 08c_settings_surveillance, 08d_settings_daemons, 08e_settings_status_overlay, 09_language_selector, 10_about.

(`screenshots/web/` is the Angular SPA's own set — leave it alone.)


## Also capture here (deferred from the code phases)

- **Nav-rail side-by-side**, deferred from `BladeWatch-ncbb.4`: the native rail vs the Flutter rail, same theme, same drive side. Confirm colours, spacing, type and the **9th destination** (`railDestAbout`, below its hairline divider) all match.
- Each Phase 2 screen task recorded in its notes which `screenshots/native/` shot its screen corresponds to. Work from those notes so nothing is missed.

## Steps

1. On the head unit at <CAR_IP>:5555, open each corresponding Flutter screen in the same state as the native shot.
2. Capture with `adb -s <CAR_IP>:5555 exec-out screencap -p > screenshots/flutter/<same_name>.png`.
3. Also re-capture the NATIVE shots from the current build if any have drifted since they were taken — comparing against a stale baseline is worse than no baseline.
4. Review each pair side by side **at the head unit's real display density**, not scaled on a desktop. Record differences in the task notes: acceptable (font rendering, antialiasing) vs not (missing control, wrong spacing, wrong colour role).

## Constraints

- Do NOT sign off from an emulator or a scaled image.
- Per `AGENTS.md`, clean up afterwards: `adb -s <CAR_IP>:5555 shell rm -f /sdcard/*.png` and remove any pulled temp copies from the dev machine. Do NOT touch `/sdcard/BladeWatch/**` (real recordings/trips) or `/sdcard/Pictures/**` (user media).
- Screenshots committed under `screenshots/flutter/` are intentional parity artifacts — but do not commit anything yourself; leave them in the working tree.

## Conventions for this refactor

- Dart lives under `flutter_ui/lib/` with `screens/<name>/` holding a pure-Dart `ChangeNotifier` controller, models, and the screen widget. Kotlin lives under `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/` with `package net.bladewatch.app.*`.
- Coverage gates: `flutter test --coverage` (Dart, `lib/gen` excluded) and `./gradlew koverVerify` (Kotlin). Both thresholds ratchet upward and may never be lowered.
- **No golden tests.** Visual parity is verified on the device against `screenshots/native/`.
- Verification happens on the head unit at <CAR_IP>:5555. Always pass `-s <CAR_IP>:5555` to every adb command.

## Tests (regression — required)

This task adds no features, so the bar is regression rather than TDD:

- `./gradlew test` passes with zero skipped tests.
- `cd flutter_ui && flutter test` passes with zero skipped tests.
- `flutter test --coverage` and `./gradlew koverVerify` both run, both figures recorded, **neither lower** than the previous recorded figure.
- If a test had to be deleted because the code under test was deleted, say which, and confirm the behaviour it covered either no longer exists or is now covered by a Dart test.
- Any bug found while verifying gets a **failing test written first**, then the fix — never a fix without a test that would have caught it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `screenshots/flutter/` contains a file for each of the 18 baseline names.
- [ ] Each pair reviewed at real density, with differences recorded.
- [ ] Any "not acceptable" difference has a follow-up bd issue filed against the relevant Epic 2 task.
- [ ] Device and dev-machine temp screenshots cleaned up.
- [ ] `./gradlew test` and `flutter test` both pass with zero skipped tests.
- [ ] Dart and Kotlin coverage figures recorded, neither lower than the previous figure.
- [ ] Any bug found got a failing test written first, then the fix.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.

title: Port the 8 dialogs to Flutter
description:
> **CODE ONLY — do not touch the head unit in this task.**
> This project deliberately writes *all* Flutter code before any device work. Everything here
> is built and tested on the dev machine against the shared fakes from `BladeWatch-ncbb.5`,
> with no device and no daemon attached. On-device bring-up, screenshots, the render go/no-go
> and parity sign-off all live in **Phase 3** (`BladeWatch-imh6`).
> If you believe something genuinely cannot be verified without hardware, note it in the task
> notes for Phase 3 to pick up — do not reach for adb.

## Context

Port the 8 dialogs. They are easy to miss because each is reachable only from a specific row, and they are explicitly on the Epic 3 verification checklist.

## The 8 dialogs

| Layout | Notes |
|---|---|
| `app/src/main/res/layout/dialog_battery_health.xml` (18.7 KB) | opened from Diagnostics via `MainActivity.invokeBatteryHealthAction()`; uses `GetSohStatusRequest` / `ResetSohRequest` |
| `app/src/main/res/layout/dialog_camera_selection.xml` (8.6 KB) | `MainActivity.invokeReconfigureCameraAction()` |
| `app/src/main/res/layout/dialog_language_picker.xml` + `app/src/main/res/layout/item_language_row.xml` | `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/dialog/LanguagePickerDialog.kt`; must switch the Flutter locale and persist it |
| `app/src/main/res/layout/dialog_reset_data.xml` (9.6 KB) | `MainActivity.invokeResetDataDialog()`; destructive — keep every confirmation step |
| `app/src/main/res/layout/dialog_setup_guide.xml` (12.7 KB) | first-run guide; `MainActivity` gates it with a `setupGuideShown` flag — reproduce that gate |
| `app/src/main/res/layout/dialog_update_progress.xml` | `updater/UpdateDialog`, via the `update.*` channel |
| `app/src/main/res/layout/dialog_vehicle_capacity.xml` (5.4 KB) | vehicle battery capacity entry |
| `app/src/main/res/layout/dialog_zrok_token.xml` | tunnel token entry — see the secret constraint below |

There are 8 files in `ui/` using `MaterialAlertDialogBuilder` / `BottomSheetDialog` / `DialogFragment`; grep for them to find every caller.

## Secret handling — Zrok token dialog

The Zrok token is a secret stored in `/data/local/tmp/bladewatch_secrets.json` (mode 600, shell-only). The app cannot write it directly as app UID — it goes through the TCP command bridge so the daemon (shell UID) writes it. Use the existing `config.*` channel path; do NOT read or write the secrets file from Dart, and never log the value. See `docs/ipc-auth-and-secrets.md` and the Security Notes in `CLAUDE.md`.

## Notes

- The language picker must drive the ARB locale and survive a restart.
- The reset-data dialog is destructive: reproduce every confirmation step exactly. Do not make it easier to trigger.

Baseline screenshot: `screenshots/native/09_language_selector.png`

## How every screen task works

1. Read the native fragment AND its controller/client/models files FULLY before writing any Dart. The controllers hold the real behaviour; the fragment is often just wiring.
2. Port the layout to Dart widgets using the shared M3 ThemeData built in Epic 1. Do not invent new styling.
3. Call the SAME RPCs via the generated Dart client, or the SAME platform-channel methods. Never add a new endpoint or a new channel method without saying why in the notes.
4. All user-facing text comes from the ARB catalogs. No hardcoded literals except the brand name BladeWatch.
5. Do **not** capture screenshots here — `BladeWatch-imh6.1` captures the whole set on the device in Phase 3. Note in your task notes which `screenshots/native/` shot this screen corresponds to, so Phase 3 knows what to reproduce.

## Universal constraints

- Do NOT delete or modify the native fragment, layout, adapter or view you are porting FROM. Both UIs must keep working — the native shell stays the default until Epic 4.
- Do NOT modify anything under `web/` (the Angular SPA), the daemon, the Connect server, or the `.proto` files.
- Do NOT commit. Leave changes in the working tree.
- **No device.** Do not run adb, do not install anything, do not capture screenshots. Build and test locally: `cd flutter_ui && flutter analyze && flutter test`. Phase 3 (`BladeWatch-imh6`) does all on-device work.
- Use the shared RPC fake and channel fake from `BladeWatch-ncbb.5`; tests must pass with no device and no daemon attached.

## Conventions for this refactor (decided — do not deviate)

**Where Dart code goes.** Mirror the native structure one-to-one, so each port is a translation rather than a redesign:

The Flutter UI is a **separate APK** (`net.bladewatch.flutter`) sharing a UID with `net.bladewatch.app`. Its Kotlin lives in `flutter_ui/android/app/src/main/kotlin/`; the main app's Kotlin is never called directly from Dart.

```
flutter_ui/lib/
  gen/                  generated protobuf — never hand-edited, excluded from coverage
  rpc/                  Connect transport + the 12 typed service clients
  platform/             Dart wrappers over the platform channels
  l10n/                 ARB catalogs
  theme/                ThemeData built from the Android M3 tokens
  shell/                nav rail, toolbar, routing
  screens/<name>/       <name>_controller.dart, <name>_models.dart, <name>_screen.dart
flutter_ui/test/        mirrors lib/ exactly
```

**State management: plain `ChangeNotifier` controllers. No Riverpod, no BLoC, no new state dependency.**
This mirrors the existing native Controller pattern (`app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/vehicle/VehicleController.kt`, `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/trips/TripsController.kt`, `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/surveillance/SurveillanceSettingsController.kt`), so porting is a direct translation.

- The controller is a **pure Dart class: it must not import `package:flutter/material.dart`.** It holds state, calls the RPC client and the platform channels, and calls `notifyListeners()`.
- The screen widget only renders controller state and forwards user intent. **No business logic in widgets.**
- This split is exactly what makes 100% coverage reachable — controllers are tested directly with no widget pump.

**No golden tests.** Visual parity is verified on the device in Phase 3 against `screenshots/native/`. Do not add `matchesGoldenFile` or `golden_toolkit`; they churn on every theme tweak and differ between host machines.

## Tests (TDD — required)

**Write the failing test first**, then the implementation, then refactor. Tests are not a closing chore — the test defines the behaviour.

- **Controller and model logic: 100% line and branch coverage.** These are pure Dart with no Flutter imports, so there is no excuse for a gap: every RPC-response-to-view-model transform, every formatter, every validation, every error branch.
- **Widget tests for every state the screen can reach**: loading, loaded, empty, error (including the "daemon not running" case), plus each interactive control. Assert on *behaviour* — that the right call was made with the right arguments — not merely that a widget rendered.
- Use the shared RPC fake and channel fake from `BladeWatch-ncbb.5`. Do not write your own.
- Tests must run green with `flutter test` on the dev machine with **no device and no daemon attached**.
- Run `flutter test --coverage`; `flutter_ui/lib/gen` is excluded from the denominator. Record the percentage in the task notes; it must not be lower than the previous task's figure.
- Anything uncovered is listed line-by-line in the notes with a concrete reason. **"Hard to test" is not a reason** — it means the logic belongs somewhere testable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every control, tab, menu and dialog present in the native screen exists and is wired in the Flutter screen.
- [ ] Loading, empty and error states match — including the "daemon not running" case.
- [ ] Renders correctly in light and dark theme.
- [ ] No hardcoded user-facing strings; all keys resolve in at least en plus one CJK locale.
- [ ] `flutter analyze` clean; `./gradlew assembleDebug` succeeds; the native UI still works unchanged.
- [ ] Tests were written before the implementation, not retrofitted.
- [ ] `flutter test` passes with zero skipped tests.
- [ ] 100% line and branch coverage of controllers and models, or every gap justified line-by-line in the notes.
- [ ] Every reachable screen state (loading / loaded / empty / error) has a widget test.
- [ ] Tests run green with no device and no daemon attached.
- [ ] `flutter test --coverage` percentage recorded and not lower than the previous task's.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason:
## Summary

Ported the 8 dialogs the task lists. Before writing anything, checked each dialog's actual current state in the Flutter port rather than assuming the task's own list was accurate (a pattern this whole session has repeatedly needed) — 4 turned out to already be built by earlier tasks (yz1e.2/yz1e.4), leaving 4 genuinely new plus one enrichment.

## Already built — verified, one enriched

- **Camera Selection** (`diagnostics_screen.dart`) — already complete, matches `MainActivity.onReconfigureCameraClicked()`.
- **Vehicle Capacity** (`dashboard_screen.dart` / `vehicle_dialog_controller.dart`) — already complete, matches `DashboardFragment.showVehicleCapacityDialog()` exactly (RPC sequence, 8.0-120.0 kWh validation bound, the "Reset = SetSohNominal() not ResetSoh()" distinction).
- **Zrok Token** (`settings_daemons_screen.dart` / `settings_daemons_controller.dart`) — already complete, with an already-documented, policy-consistent simplification for `disableEnvironment()` (native's shell-based environment-file cleanup is out of scope per this project's own "Epic 1 IPC-only rule" for daemon process control, tracked separately by BladeWatch-abcx).
- **Battery Health** (`diagnostics_screen.dart` / `diagnostics_controller.dart`) — was built but showed only the SOH percent. Enriched with Source/Method/Capacity rows and the 4-way status text, backed by `GetSohStatus` fields (`nominalCapacityKwh`/`nominalSource`/`displaySource`) the controller was already fetching but not exposing. Model/pack-capacity/estimated-capacity/calibration-anchor remain out of scope — those are file-only in native (`/data/local/tmp/abrp_soh_estimate.properties`), unavailable here for the same reason already documented on `resetBattery()`.

## Newly built

**Reset Data** (`settings_privacy_screen.dart`) — 3-dialog flow (checklist → "reset the following?" confirmation → result) calling `SystemService.ResetPerformance`, matching `MainActivity.kt`'s exact category-id strings and RPC. Removed the `onResetData: VoidCallback` indirection threaded from `main.dart` (a bare callback can't carry the `BuildContext` a dialog needs) — `SettingsPrivacyScreen` now takes `SystemServiceClient` directly and shows its own dialog, matching every other in-screen dialog this session.

**Language Picker** (`shell/locale_controller.dart` + `screens/dialogs/language_picker_sheet.dart`) — genuinely new app-wide infrastructure; `MaterialApp` had no `locale:` override at all before this. Key decisions, each verified against source rather than assumed:
- Persists to `/data/local/tmp/.bladewatch/locale` via direct `dart:io` file I/O, not a platform channel — `LocaleManager.java`'s own doc comment and its `setReadable(true, false)` calls confirm this file is deliberately cross-UID-readable (both APKs share `android:sharedUserId="net.bladewatch.app"`, confirmed in both manifests), unlike the SOH properties file or `UnifiedConfigManager`'s JSON, which carry no such guarantee and remain treated as unavailable.
- The 17-language list (`kSupportedLocaleTags`) is hardcoded to match `LocaleManager.SUPPORTED` exactly — deliberately narrower than `AppLocalizations.supportedLocales` (19 entries; Flutter's own l10n tool adds bare `pt`/`zh` fallbacks native never treats as selectable languages).
- Native-script names (`kLocaleNativeNames`) are a hardcoded Dart map, not ARB — a language's name in its own script doesn't change with the picker's current display language, matching native's own hardcoded map.
- `FileLocaleStore` is covered by a real-file integration test (temp path), not excluded from the coverage gate.

**Setup Guide** (`screens/dialogs/setup_guide_controller.dart` + `setup_guide_dialog.dart`) — 3 steps (Language, Auto-start, Overlay) behind a version-change re-show gate.
- New `setup.*` platform channel (Dart: `platform/setup_channel.dart`; Kotlin: 2 new functions in `MainActivity.kt`) — the first channel in this app that launches an Android `Intent`. `openAutoStartSettings()` ports native's exact 4-level BYD-autostart fallback cascade verbatim. `openOverlaySettings()` targets **`net.bladewatch.app`'s package**, not this Flutter APK's own — the Flutter APK declares no `SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW` (confirmed by grepping both manifests) and has no overlay-service equivalent; the main app does. Both fire-and-forget, matching native's own swallow-and-give-up ending. `MainActivity.kt` is already wholesale-excluded from the Kover gate — these functions add no new exclusion.
- Two of native's 3 step checkmarks are intentionally never shown, matching (not "fixing") what native's own code actually does: Language's is hardcoded always-visible; Auto-start's is dead code in native (defaults invisible, never set visible anywhere in `SetupGuideDialog.java`); Overlay's native equivalent checks its *own* package's permission, which doesn't apply once this port targets the main app's package instead — querying another package's overlay grant needs `AppOpsManager` reflection unverifiable without a device, left for BladeWatch-imh6.
- "Seen" marker persists via the existing `PrefsChannel` (2 new per-key methods, matching its established pattern), keyed by build number rather than `PackageInfo.lastUpdateTime` (native's own signal) since `package_info_plus` has no install-timestamp equivalent — the same "did the installed build change" signal, measured differently.
- `showSetupGuideDialog`'s version banner is caller-supplied, not computed internally — mirrors native's own two real call sites: `showIfNeeded()`'s real `isUpdate` verdict for auto-show, hardcoded `false` for the force-show "show setup guide again" row (native never shows a stale banner there regardless of what actually changed).

## Two real bugs found by the full-app smoke test, not by inspection

1. **Context-capture bug (Language Picker).** `onLanguageTap`/`onOpenLanguagePicker` closures built in `_BladeWatchAppState.build(BuildContext context)` captured that outer context — which sits *above* `MaterialApp` itself (it's the context this widget's own parent gave it), with no `Localizations`/`Navigator` ancestor. The smoke test hit "No MaterialLocalizations found" on the very first language-button tap. Fixed by wrapping `MaterialApp.home` in a `Builder` and using that `Builder`'s context for every main.dart-shown dialog/sheet.
2. **Unguarded platform-channel call in a post-frame callback (Setup Guide).** `SetupGuideController.checkIfNeeded()` had no try/catch. Triggered from `main.dart`'s auto-show-on-launch path (a post-frame callback, not a direct user gesture) before any channel handler is registered, the awaited `Future` never resolved rather than throwing promptly — a different failure shape from BladeWatch-yz1e.10's `createTexture()` bug (immediate throw) but the same lesson: code with no direct caller to hand a failure to needs to handle its own. Fixed by treating any failure as "nothing to show" (the safe default for an onboarding dialog). `BladeWatchApp` gained an injectable `setupGuideController` (matching `dashboardController`/`tripsController`'s shape) so the smoke test could inject a fake-backed one and exercise the auto-show dialog end to end, not just its early-return path.

## Tests / coverage

- `flutter analyze`: clean.
- `flutter test`: 1263 tests, 0 failures, 0 skipped.
- Dart coverage: **99.97% (6547/6549 lines, 99.9695% unrounded)** — up from BladeWatch-yz1e.10's 99.9679% (6226/6228). Every new/changed file reached 100%. The only 2 permanently-uncovered lines remain `main.dart`'s literal `void main()`.
- Kotlin (Flutter APK): 100%, unchanged — the 2 new `setup.*` functions live in `MainActivity.kt`, already wholesale-excluded. `./gradlew :app:test :app:koverVerify :app:assembleDebug` — exit 0.
- Main app (`app/`): untouched by this task (confirmed via `git status` — the same pre-existing unrelated diff set noted by every prior yz1e task, none of it touched here); `./gradlew :app:assembleDebug` still succeeds (verified in background earlier this session, unrelated to this task's changes).
- Every native dialog source file, layout XML, `.proto`, and `web/` confirmed untouched via `git status`.

No hardcoded user-facing strings — every ARB key used already existed from the Epic 1 bulk import (verified present in en, plus spot-checked ja/ko/zh); `flutter gen-l10n` reports 0 untranslated. No new ARB keys were needed this task.

No daemon, WebSocket protocol, `.proto`, or `web/` changes. No device work performed (no adb, no install, no screenshots) — on-device bring-up and verifying the Auto-start/Overlay intents actually resolve correctly is BladeWatch-imh6's job.

title: Port Live View with a Flutter H.264 texture plugin
description:
> **CODE ONLY — do not touch the head unit in this task.**
> This project deliberately writes *all* Flutter code before any device work. Everything here
> is built and tested on the dev machine against the shared fakes from `BladeWatch-ncbb.5`,
> with no device and no daemon attached. On-device bring-up, screenshots, the render go/no-go
> and parity sign-off all live in **Phase 3** (`BladeWatch-imh6`).
> If you believe something genuinely cannot be verified without hardware, note it in the task
> notes for Phase 3 to pick up — do not reach for adb.

## Context

Port Live View. **This is the one screen that keeps Kotlin**, by explicit decision.

## Why it is the exception

The feed is raw H.264 Annex-B arriving over a WebSocket and decoded by `MediaCodec` into a `Surface`. Dart has no hardware video decode, and a software H.264 decoder cannot hold frame rate on an Adreno 610 head unit. (For reference, the Angular SPA uses a JS software decoder, `web/dist/vendor/SotaPlayer.js` — acceptable for a remote browser, not for the in-car screen.)

## Approach

Build a small Flutter **texture plugin**, not a platform view: register a `TextureRegistry.SurfaceTextureEntry` in Kotlin, hand its `Surface` to the existing decode logic, and render `Texture(id)` in Dart. A texture composites inside the Flutter scene with no platform-view jank.

## Native source

- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/LiveViewFragment.kt` (39 — thin)
- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/liveview/LiveViewController.kt` (200)
- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/liveview/LiveStreamClient.kt` (350) — **port this logic into the plugin**
- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/liveview/LiveViewModels.kt`

`LiveStreamClient` already does exactly what is needed: `setPreviewSurface(Surface)`, WebSocket connect with handshake key, fragmented-message reassembly (the server splits large messages), codec-config vs frame flag handling, `MediaCodec.createDecoderByType("video/avc")`, and `drainDecoder`. Reuse it; the only change is where the Surface comes from.

## Dart side

- The camera selector: All / Front / Right / Rear / Left, mapping to `StreamService.SetViewMode` with viewMode 0=Mosaic/All, 1=Front, 2=Right, 3=Rear, 4=Left (5=Raw exists in the proto — check whether the native UI exposes it before adding it).
- Connect/disconnect state with a retry affordance.
- `StreamService` also has Enable, Disable, GetStatus, GetQuality, SetQuality, GetViewMode — check `LiveViewController` for which the screen uses.

## Constraints

- Do NOT change the daemon-side streaming server or the WebSocket protocol.
- Do NOT modify the native `LiveViewFragment` — copy the logic into the plugin, leave the original in place until Epic 4.
- Release the codec and close the socket when the screen is not visible. A leaked MediaCodec on this device is unrecoverable without restarting the daemon.

Baseline screenshot: `screenshots/native/03_live_view.png`

## How every screen task works

1. Read the native fragment AND its controller/client/models files FULLY before writing any Dart. The controllers hold the real behaviour; the fragment is often just wiring.
2. Port the layout to Dart widgets using the shared M3 ThemeData built in Epic 1. Do not invent new styling.
3. Call the SAME RPCs via the generated Dart client, or the SAME platform-channel methods. Never add a new endpoint or a new channel method without saying why in the notes.
4. All user-facing text comes from the ARB catalogs. No hardcoded literals except the brand name BladeWatch.
5. Do **not** capture screenshots here — `BladeWatch-imh6.1` captures the whole set on the device in Phase 3. Note in your task notes which `screenshots/native/` shot this screen corresponds to, so Phase 3 knows what to reproduce.

## Universal constraints

- Do NOT delete or modify the native fragment, layout, adapter or view you are porting FROM. Both UIs must keep working — the native shell stays the default until Epic 4.
- Do NOT modify anything under `web/` (the Angular SPA), the daemon, the Connect server, or the `.proto` files.
- Do NOT commit. Leave changes in the working tree.
- **No device.** Do not run adb, do not install anything, do not capture screenshots. Build and test locally: `cd flutter_ui && flutter analyze && flutter test`. Phase 3 (`BladeWatch-imh6`) does all on-device work.
- Use the shared RPC fake and channel fake from `BladeWatch-ncbb.5`; tests must pass with no device and no daemon attached.

## Conventions for this refactor (decided — do not deviate)

**Where Dart code goes.** Mirror the native structure one-to-one, so each port is a translation rather than a redesign:

The Flutter UI is a **separate APK** (`net.bladewatch.flutter`) sharing a UID with `net.bladewatch.app`. Its Kotlin lives in `flutter_ui/android/app/src/main/kotlin/`; the main app's Kotlin is never called directly from Dart.

```
flutter_ui/lib/
  gen/                  generated protobuf — never hand-edited, excluded from coverage
  rpc/                  Connect transport + the 12 typed service clients
  platform/             Dart wrappers over the platform channels
  l10n/                 ARB catalogs
  theme/                ThemeData built from the Android M3 tokens
  shell/                nav rail, toolbar, routing
  screens/<name>/       <name>_controller.dart, <name>_models.dart, <name>_screen.dart
flutter_ui/test/        mirrors lib/ exactly
```

**State management: plain `ChangeNotifier` controllers. No Riverpod, no BLoC, no new state dependency.**
This mirrors the existing native Controller pattern (`app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/vehicle/VehicleController.kt`, `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/trips/TripsController.kt`, `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/surveillance/SurveillanceSettingsController.kt`), so porting is a direct translation.

- The controller is a **pure Dart class: it must not import `package:flutter/material.dart`.** It holds state, calls the RPC client and the platform channels, and calls `notifyListeners()`.
- The screen widget only renders controller state and forwards user intent. **No business logic in widgets.**
- This split is exactly what makes 100% coverage reachable — controllers are tested directly with no widget pump.

**No golden tests.** Visual parity is verified on the device in Phase 3 against `screenshots/native/`. Do not add `matchesGoldenFile` or `golden_toolkit`; they churn on every theme tweak and differ between host machines.

## Tests (TDD — required)

**Write the failing test first**, then the implementation, then refactor. Tests are not a closing chore — the test defines the behaviour.

- **Controller and model logic: 100% line and branch coverage.** These are pure Dart with no Flutter imports, so there is no excuse for a gap: every RPC-response-to-view-model transform, every formatter, every validation, every error branch.
- **Widget tests for every state the screen can reach**: loading, loaded, empty, error (including the "daemon not running" case), plus each interactive control. Assert on *behaviour* — that the right call was made with the right arguments — not merely that a widget rendered.
- Use the shared RPC fake and channel fake from `BladeWatch-ncbb.5`. Do not write your own.
- Tests must run green with `flutter test` on the dev machine with **no device and no daemon attached**.
- Run `flutter test --coverage`; `flutter_ui/lib/gen` is excluded from the denominator. Record the percentage in the task notes; it must not be lower than the previous task's figure.
- Anything uncovered is listed line-by-line in the notes with a concrete reason. **"Hard to test" is not a reason** — it means the logic belongs somewhere testable.

### Kotlin side (the texture plugin)

**Write the failing test first**, then the implementation, then refactor.

- JVM unit tests go in `app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/`. The existing suite is ~20 files / ~3,100 LOC — read the closest neighbours first: `app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/connect/ConnectWireParityTest.java` (proto/JSON wire parity), `app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/auth/AuthManagerTest.java`, `app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/AuthMiddlewareTest.java`, `app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/IpcRoundTripTest.java`, `app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/IpcTokenManagerTest.java`, `app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/logging/SecretRedactorTest.java`, and the `vehicle/` suite (`app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/vehicle/VehicleClientMapTest.kt`, `app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/vehicle/VehicleFormattersTest.kt`, `app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/vehicle/TyreTierTest.kt`, `app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/vehicle/VehicleI18nParityTest.kt`). **CLAUDE.md's Testing section lists only four of these and is stale — trust the filesystem.**
- **100% coverage of every method you add, including every error path.** On this head unit the real failures are: the shell call fails, the daemon is not up yet, permission denied, the IPC token is unreadable. Each needs a test proving the right error reaches the caller rather than being swallowed.
- Test argument marshalling in **both** directions. A dropped or mistyped field across a platform channel produces a bug that only appears on the car.
- **Never put a real secret in a fixture.** Use obviously-fake values; `SecretRedactorTest` is the reference for this.
- Android's `org.json` is a stub in JVM unit tests — that is why `org.json:json:20240303` is a `testImplementation`. `protobuf-java-util` is available for proto/JSON assertions.
- Run `./gradlew test koverVerify` and record the percentage in the notes; it must not drop.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every control, tab, menu and dialog present in the native screen exists and is wired in the Flutter screen.
- [ ] Loading, empty and error states match — including the "daemon not running" case.
- [ ] Renders correctly in light and dark theme.
- [ ] No hardcoded user-facing strings; all keys resolve in at least en plus one CJK locale.
- [ ] `flutter analyze` clean; `./gradlew assembleDebug` succeeds; the native UI still works unchanged.
- [ ] Tests were written before the implementation, not retrofitted.
- [ ] `flutter test` passes with zero skipped tests.
- [ ] 100% line and branch coverage of controllers and models, or every gap justified line-by-line in the notes.
- [ ] Every reachable screen state (loading / loaded / empty / error) has a widget test.
- [ ] Tests run green with no device and no daemon attached.
- [ ] `flutter test --coverage` percentage recorded and not lower than the previous task's.
- [ ] `./gradlew test` passes with zero skipped tests.
- [ ] 100% coverage of every new method including every error path, or each gap justified in the notes.
- [ ] Both marshalling directions tested for every channel method.
- [ ] No real secret value appears in any fixture.
- [ ] `./gradlew koverVerify` passes and the percentage is recorded in the notes.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.

## Summary

Ported Live View to Flutter as a texture plugin, per the task's explicit "this is the one screen that keeps Kotlin" design. Read all native source in full before writing anything: `LiveViewFragment.kt` (39 LOC), `LiveViewModels.kt` (32), `LiveViewController.kt` (200), `LiveStreamClient.kt` (350), `stream.proto` (7 RPCs), and grepped `CameraDaemon.java` for `HTTP_PORT`.

Baseline screenshot for Phase 3: `screenshots/native/03_live_view.png`.

## Architecture decision (documented in full in docs/build-and-operations.md)

Dart owns the WebSocket connection and the 3 `StreamService` RPCs the screen actually calls (Enable/SetViewMode/GetQuality — of 7 total; Disable/GetStatus/SetQuality/GetViewMode have no call site in this screen either, native or here). Kotlin owns only `MediaCodec` decode into a Flutter `Texture`. This diverges from the task's "port LiveStreamClient wholesale, just swap the Surface" framing for two reasons, not one preference:

1. **Unavoidable regardless of preference**: `LiveStreamClient.kt`'s RPC calls and JWT minting go through the main app's `ConnectClientProvider`/`AuthManager` singletons, which the separate Flutter APK (net.bladewatch.flutter vs net.bladewatch.app — different classloaders, shared UID only) cannot reach at all.
2. **A genuine choice**: the WebSocket handshake/frame-reassembly itself *could* have been ported to new native networking code instead of using `dart:io`'s `WebSocket`. It was not, because `dart:io`'s WebSocket is RFC 6455 compliant and already proven against this exact server (the Angular SPA's own standard browser WebSocket client). This keeps the new native surface to exactly the one thing Dart cannot do (hardware H.264 decode) — the smallest surface for the task's own "a leaked MediaCodec is unrecoverable" warning to apply to.

Corrections made along the way, all verified against source rather than assumed:
- `stream.proto`'s own comment claims port 8887; `CameraDaemon.HTTP_PORT = 8080` is the real port (same port as HTTP/ConnectRPC). The client connects to `ws://127.0.0.1:8080/ws`.
- Only 5 directions exist (Mosaic/Front/Right/Rear/Left) — `stream.proto`'s `ViewMode` has a 6th value (`VIEW_MODE_RAW`), but `LiveViewModels.kt`'s own `LiveViewDirection` enum never exposes it. Not added here either.

## Kotlin (flutter_ui/android/app/src/main/kotlin/net/bladewatch/bladewatch_ui/liveview/)

- `FrameDecoder` (interface) / `MediaCodecFrameDecoder` (real implementation, mirrors `LiveStreamClient.kt`'s `feedToDecoder`/`drainDecoder` exactly) / `LiveViewTexturePlugin` (testable orchestration: texture lifecycle, frame-vs-codec-config bookkeeping, PTS = `frameCounter++ * 66_667L` matching native exactly).
- Split so every line of decision logic is JVM-testable: `MediaCodecFrameDecoder` is the only class touching real `android.media.MediaCodec`/`android.view.Surface` (throws "not mocked" in a plain JVM test); `LiveViewTexturePlugin` never touches those, only the injected `FrameDecoder` and Flutter's own plain-JVM-interface `TextureRegistry`/`SurfaceProducer`/`TextureEntry`.
- `MainActivity.kt`: registers a **new, separate** `MethodChannel` (`net.bladewatch.flutter/live_view_texture`) on its own `BinaryMessenger.makeBackgroundTaskQueue()` — not the shared `net.bladewatch.flutter/privileged` channel — because `MediaCodec.dequeueInputBuffer`'s bounded wait, called once per frame, must not block the platform/UI thread the way the shared channel's synchronous handlers do for everything else. Added `Map<*,*>.long(key)` handling both `Int` and `Long` (the standard method codec sends whichever fits), defending against the exact platform-channel marshalling gotcha the task's own notes warn about.
- Tests: `LiveViewTexturePluginTest.kt`, 17 tests, hand-rolled fakes (no Mockito, matching the established `DaemonControlTest.kt` convention), including both directions of every channel method.
- Verified: `./gradlew :app:compileDebugKotlin` (clean against the real bundled Flutter embedding classes, extracted+javap-disassembled from the actual `flutter_embedding_debug-*.jar` to confirm the exact `TextureRegistry`/`SurfaceProducer`/`MethodChannel`/`BinaryMessenger`/`FlutterRenderer` API shapes rather than relying on memory), then `./gradlew :app:test :app:koverVerify :app:assembleDebug` — exit 0.
- Kover: **100%** for `LiveViewTexturePlugin`/`FrameDecoder`. One new named exclusion: `net.bladewatch.bladewatch_ui.liveview.MediaCodecFrameDecoder` (real MediaCodec/Surface calls, same class of exclusion as the gate's existing `LocationServiceChannel*`/`HttpConnectionsKt` entries). `minBound(100)` unchanged and still passes.

## Dart (flutter_ui/lib/)

- `screens/live_view/live_view_models.dart` — `LiveViewDirection` (5 values), `LiveStreamPhase`, `LiveStreamStatus`, `LiveViewState`.
- `platform/live_view_texture_channel.dart` — thin wrapper over the new channel group (`createTexture`/`configure`/`feedFrame`/`dispose`).
- `screens/live_view/live_view_controller.dart` — `LiveSocket`/`IoLiveSocket`/`connectIoLiveSocket` (the real `dart:io` WebSocket wrapper) + the full `LiveViewController extends ChangeNotifier` (connect-retry loop with a 20-attempt/2s-delay budget mirroring native, direction selection, mid-stream disconnect handling).
- `screens/live_view/live_view_screen.dart` — full-bleed `Texture` + status banner + 5-button direction bar.
- Two real bugs found and fixed via testing, not by construction:
  1. `LiveViewController.start()`'s texture-creation call had no try/catch (every RPC/socket step inside the retry loop did). Visiting the route in the full-app smoke test with no native handler registered surfaced an unhandled Future exception. Fixed: caught and published as `LiveStreamStatus.unavailable('Camera starting — tap retry')`, the same message an exhausted connect budget already uses.
  2. `LiveViewController` could call `notifyListeners()` after being disposed: `LiveViewScreen.dispose()` calls `stop()` fire-and-forget (required — `dispose()` is synchronous), and `stop()`'s async chain can still be suspended when the *whole app* tears down and calls `_liveViewController.dispose()` in the same pass — exactly what happens between the two `testWidgets` blocks in `test/widget_test.dart`. Fixed with a `_disposed` flag checked in `_publish()`.
- A UX improvement, not a functional change to daemon behavior: a mid-stream disconnect now shows the same Error+retry state a failed initial connect already gets. Native's read loop just `break`s silently, leaving a frozen frame with no recovery short of leaving the screen (confirmed by reading `LiveStreamClient.kt`'s frame loop directly).
- Styling: an initial draft used theme-derived rounded containers for the banner/direction bar. Checked directly against `LiveViewController.kt`'s `buildView()` and corrected — native builds a `BladeTheme` there but never references it; every color is a literal ARGB value and every container is a flat rectangle (no corner radius). Now matches exactly: `Color(0xCC000000)` banner, `Color(0xCC101010)` direction bar, `Color(0xEDEFEFEF)`/`Color(0xFF151515)` selected button, no border radius anywhere.

## ARB / i18n

5 new keys: `live_direction_all/front/right/rear/left`. Not a reuse of Surveillance's `surveillance_advanced_camera_front/right/rear/left` (grammatically adjectives for "which cameras feed the pipeline", no "all" concept) or Vehicle (which has no camera-direction strings at all, once actually checked — the resemblance I initially expected wasn't there). Live View's labels are a *view selector*, a different enough role to warrant fresh keys per this project's ARB discipline. Front/Right/Rear/Left's translated values were copied verbatim from Surveillance's already-reviewed strings for terminology consistency within each locale; "All" was translated fresh into all 18 non-English locales. `flutter gen-l10n` reports 0 untranslated across all locales.

The 4 other keys this screen needed (`live_retry`/`live_connecting`/`live_error_fmt`/`live_camera_unavailable_fmt`) already existed from the Epic 1 bulk import.

## Tests / coverage

- `flutter analyze`: clean.
- `flutter test`: 1197 tests, 0 failures, 0 skipped.
- Dart coverage: **99.97% (6226/6228 lines, 99.9679% unrounded)** — up from BladeWatch-yz1e.9's 99.9670% (6056/6058). `live_view_controller.dart`, `live_view_models.dart`, `live_view_screen.dart`, `live_view_texture_channel.dart` all at 100%. `IoLiveSocket`/`connectIoLiveSocket` needed no coverage-gate exclusion at all — `test/screens/live_view/io_live_socket_test.dart` covers them with a real local `HttpServer`+`WebSocketTransformer.upgrade` round trip, the same approach `raw_http_sender_test.dart` already uses (checked directly: that file is 100%-covered this way, not exempted — the "thin real-I/O wrapper" precedent I initially assumed meant "accepted gap" actually means "tested against a real local server"). The only 2 permanently-uncovered lines are `main.dart`'s literal `void main()`, unrelated to this task and present in every prior coverage snapshot too.
- Kotlin (Flutter APK) coverage: 100% for new code, `MediaCodecFrameDecoder` newly excluded (see above). `./gradlew :app:test :app:koverVerify :app:assembleDebug` — exit 0.
- Main app (`app/`): untouched by this task (confirmed via `git status` — zero diff on any native Live View/proto/daemon/web file); `./gradlew :app:assembleDebug` still succeeds (verified).

## Wiring

- `shell/app_shell.dart`: added `liveViewScreen` slot for the pre-existing `BwRoutes.liveView` route constant (already scaffolded by the Epic 2 route-stub task).
- `main.dart`: `StreamServiceClient` (shared `_rpcTransport`), a **separate** `LiveViewTextureChannel` backed by its own `MethodChannelBridge(MethodChannel('net.bladewatch.flutter/live_view_texture'))`, `LiveViewController` (using the shared `_authChannel` as its `JwtSource`), disposed alongside every other controller.
- `test/shell/app_shell_test.dart`: added the liveView slot test.
- `test/widget_test.dart`: Live View **is** visited in the full-app smoke test (unlike Vehicle, which is skipped for an unrelated, unfixable reason — constructing a real `WebViewController` throws with no platform implementation registered). Live View is safe to visit unfaked because texture creation fails immediately with no handler registered, and (after the fix above) that's now caught and turned into an ordinary `unavailable` state — this is exactly the test that caught both real bugs described above.

## Deviations from the task's literal framing (both explained above, both necessary)

## Context

## Native source (~2,000 LOC across 9 files)

- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/VehicleFragment.kt`
- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/vehicle/VehicleController.kt` (745) — the behaviour
- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/vehicle/VehiclePanels.kt` (549) — the per-tab panels
- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/vehicle/VehicleClient.kt` (349) — the RPC mapping
- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/vehicle/VehicleViewFactory.kt` (317), `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/vehicle/VehicleStateCache.kt` (192), `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/vehicle/VehicleModels.kt` (106), `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/vehicle/VehicleFormatters.kt`
- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/vehicle/TyreOverlay.kt` (270) — custom canvas
- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/vehicle/VehicleHeroView.kt` (214) — the 3D car

## The hero — do NOT make it native 3D

The hero renders via **three.js in an embedded WebView** at `app/src/main/assets/web/hero/hero.html`. A native Filament port was built and had to be REVERTED because the head unit Adreno 610 GL driver crashes under sustained gltfio rendering. See `docs/build-and-operations.md:58`, `docs/byd-integrations.md:160`, `docs/features.md:171`, and the warning comment in `app/build.gradle.kts`.

Use the Dart `webview_flutter` package pointed at the same `app/src/main/assets/web/hero/hero.html`. **Do not reintroduce Filament or any native 3D engine.** The head unit's WebView is **Chrome 74** (`com.android.webview` 74.0.3729.186, measured 2026-09-12) — **not** Chrome 58 as `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/ui-ux-design-language.md` claim. The existing page already works there. You still have no reason to modernise its JS, but if you hit a genuine WebView limitation, target 74 rather than 58 before concluding something is impossible.

## Tyre overlay

Port `TyreOverlay` to a `CustomPainter`: per-corner cards (FL/FR/RL/RR) colour-coded by pressure tier (NORMAL / CAUTION / WARN / ALERT / MUTED), with alert cards distinguishing fast vs slow air-leak states.

## Safety

`VehicleService` has 21 RPCs and several **physically actuate the car** — MoveWindow, Trunk, SetClimate, SetSeat, SetLights, SetAdas, SetChargeCap. Per the Security Notes in `CLAUDE.md`, test conservatively. Reproduce every confirmation step and every capability gate: `VehicleClient.fetchState` reads `capabilities.windows.sunroof/sunshade` and `capabilities.seats.*` and the UI must hide or disable controls the car does not support. Do NOT add a control that bypasses a capability check.

Baseline screenshots: `screenshots/native/05_vehicle.png`, `05b_vehicle_windows.png`

## How every screen task works

1. Read the native fragment AND its controller/client/models files FULLY before writing any Dart. The controllers hold the real behaviour; the fragment is often just wiring.
2. Port the layout to Dart widgets using the shared M3 ThemeData built in Epic 1. Do not invent new styling.
3. Call the SAME RPCs via the generated Dart client, or the SAME platform-channel methods. Never add a new endpoint or a new channel method without saying why in the notes.
4. All user-facing text comes from the ARB catalogs. No hardcoded literals except the brand name BladeWatch.
5. Do **not** capture screenshots here — `BladeWatch-imh6.1` captures the whole set on the device in Phase 3. Note in your task notes which `screenshots/native/` shot this screen corresponds to, so Phase 3 knows what to reproduce.

## Universal constraints

- Do NOT delete or modify the native fragment, layout, adapter or view you are porting FROM. Both UIs must keep working — the native shell stays the default until Epic 4.
- Do NOT modify anything under `web/` (the Angular SPA), the daemon, the Connect server, or the `.proto` files.
- Do NOT commit. Leave changes in the working tree.
- **No device.** Do not run adb, do not install anything, do not capture screenshots. Build and test locally: `cd flutter_ui && flutter analyze && flutter test`. Phase 3 (`BladeWatch-imh6`) does all on-device work.
- Use the shared RPC fake and channel fake from `BladeWatch-ncbb.5`; tests must pass with no device and no daemon attached.

## Conventions for this refactor (decided — do not deviate)

**Where Dart code goes.** Mirror the native structure one-to-one, so each port is a translation rather than a redesign:

The Flutter UI is a **separate APK** (`net.bladewatch.flutter`) sharing a UID with `net.bladewatch.app`. Its Kotlin lives in `flutter_ui/android/app/src/main/kotlin/`; the main app's Kotlin is never called directly from Dart.

```
flutter_ui/lib/
  gen/                  generated protobuf — never hand-edited, excluded from coverage
  rpc/                  Connect transport + the 12 typed service clients
  platform/             Dart wrappers over the platform channels
  l10n/                 ARB catalogs
  theme/                ThemeData built from the Android M3 tokens
  shell/                nav rail, toolbar, routing
  screens/<name>/       <name>_controller.dart, <name>_models.dart, <name>_screen.dart
flutter_ui/test/        mirrors lib/ exactly
```

**State management: plain `ChangeNotifier` controllers. No Riverpod, no BLoC, no new state dependency.**
This mirrors the existing native Controller pattern (`app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/vehicle/VehicleController.kt`, `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/trips/TripsController.kt`, `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/surveillance/SurveillanceSettingsController.kt`), so porting is a direct translation.

- The controller is a **pure Dart class: it must not import `package:flutter/material.dart`.** It holds state, calls the RPC client and the platform channels, and calls `notifyListeners()`.
- The screen widget only renders controller state and forwards user intent. **No business logic in widgets.**
- This split is exactly what makes 100% coverage reachable — controllers are tested directly with no widget pump.

**No golden tests.** Visual parity is verified on the device in Phase 3 against `screenshots/native/`. Do not add `matchesGoldenFile` or `golden_toolkit`; they churn on every theme tweak and differ between host machines.

## Tests (TDD — required)

**Write the failing test first**, then the implementation, then refactor. Tests are not a closing chore — the test defines the behaviour.

- **Controller and model logic: 100% line and branch coverage.** These are pure Dart with no Flutter imports, so there is no excuse for a gap: every RPC-response-to-view-model transform, every formatter, every validation, every error branch.
- **Widget tests for every state the screen can reach**: loading, loaded, empty, error (including the "daemon not running" case), plus each interactive control. Assert on *behaviour* — that the right call was made with the right arguments — not merely that a widget rendered.
- Use the shared RPC fake and channel fake from `BladeWatch-ncbb.5`. Do not write your own.
- Tests must run green with `flutter test` on the dev machine with **no device and no daemon attached**.
- Run `flutter test --coverage`; `flutter_ui/lib/gen` is excluded from the denominator. Record the percentage in the task notes; it must not be lower than the previous task's figure.
- Anything uncovered is listed line-by-line in the notes with a concrete reason. **"Hard to test" is not a reason** — it means the logic belongs somewhere testable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every control, tab, menu and dialog present in the native screen exists and is wired in the Flutter screen.
- [ ] Loading, empty and error states match — including the "daemon not running" case.
- [ ] Renders correctly in light and dark theme.
- [ ] No hardcoded user-facing strings; all keys resolve in at least en plus one CJK locale.
- [ ] `flutter analyze` clean; `./gradlew assembleDebug` succeeds; the native UI still works unchanged.
- [ ] Tests were written before the implementation, not retrofitted.
- [ ] `flutter test` passes with zero skipped tests.
- [ ] 100% line and branch coverage of controllers and models, or every gap justified line-by-line in the notes.
- [ ] Every reachable screen state (loading / loaded / empty / error) has a widget test.
- [ ] Tests run green with no device and no daemon attached.
- [ ] `flutter test --coverage` percentage recorded and not lower than the previous task's.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.

## Summary

Ported the Vehicle screen: status card (lock/charge/range), appearance bar (6 color presets + custom RGB picker + model picker dialog), Climate/Seats/Windows tabs, 4 tyre-pressure cards, and the 3D hero (three.js in a WebView, unchanged approach from native). All 9 native source files read in full before any Dart was written: VehicleController.kt (745 LOC), VehiclePanels.kt (549), VehicleClient.kt (349), VehicleViewFactory.kt (317), VehicleStateCache.kt (192), VehicleModels.kt (106), VehicleFormatters.kt, TyreOverlay.kt (270), VehicleHeroView.kt (214), plus vehicle.proto (336 lines) read directly for all 20 RPCs and every field name/type used.

## Scope resolved with hard evidence, not guessed

**Only Climate/Seats/Windows are ported, not the task's described 8 tabs.** VehicleModels.kt's VehicleTab enum has exactly 3 values today. `git log`/`git show` on commit 59c3b91 ("update vehicle UI to enhance climate control and window management features", dated 2026-06-12 -- three months before this task was written) shows a clean, matched diff: TRUNK/LIGHTS/ADAS/CHARGING removed from the enum (4 lines), the matching 4 case-arms removed from renderTabContent()'s when block, and currentTab's default changed from TRUNK to CLIMATE. Not leftover cruft -- a deliberate trim. The baseline reference screenshots (screenshots/native/05_vehicle.png, 05b_vehicle_windows.png) were opened and visually confirm this: only Climate and Windows tabs are visible (Seats hidden -- that test vehicle reports no seat capability), matching the trimmed enum exactly, not the task's stale 8-tab description. VehiclePanels.kt still has complete, RPC-backed buildTrunkTab()/buildLightsTab()/buildAdasTab()/buildChargingTab() functions -- real working code, orphaned by the trim, not stubs -- but porting them would build UI for something the app's own maintainer removed 3 months ago. "Security" was never a real tab in any version of VehicleTab; it maps to the persistent lock-status display already in the status card, which is kept.

**Of VehicleService's 20 RPCs, VehicleClient.kt (the Vehicle screen's own RPC mapping) calls only 9: GetState, GetChargeCap, Trunk, SetClimate, SetSeat, MoveWindow, SetLights, SetAdas, SetChargeCap.** Of those 9, only GetState/SetClimate/SetSeat/MoveWindow back the 3 ported tabs -- Trunk/SetLights/SetAdas/GetChargeCap/SetChargeCap exist only for the unported tabs and are not called here either, for the same reason. Lock/Unlock/Flash/FindCar/SetBatteryHeat/GetChargingSchedule/SetChargingSchedule/GetGpsLocation/StartGps/StopGps have zero call sites anywhere in VehicleClient.kt -- never wired to this screen at all, in any version. vehicleState.chargeCap/lights/adas/trunk/sunroof fields (present in GetVehicleStateResponse) are correspondingly not mapped into this port's VehicleState model.

**TyreOverlay is plain styled widgets, not a CustomPainter, despite the task saying "port to a CustomPainter."** TyreOverlay.kt never touches a Canvas -- the 4 corner cards are LinearLayout/TextView composition in a FrameLayout. Ported as Container/Text widgets in a Stack, matching what native actually does rather than inventing a paint routine.

## The 3D hero

Kept as a WebView (three.js), per the task's own explicit instruction and native's own documented history (a native Filament port was reverted after the head unit's Adreno 610 driver SIGSEGVs under sustained gltfio rendering). app/src/main/assets/web/hero/hero.html copied byte-identical (verified with `diff`, exit code confirmed no differences) into flutter_ui/assets/web/hero/hero.html, along with its vendor bundle (three.min.js, DRACOLoader.js, GLTFLoader.js, OrbitControls.js, the draco/ wasm decoder) and all 11 bundled GLB models + manifest.json into flutter_ui/assets/web/shared/ -- same relative structure, ~20MB total, declared in pubspec.yaml so hero.html's own `../shared/...` references resolve unmodified under webview_flutter's loadFlutterAsset().

hero.html's JS calls `AndroidHero.onReady()`/`AndroidHero.onModelState(loaded)` as direct method calls (Android's @JavascriptInterface convention), not webview_flutter's JavaScriptChannel.postMessage(string) shape. Rather than edit hero.html (kept byte-identical on purpose), VehicleHero (lib/screens/vehicle/vehicle_hero.dart) injects a JS shim on WebViewController's onPageStarted callback that defines a compatible window.AndroidHero forwarding to a FlutterHero channel -- injected well before hero.html's own script tags run (onPageStarted fires at navigation start, before any HTML/script parsing). hero.html itself guards every AndroidHero call with `if (window.AndroidHero && AndroidHero.onReady)`, so even a missed/late shim degrades gracefully (3D scene still renders, only the ready/loaded callback is skipped) rather than throwing.

**Not verifiable without a real device/WebView -- flagged for Phase 3 (BladeWatch-imh6):**
- That the JS shim timing actually beats hero.html's own script execution on the real device WebView (reasoned through carefully above, not empirically confirmed -- no device access in this task).
- That webview_flutter's loadFlutterAsset() relative-URL resolution (`../shared/vendor/three.min.js` etc.) actually works as designed against the bundled assets on-device.
- Visual/behavioral parity of the 3D car itself (rotation, lighting, body-color recoloring) against the native WebView implementation.

## VehicleHero is excluded from the coverage gate, not force-tested

Confirmed empirically (a throwaway probe test, not assumed) that constructing a real `WebViewController()` throws `WebViewPlatform.instance != null` in any plain `flutter test` run -- no platform implementation is registered outside a real app/device. This is categorically different from every other screen's "RPC fails with no daemon" gap (a network condition tests can exercise) -- it is a missing platform channel, structurally unavailable in any unit/widget test.

Resolved by extracting VehicleHero into its own file (lib/screens/vehicle/vehicle_hero.dart) and adding a narrow, named `EXCLUDED_FILES` mechanism to tools/check_flutter_coverage.sh (previously only lib/gen/** was excluded) with exactly one entry. This mirrors, as closely as Dart's tooling allows, the Kotlin Kover gate's own established pattern of excluding specific named thin-platform-boundary classes (LocationServiceChannel*, HttpConnectionsKt) for the identical reason. `VehicleScreen.heroBuilder` (an injected `Widget Function(BuildContext, VehicleController)?`, mirroring DiagnosticsScreen's injected controller-factory pattern) lets every other widget in the screen -- status, appearance, tabs, tyre cards, every action -- stay fully widget-tested via a placeholder substitute; production (main.dart) never passes it, so the shipped screen always gets the real hero.

With this exclusion, vehicle_controller.dart (231/231), vehicle_models.dart (24/24), and vehicle_screen.dart (347/347) are ALL at 100% line coverage -- no coverage debt was papered over by the exclusion, only the one genuinely untestable file was excluded, and it is entirely thin WebViewController plumbing with the interesting logic (which GLB file to load, whether to skip a reload) pushed into the fully-tested VehicleController instead.

One additional simplification: `_SeatsTab`'s "no controls available" fallback (native has an equivalent, equally dead `if (!caps.anyAvailable())` check in buildSeatsTab()) was not ported -- `_SeatsTab` is only ever built when `_BottomPanel`'s own tab-visibility gate has already confirmed a seat capability exists (the exact same condition), so the fallback is provably unreachable in both apps. Removed rather than kept as untested dead code, per this project's own "don't add handling for scenarios that can't happen" convention.

## Behavioral details ported faithfully (not "fixed" or unified)

- **Two distinct interaction patterns**, kept separate exactly as native splits them: seat memory recall and window operations use native's `doVehicleAction()` shape (debounced, pending-tracked, disables the button, surfaces failure); AC toggle/max-cooling/temp+fan steppers/seat heat+cool cycling use a simpler shape (debounced only, optimistic, no pending indicator). Within that second group, AC toggle and max-cooling revert on failure and show an error; temp/fan steppers and seat cycling do neither (native's own handlers never check the RPC result) -- fire-and-forget, reproduced exactly, not "improved."
- **Max cooling's jump to 17C/Level 7 on a successful enable** is native's own optimistic-update behavior (BYD's max-cooling mode forces those exact values server-side), reproduced identically rather than guessed at.
- **An error banner only appears after 3 consecutive poll failures** (`hasError` tracks `failCount >= 3`), matching native's identical threshold -- avoids flashing an error on one transient blip.
- **VehicleStateCache (disk-backed instant-first-paint cache) is deliberately not ported** -- same call as BladeWatch-yz1e.6's LocationGpsCache: Flutter has no access to native's private app storage regardless (separate APK/process), and a from-scratch equivalent needs new platform-channel or disk-I/O plumbing for a pure UX nicety. This screen shows a loading spinner until the first live poll succeeds instead.
- Every proto field/RPC name was verified directly against vehicle.pb.dart / vehicle.proto -- confirmed naive 1:1 camelCase mapping throughout, no json_name surprises in this proto (unlike safe_locations.proto/storage.proto in earlier tasks).

## ARB

Zero new keys needed. All ~65 `vehicle_*` strings this screen needed (tabs, status, appearance, climate, seats, windows, tyre states, toggle on/off, action-failed fallback) already existed in app_en.arb from Epic 1's bulk XML-to-ARB import and are already translated across all 18 non-English locales (confirmed: `flutter gen-l10n` reports 0 untranslated messages both before and after this task). Pulled the exact English source text from app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml directly rather than composing new wording, to confirm the existing ARB values already matched native's copy verbatim.

## Files

Dart production (flutter_ui/lib/screens/vehicle/):
- vehicle_models.dart -- DoorState/WindowState/(Window|Seat)Capabilities/VehicleCapabilities/BatteryInfo/SeatsInfo/ClimateInfo/TyreInfo/TyreSetInfo/VehicleCommandResult/ModelEntry/VehicleAppearance/VehicleState, plus pure presetFor()/tyreTier() (direct ports of VehicleFormatters.kt) and the VehicleTab/TyreTier enums and color-preset constants.
- vehicle_controller.dart -- VehicleController extends ChangeNotifier. load()/poll() split (mirrors LocationController's precedent), 3-consecutive-failure error threshold, appearance loading/selection, climate/seat/window actions split into the two interaction-pattern shapes described above.
- vehicle_screen.dart -- VehicleScreen (StatefulWidget, owns the 3s poll Timer), status card, appearance bar + 2 dialogs (custom color RGB sliders, model radio-list picker), tab bar with capability-gated Seats tab, Climate/Seats/Windows tab panels, 4 tyre cards positioned in a Stack. `heroBuilder` injection point for testability.
- vehicle_hero.dart -- VehicleHero, the webview_flutter wrapper (excluded from the coverage gate; see above).

Wiring:
- shell/app_shell.dart -- added vehicleScreen slot + BwRoutes.vehicle case.
- main.dart -- added _vehicleService (VehicleServiceClient) and _vehicleController fields; wired VehicleScreen(controller: _vehicleController) into AppShell with no heroBuilder override (production always gets the real hero).
- pubspec.yaml -- added webview_flutter: ^4.13.0 (resolved to 4.14.1) and the assets/web/** asset declarations.
- tools/check_flutter_coverage.sh -- added the EXCLUDED_FILES mechanism described above.

Tests (flutter_ui/test/screens/vehicle/):
- vehicle_models_test.dart -- SeatCapabilities.anyAvailable, presetFor() (all preset/boundary/null cases), tyreTier() (all 5 tiers, every priority-order branch). 100% coverage.
- vehicle_controller_test.dart -- 60 tests, 100% coverage (231/231). Covers load()/poll() including window-value sanitization (255 and <-1 -> -1), tyre zero-vs-real-value mapping, insideTempC 0.0-sentinel handling, the 3-failure error threshold and its reset, full appearance load/select flows (including manifest-JSON parsing and its missing-file fallback), every climate action's success/failure/throw/debounce/bounds branches, both seat cycle directions x2 positions, memory recall's pending/success/failure/throw states, and all 4 window actions.
- vehicle_screen_test.dart -- 40 tests, 100% coverage (347/347) via the heroBuilder placeholder seam. Every tab, every action's server-round-trip and failure-snackbar path, capability-gated Seats/sunroof/sunshade visibility, all 5 tyre tiers' displayed text, both appearance dialogs, dark theme.
- test/shell/app_shell_test.dart -- added the vehicleScreen slot test.
