   reasoning BladeWatch-1xt9 used for pgrep. The exact command is reconstructible from the
   observed live process:
     sh -c CLASSPATH=<apk path> app_process /system/bin --nice-name=<name> <class>
   The APK path must be resolved at runtime, not baked in: it changes on every reinstall
   (observed today: net.bladewatch.app-_j1fxja9… then -vXP3uLdeg22…).

THE DECISION NEEDED: where does "the user stopped this daemon" live so that both processes agree?

  (a) Persist it in UnifiedConfigManager (e.g. a `daemons` section), read by both the new IPC
      command and DaemonStartupManager.runHealthCheck(). Cheap, and the public-config IPC for
      exactly this shape already exists (BladeWatch-hygs). BUT it changes behaviour: native
      deliberately clears user-stopped on every launch and boot, so today a stopped daemon comes
      back after a reboot. Persisting it means a user could stop the DASHCAM and have it stay
      stopped across reboots. That is a product/safety call, not a technical one.
  (b) Keep the native semantics (stop lasts until the next app launch/boot) by holding the flag
      in the daemon and having DaemonStartupManager ask the daemon for it. No behaviour change,
      more moving parts, and the flag dies with the daemon it describes.
  (c) Restrict the feature to ZROK_TUNNEL only. Its enabled state is ALREADY persisted natively
      (OPTIONAL_DAEMONS + PreferencesManager.isDaemonEnabled/onDaemonToggled), so the question is
      already answered for it. The other three keep the honest "not supported" message. Smallest
      correct step; leaves most of the screen inert.

Note (a) and (b) both require editing DaemonStartupManager, which is outside this task's stated
"nothing else under server//daemon/" constraint — the scope needs widening either way.

Do not guess. Get this decided before writing code.
close_reason: Implemented per the decisions recorded on this issue: ZROK_TUNNEL only, CAMERA_DAEMON not stoppable. Added daemon_set_enabled to TcpCommandServer, gated by a fixed allow-list (TOGGLEABLE_DAEMONS) checked before anything happens; nothing from the wire reaches a shell and the PIDs signalled come from the server's own procfs scan keyed by the enum, never from the request. Enabling records intent in UnifiedConfigManager's new cross-process daemons section and lets DaemonStartupManager's health check do the real launch through the full ZrokLauncher flow; disabling records intent AND kills the process, because that health check only ever relaunches. DaemonStartupManager now prefers the config section over app-private SharedPreferences (falling back to it when unset) so a toggle from either UI cannot drift. Added DaemonControl.setDaemonEnabled (Kotlin), daemon.setEnabled in MainActivity, DaemonChannel.setDaemonEnabled (Dart), DaemonKind.canToggle, and SettingsDaemonsController.enabledSetterFor wired in main.dart. The Zrok row now has both a configure button and a working switch; the other three keep a switch for visibility but are refused locally with the existing message and no IPC round trip. 9 new Java tests, 2 Kotlin, 2 Dart channel, plus updated controller/screen tests -- 3 existing tests pinned the old behaviour and were rewritten to the new truth. Verified on device: all three core daemons and a shell-metacharacter type refused, ZROK accepted, config round-trips to daemons.ZROK_TUNNEL and back, tapping Surveillance Daemon shows the honest message with the switch and daemon untouched. NOTE: the config now records daemons.ZROK_TUNNEL=false, which matches the tunnel's actual pre-existing state (no token configured, never running). 1334 Dart tests, coverage back to 99.97% after extracting the main.dart wiring closure into a testable factory, both Kover gates green, assembleDebug green. docs/ipc-auth-and-secrets.md and docs/daemons-and-processes.md updated.

title: Expose UnifiedConfigManager's public config sections over IPC (no path exists today)
description:
## Problem

Several Settings screens need to read/write `UnifiedConfigManager`'s PUBLIC (non-secret) config
sections from the Flutter APK, but no IPC command exposes that store — only the daemon-owned
SECRET store (`SecretConfigStore`, via `secret_get`/`secret_put`/`secret_delete`, wrapped by
`ConfigChannel`/`SecretConfigChannel` from BladeWatch-ncbb.2) is reachable today.

Traced while building BladeWatch-yz1e.3 (Settings hub), not assumed:

- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/settings/SettingsOverlayFragment.kt`
  reads/writes `UnifiedConfigManager.getStatusOverlay()`/`setStatusOverlay()` — the
  `statusOverlay` section (`cameraVisible`/`tripVisible` booleans) that gates the floating
  status-pill segments.
- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/settings/SettingsPrivacyFragment.kt`
  reads/writes `UnifiedConfigManager.isTimingLogsEnabled()`/`setTimingLogsEnabled()` and
  `isDebugLogsEnabled()`/`setDebugLogsEnabled()` — the `developerOptions` section
  (`timingLogsEnabled` default true, `debugLogsEnabled` default false).
- `UnifiedConfigManager`'s file (`/storage/emulated/0/BladeWatch/data/bladewatch_config.json`) is
  world-rw (chmod 666) and BOTH the app UID and daemon UID already read/write it directly — but
  this path is NOT inside `net.bladewatch.flutter`'s package-scoped storage, and there is no
  existing IPC command mirroring `secret_get_section`/`secret_put` for this store. Grepped
  `TcpCommandServer.java`'s full command switch: no `config_get`/`config_put` case exists for the
  public store, only the `secret_*` family.

Both screens were built against an injectable `loadSettings`/`persist` function pair (see
`SettingsOverlayController`/`SettingsPrivacyController` in
`flutter_ui/lib/screens/settings/`) — same shape as `DashboardController.tunnelUrlSource` from
BladeWatch-m1po — so this task can wire in a real implementation later without touching either
controller. Their current defaults: Overlay always reports both indicators visible (native's own
fallback values) and silently no-ops on write; Privacy's logging toggles default to
timing=on/debug=off (native's own defaults) and also no-op on write. Toggling either currently
updates in-memory UI state for the session but does not persist across an app restart.

## Fix

Add a new IPC command family (e.g. `config_get_section`/`config_put`/`config_delete`, mirroring
`secret_get_section`/`secret_put`/`secret_delete`'s shape exactly) to `TcpCommandServer.java`,
backed by `UnifiedConfigManager` instead of `SecretConfigStore`. Since this store is NOT secret,
consider whether a stricter allowlist of writable sections is warranted (`statusOverlay`,
`developerOptions` at minimum) rather than accepting an arbitrary section name, to avoid a new
command becoming a generic "write anything to the public config" primitive without review.

Then, mirroring BladeWatch-1xt9/ncbb.2's pattern: add a Kotlin wrapper
(`flutter_ui/android/.../config/PublicConfigChannel.kt` or similar) alongside the existing
`SecretConfigChannel.kt`, wire `"publicConfig.get"`/`"publicConfig.put"` (or similar) in
`MainActivity.kt`, add a Dart `PublicConfigChannel` (`flutter_ui/lib/platform/`) alongside the
existing `ConfigChannel`. Then swap `SettingsOverlayController`'s and
`SettingsPrivacyController`'s injected functions in `flutter_ui/lib/main.dart` from their current
defaults to real implementations backed by the new channel.

## Constraints

Same as BladeWatch-1xt9/m1po: this task may modify `TcpCommandServer.java` (that's the point of
it) but nothing else under `server/`/`daemon/`; don't touch `PeerCredentials.java`; don't
reintroduce free-form shell execution. Do NOT commit.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New IPC command(s) added, reads/writes real `UnifiedConfigManager` sections without ADB.
- [ ] Kotlin/Dart wrapper methods added, tests written first.
- [ ] `SettingsOverlayController`/`SettingsPrivacyController`'s injected functions are swapped
      from their always-default/no-op fallbacks to the real channel in `main.dart`; existing
      tests (already covering the "no follow-up yet" default path via the injected-function seam)
      still pass, plus new tests for the real-channel path.
- [ ] All 3 coverage gates pass, none lower than before.
- [ ] `./gradlew assembleDebug` (both Gradle projects) succeeds.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason: Added config_get_section/config_put to TcpCommandServer, backed by UnifiedConfigManager and gated by an explicit allow-list (statusOverlay, developerOptions only). Reads route through the same typed accessors the native UI uses, so defaults for absent keys match native exactly. Added PublicConfigChannel on both the Kotlin and Dart sides (separate from the secret-store ConfigChannel) and wired SettingsOverlayController/SettingsPrivacyController to it via their existing injected-function seams. Both controllers now revert the switch if the IPC write fails, so a failed write cannot look like a saved setting. Verified on device: both panes read the real config (Overlay showed both off, Privacy showed debug-logs on, neither of which is the hardcoded default), writes persist across an app restart, and the native StatusOverlayService picked the change up live with no service restart. Non-allow-listed sections (network, surveillance) refused for both read and write. IPC token still 644; PeerCredentials untouched. 1324 Dart tests, 99.97% coverage, both Kover gates green. docs/ipc-auth-and-secrets.md updated (and its stale references to the removed shell command corrected).

title: Expose the Zrok tunnel URL over IPC (no IPC path exists today)
description:
## Problem

The Dashboard's tunnel tile/hero-chip/QR-code feature needs the current Zrok tunnel URL, but
there is no IPC or RPC path to it from the Flutter APK — traced through the actual native
source while building BladeWatch-yz1e.2 (Dashboard), not assumed:

- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/daemon/ZrokController.kt`: `_tunnelUrl` is
  an in-memory `MutableLiveData<String?>`, set only from `ZrokLauncher`'s callback when a
  tunnel process is launched/monitored via ADB (`onTunnelUrl(url: String)`).
- The URL is separately cached in `PreferencesManager.setLastZrokUrl()`
  (`app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/util/PreferencesManager.kt:179`) — but that
  uses plain Android `SharedPreferences`, private to `net.bladewatch.app`, not the IPC-backed
  `SecretConfigStore`/`secret_*` family. Not reachable from `net.bladewatch.flutter` even
  though the two APKs share a UID.
- No proto service exposes a tunnel/Zrok concept at all (checked all 12: Auth, Notifications,
  Recordings, SafeLocations, Settings, Storage, Stream, Surveillance, System, Trips, Update,
  Vehicle).

So there is currently no IPC-only way for the Flutter APK to learn the tunnel URL, matching
the exact shape of the gap BladeWatch-1xt9 already fixed for daemon process status — same
root cause (a native feature built ADB/local-storage-first, before the Flutter APK's
IPC-only constraint existed).

## Fix

Add a new IPC command (e.g. `tunnelStatus`) to `TcpCommandServer.java`, returning the current
Zrok tunnel URL if one is active. Read `ZrokController.kt` and `ZrokLauncher.kt` fully first —
the daemon-side implementation needs to determine the current URL without an app-UID-only
`PreferencesManager`/SharedPreferences read (the daemon runs as shell UID, in a different
process than `PreferencesManager`'s owner). Options to investigate: whether `zrok status`
(shell-invoked, no ADB needed — the daemon already runs as shell UID, same reasoning as
BladeWatch-1xt9's `pgrep` approach) reports the active share URL directly, or whether the
daemon has its own independent record of the URL from launching the tunnel itself.

Response shape suggestion: `{"status":"ok","url": "<url or null>"}`.

Then, mirroring BladeWatch-1xt9's pattern exactly: add `DaemonControl.tunnelStatus()`
(Kotlin, `flutter_ui/android/.../daemon/DaemonControl.kt`), wire `"daemon.tunnelStatus"` in
`MainActivity.kt`, add `DaemonChannel.tunnelStatus()` (Dart,
`flutter_ui/lib/platform/daemon_channel.dart`). BladeWatch-yz1e.2 (Dashboard) built its tunnel
UI against an injectable data-source interface specifically so this can be swapped in without
touching the screen/controller once this lands — see `DashboardController`'s
`TunnelUrlSource` (or similarly-named) constructor parameter, whose default currently always
reports "no tunnel."

## Constraints

Same as BladeWatch-1xt9: this task is allowed to modify `TcpCommandServer.java` (that's the
point of it) but nothing else under `server/`/`daemon/`; don't touch `PeerCredentials.java`;
don't reintroduce free-form shell execution — only whatever fixed, narrow check the chosen
implementation needs. Do NOT commit.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New IPC command added, returns the real tunnel URL (or none) without ADB.
- [ ] Kotlin/Dart wrapper methods added, tests written first.
- [ ] `DashboardController`'s tunnel data source is swapped from the always-empty default to
      the real one; existing Dashboard tests (already covering "no tunnel" via the fake) still
      pass, plus new tests for the "has a tunnel" case.
- [ ] All 3 coverage gates pass, none lower than before.
- [ ] `./gradlew assembleDebug` (both Gradle projects) succeeds.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
acceptance_criteria: New daemonStatus-sibling IPC command returns the real tunnel URL; Kotlin/Dart wrappers added with tests; DashboardController's tunnel data source swapped to the real implementation; all coverage gates pass; assembleDebug succeeds for both Gradle projects.
close_reason: Added tunnelStatus to TcpCommandServer: reads the share URL from zrok's own log (daemon already runs as shell UID, so no ADB and no shell exec), gated on the tunnel process being alive exactly as native gates it. Two deliberate improvements over native's grep head -1: takes the LAST URL in the log, since the log spans launches and the first match can be a dead session's name (the drift native patches up afterwards with reconcileTunnelUrl), and never loads the log into memory. Added DaemonControl.tunnelStatus (Kotlin), daemon.tunnelStatus in MainActivity, DaemonChannel.tunnelUrl (Dart), and swapped DashboardController's tunnelUrlSource in main.dart from the always-empty default to the real channel. 9 Java tests, 2 Kotlin, 4 Dart; the last-match behaviour is mutation-verified (flipping it to first-match fails the test). The tail-seek is a memory bound, not a behaviour, and no test claims to cover it. Verified on device: no tunnel returns running:false/url:null; a log containing a URL with no live process still returns null (the stale-URL gate); with a sleep-only stand-in process the Dashboard rendered the QR code, the URL and an Online chip. All device test artefacts removed and the Dashboard confirmed back to No tunnel running / Offline. Found and filed BladeWatch-xzhv while testing: isProcessRunning matches any command line containing a daemon name, which weakens this gate. 1328 Dart tests, 99.97% coverage, both Kover gates green, assembleDebug green. docs/ipc-auth-and-secrets.md and docs/networking-and-tunnels.md updated.

title: Native app: translatable=false URL strings corrupted by a past translation pass in most locales
description:
## Problem

4 keys in `app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml` are marked `translatable="false"` because they are plain URLs that must never vary by locale:

- `settings_about_support_kofi_url` = `https://ko-fi.com/E1E71XALHX`
- `settings_about_license_url` = `https://github.com/yash-srivastava/BladeWatch-release/blob/main/LICENSE`
- `settings_about_source_url` = `https://github.com/yash-srivastava/BladeWatch-release`
- `settings_about_star_url` = `https://github.com/yash-srivastava/BladeWatch-release`

Despite the `translatable="false"` marker, a past bulk/LLM translation pass over this catalog translated these 4 keys anyway in most of the 16 non-English `values-*/strings.xml` files. Having no real content to translate (a bare URL), it hallucinated unrelated sentences instead of leaving them alone. This is live in the shipped app today: on a device set to one of the affected locales, Settings → About → Source/License/Star/Support opens (or tries to open) garbage text instead of the real link.

Verified by direct inspection (`grep -oP` against each `values-*/strings.xml`) on 2026-09-12:

- **Hallucinated/unrelated text** (8 locales): `values-de`, `values-es`, `values-fr`, `values-it`, `values-ja`, `values-nl`, `values-zh-rCN`, `values-zh-rTW`. Example: `values-de`'s `settings_about_source_url` is `"Das ist ein sehr schönes Beispiel."` ("This is a very nice example.") — not a URL at all. `values-zh-rTW`'s is `"沒有任何樓盤符合您的搜尋 -"` ("No listings match your search") — looks like leftover real-estate-app boilerplate from whatever bulk corpus the translation pass drew from.
- **Blank** (1 locale): `values-th` — all 4 keys are empty strings.
- **Malformed but recognizable** (2 locales): `values-ko` (URL wrapped in literal `[...]` brackets, `http://` not `https://`), `values-nb` (`settings_about_license_url` is literally `"HTTPS: http://github.com/.../LICENSE"` — a stray "HTTPS:" prefix glued onto an `http://` URL).
- **Already correct** (5 locales): `values-hi`, `values-pt-rBR`, `values-ru`, `values-tr`, `values-vi`.

This was discovered while writing `tools/i18n/xml_to_arb.py` for BladeWatch-ncbb.3 (porting these strings to Flutter ARB). The Flutter side is unaffected — that script pins all 4 `translatable="false"` keys to the English template's value for every locale ARB, regardless of what (if anything) the source locale XML says, so this bug does not propagate into the new Flutter UI. This task is only about fixing it at the source, for the native UI, which still reads these files directly.

## Fix

For each of the 16 non-English `app/src/main/res/values-*/strings.xml` files, **delete** the `<string>` element for these 4 keys entirely (do not just overwrite the text). Since the keys are `translatable="false"`, Android's normal resource fallback already serves `values/strings.xml`'s correct value to every locale that has no override — deleting the bad per-locale copies is the permanent fix; it also means these 4 values can never drift out of sync again, since after this change they exist in exactly one file. (Do not delete the entries from `values/strings.xml` itself — that is the template and is already correct.)

`app/build.gradle.kts`'s `validateAndroidStrings` task already excludes `translatable="false"` keys from its key-parity comparison (`parseStrings()`: `if (el.getAttribute("translatable") == "false") continue`), so removing these 4 entries from the 16 locale files will not trip a "missing key" failure there.

## Constraints

- Only touch the 4 named keys. Do not touch any other `<string>`/`<plurals>` entry.
- Do not touch `values/strings.xml` (the English template) — it already has the correct values and is not `translatable="false"`-affected there.
- Do not touch `flutter_ui/` — the Flutter ARBs already work around this independently (see Problem section); no change needed there as a result of this task.
- Do NOT commit. Leave changes in the working tree.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The 4 keys are completely removed from all 16 `values-*/strings.xml` files (grep confirms zero remaining occurrences of `settings_about_support_kofi_url`, `settings_about_license_url`, `settings_about_source_url`, `settings_about_star_url` outside `values/strings.xml`).
- [ ] `values/strings.xml` is unchanged.
- [ ] `./gradlew validateAndroidStrings` still passes (proves the deletion doesn't trip the parity check).
- [ ] `./gradlew assembleDebug` succeeds.
- [ ] Spot-check on a device or emulator set to at least one previously-broken locale (e.g. German) that Settings → About → Source/License/Star/Support now show/open the real GitHub/Ko-fi URLs.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
acceptance_criteria: 16 locale files have the 4 settings_about_*_url keys removed; values/strings.xml unchanged; ./gradlew validateAndroidStrings passes; ./gradlew assembleDebug succeeds; spot-checked on-device in at least one previously-broken locale.

  content did not respond to `input swipe` at the coordinates tried; navigation was done

  fresh "Allow USB debugging?" prompt and a storage-permission prompt after the reinstall —
  both handled via `input tap`/checked "always allow" so they will not recur).
- Also handled during reinstall (routine, not part of this fix): daemons stopped/relaunched
  correctly, ADB TCP connection dropped and recovered twice as documented in CLAUDE.md
  ("killing daemons can briefly drop the ADB-over-TCP connection").

## Constraints honored

- Only the 4 named keys touched, only in the 16 non-English locale files.

- `flutter_ui/` untouched (its ARBs already independently pin these 4 keys to the template,
  per BladeWatch-ncbb.3 — unaffected by and unrelated to this native-side fix).
- Not committed — changes left in the working tree.

No mistakes found on verification.

title: Add build-failing key-parity validation for res/values*/strings.xml (17 locales, currently unguarded)
description:
## Context

`res/values*/strings.xml` has **624 translatable keys across 17 locales** and **nothing validates them**. A key added to English alone builds clean and ships missing strings in 16 languages, with no warning at any point.

This is not hypothetical for this project. The web catalogs had exactly this class of failure twice — a stale cached catalog rendered raw keys across the whole SPA, and LLM-edited locale JSON shipped with smart-quote delimiters and unescaped quotes in CJK values. Both were fixed by adding a check that **fails the build**, which is how `validateI18nCatalogs` came to exist.

That task guards only `src/main/assets/web/i18n/*.json`. The Android string catalogs — the larger, older, more edited set — are still unguarded.

## Why now

Any task that adds a user-facing string touches all 17 files by hand. `BladeWatch-ofzb` is the immediate example and currently has to verify parity by counting occurrences manually. That does not scale and will be skipped.

## Steps

1. Add a `validateAndroidStrings` Gradle task in `app/build.gradle.kts`, next to the existing `validateI18nCatalogs` (line 568) and hooked into `preBuild` the same way (line 613). Follow that task's structure rather than inventing a new pattern.
2. Parse `app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml` as the master key set — only elements marked translatable (the existing file uses `translatable="false"` for some entries; respect that attribute).
3. For each of the 16 `values-<lang>/strings.xml` files, compare key sets against the master and **fail the build** listing the missing keys per locale, in the same style as the existing task's error output.
4. Also fail on malformed XML, and on unescaped apostrophes in string values — the Android-specific footgun equivalent to the smart-quote problem that hit the JSON catalogs.
5. Run it against the current tree **before** adding any enforcement: if the existing 17 files already have gaps, report the count and fix them, or record an explicit allow-list with a reason. Do not ship a task that fails on day one.

## Constraints

- Locale directory names are Android-style: `values-pt-rBR`, `values-zh-rCN`, `values-zh-rTW`, and `values-<lang>` for the rest. `values-night` is **theme colours, not a locale** — exclude it.
- Do NOT modify `validateI18nCatalogs` or weaken its behaviour.
- Do NOT modify `web/`.
- Do NOT auto-translate or auto-fill missing values. The task reports; a human supplies text.
- Do NOT commit.

## Conventions for this refactor

- Kotlin lives under `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/` with `package net.bladewatch.app.*`. Gradle logic lives in `app/build.gradle.kts` — there is no root `app/build.gradle.kts`.
- JVM tests go in `app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/`, measured by Kover (`./gradlew test koverVerify`).

## Tests (TDD — required)

**Write the failing test first.**

- Prove the task **fails** when a key is removed from one locale, and **passes** once restored. Do this for real, then restore — a guard nobody has seen fail is not a guard.
- Prove it fails on malformed XML and on an unescaped apostrophe.
- Prove `values-night` is excluded and does not trigger a false failure.
- 100% coverage of the comparison and reporting logic, or each gap justified in the notes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `validateAndroidStrings` exists in `app/build.gradle.kts` and is hooked into `preBuild`.
- [ ] It fails the build on a missing key, naming the locale and the key.
- [ ] It fails on malformed XML and on an unescaped apostrophe.
- [ ] `values-night` is excluded; `translatable="false"` entries are excluded.
- [ ] The current tree passes, or every pre-existing gap is fixed or explicitly allow-listed with a reason recorded.
- [ ] Each failure mode demonstrated once for real and then restored.
- [ ] `./gradlew assembleDebug` and `./gradlew test` pass; `koverVerify` figure recorded and not lower than before.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason:
Added `validateAndroidStrings` to app/build.gradle.kts, right after `validateI18nCatalogs` and hooked into `preBuild` the same way (did not modify validateI18nCatalogs itself — confirmed by diff, still exactly 2 references: its definition and its preBuild dependency line, both pre-existing).

What it checks, using javax.xml.parsers.DocumentBuilderFactory (stdlib, no new dependency):
- values/strings.xml is the master key set (translatable="false" entries excluded from the required set, matching how Android itself treats them).
- Every values-<lang>/strings.xml (values-pt-rBR, values-zh-rCN, values-zh-rTW, values-<lang> for the rest) is compared against the master key set; any missing key fails the build naming the locale and up to 5 example keys.
- Malformed XML fails the build with the parser's own message, and — since a parse failure has no real key set — does NOT also cascade into reporting every master key as "missing" (an early version of this did exactly that noise; fixed by making parseStrings return a nullable key set and skipping the key-comparison when null).
- Unescaped apostrophes fail the build. Implemented as a small state-machine scanner (track whether a `\` immediately precedes the char, and whether we're inside a `"..."` span) rather than a naive `contains("'")/ count` check, specifically because Android allows two valid styles — `\'` and wrapping the whole value in double quotes — and a naive check would false-positive on the second, legitimate style.
- values-night is excluded by name (it's dark-mode colors/themes, not a locale — it doesn't even have a strings.xml on this tree, confirmed by listing the directory).

Ran against the current tree before wiring in any enforcement, per the task's own instruction: zero pre-existing gaps. 620 translatable keys (not 624 as the task's context paragraph said — that figure was measured before this session's other tasks touched a few strings; 620 is the fresh, live count and is what matters) across 16 non-English locales, full parity, valid XML, no unescaped apostrophes. No fixes or allow-list needed.

Verification — each failure mode demonstrated for real against the actual tracked files, then restored, with MD5 checksums confirming byte-for-byte restoration each time (git checkout was not used for restore since values-de/es/fr already carry legitimate uncommitted edits from BladeWatch-ofzb earlier this session that must not be discarded):
1. Deleted `dialog_ok` from values-de/strings.xml (line removed via sed, backed up first) → validateAndroidStrings FAILED: "values-de/strings.xml: 1 key(s) missing vs values/strings.xml (dialog_ok)". Restored from backup, MD5 matched the pre-mutation hash (32aa2f74...), task PASSED again.
2. Corrupted values-fr/strings.xml by stripping its closing `</resources>` tag → FAILED: "values-fr/strings.xml: malformed XML — XML document structures must start and end within the same entity." (and nothing else — confirmed the no-cascade fix). Restored from a full-file backup, MD5 matched (c044fdbe...), task PASSED.
3. Changed values-es's `dialog_ok` to `OK, don't worry` (bare unescaped apostrophe) → FAILED: "values-es/strings.xml: dialog_ok: unescaped apostrophe (use \' or wrap the whole value in double quotes)". Then changed it to `"OK, don't worry"` (double-quote-wrapped, Android's other valid style) → PASSED, proving the double-quote exception is not a false-positive gap. Restored the original `OK`, MD5 matched (b4498c27...), task PASSED.
4. Created a throwaway app/src/main/res/values-night/strings.xml containing exactly one unrelated key (nowhere near the other 620) → task still PASSED (still reported "16 locales", not 17) — proves the exclusion actually does something rather than accidentally passing because the file never existed. Deleted the throwaway file afterward; `git status` shows no diff for values-night (it was never a tracked file).

`./gradlew clean assembleDebug test` — BUILD SUCCESSFUL from a clean build; confirmed validateAndroidStrings actually executes (not skipped/cached — it has no declared inputs/outputs so Gradle never marks it UP-TO-DATE) and prints "Android strings: 16 locales, full key parity with values/strings.xml (620 keys), valid XML, no unescaped apostrophes ✓" as part of the real build.

Not applicable: this is Gradle build-script logic (Kotlin DSL), not application code — like its sibling validateI18nCatalogs, there is no JUnit test file for it; "test coverage" here means every branch demonstrated failing-then-passing for real against the live tree, as done above and as the task's own Tests section asked for ("do this for real, then restore — a guard nobody has seen fail is not a guard"). `./gradlew koverVerify` still doesn't exist (same pre-existing gap noted on BladeWatch-7965.1 and BladeWatch-ofzb — Kover isn't wired in until BladeWatch-ncbb.5, which is gated behind unrelated epics) and this task adds no Kotlin/Java application code for Kover to measure regardless.

Did not modify validateI18nCatalogs or web/. Did not auto-translate or auto-fill anything (none was needed — zero gaps found). Not committed — all changes left in the working tree.

title: Update docs and CLAUDE.md for the Flutter architecture
description:
## Context

Update the documentation to match reality. `CLAUDE.md` has a Documentation Maintenance section mandating this, and the docs are the onboarding path for future agents — stale docs here actively cause wrong work.

## Files to update

- `docs/architecture.md` — the "Android app process — UI shell only" description now means a Flutter host. Update the hybrid-architecture split.
- `docs/ui-ux-design-language.md` (22.5 KB) — **the biggest change.** It currently states the native Android shell is the canonical M3 source of truth and lists `app/src/main/res/values/themes_bladewatch.xml` / `app/src/main/res/values/colors_m3.xml` / `app/src/main/res/values/dimens_bladewatch.xml` as authoritative. Those files are gone or reduced. The Dart `ThemeData` is now the source of truth, with the Angular SPA still tracking the same language by convention. Update the "Two layers, one language" table.
- `docs/features.md` (16.6 KB) — any description of native screens.
- `docs/webview-migration.md` (11.9 KB) — this documents the OLD WebView-to-native migration and its status line says "Migration complete". It is now doubly historical, and it describes `WebViewFragment` as "still present", which will be false. Either retire it or add a clear header explaining it describes a superseded architecture.
- `docs/build-and-operations.md` — add the Flutter build step; keep the existing Filament/Adreno 610 warning, it still applies to the three.js hero.
- `docs/daemons-and-processes.md` — only if daemon behaviour changed (it should not have).
- `docs/README.md` — the one-line app description.

system was verified running on the head unit with the native UI gone.

## What went

- `ui/fragment/**` — 53 files, every screen and its liveview/location/performance/recording/
  surveillance/trips/vehicle/settings subpackages
- `ui/adapter/**`, `ui/view/**`, `ui/dialog/**`, `ui/common/BladeTheme.kt`,
  `ui/dashboard/DashboardInsight.kt`
- `ui/util/{QrCodeGenerator,RecordingScanner,RecordingSectionHeaderDecoration,NavOptionsExt}.kt`
- `ui/viewmodel/{Logs,Main,Recording}ViewModel.kt`

- **10,200 strings**: every `values*/strings.xml` pruned from 618 keys to 29

`MainActivity` was rewritten rather than edited down — 1,753 lines to ~330, keeping the bootstrap
verbatim in its original order. It extends `Activity` instead of `AppCompatActivity` now (no
AppCompat UI left to host, and it takes the daemon APK off a dependency BladeWatch-81g9.3 can
drop) and never calls `setContentView`.

## Three places the task's delete-list was wrong, found by rebuilding rather than trusting it

1. **`overlay_status.xml` and `dialog_setup_guide.xml` must survive.** They belong to
   `StatusOverlayService` and `SetupGuideDialog` — a floating system-overlay window Flutter
   cannot provide. Deleting them crashed the build; both restored from git.
2. **`values*/strings.xml` cannot be deleted, only pruned.** Four surviving components still use
   `R.string`. The 29 keys kept were derived by scanning actual consumers (Java/Kotlin `R.string.`,
   every surviving `@string/` in res/, and the manifest) — not guessed. Each is listed with its
   consumer in a header comment on the file.
3. **`SetupGuideDialog`'s language step opened the deleted native picker.** Language belongs to
   the Flutter UI now, so that row opens the Flutter app instead, with a silent no-op if that APK
   is absent.

## Tests deleted, and why that is safe

Five Kotlin tests in `net.bladewatch.app.ui.fragment.vehicle` went with their package. Each was
checked for Dart coverage first, not assumed:

- `TyreTierTest` → `tyreTier()` is ported to `vehicle_models.dart` with identical tier logic and
  a Dart test group covering every branch INCLUDING both boundaries (33.9/34, 45/45.1).
- `VehicleFormattersTest` → `presetFor()` is ported with its own Dart group.
- `VehicleClientMapTest`, `VehicleClientTyreMapTest`, `VehicleClientCommandResultTest` → the
  vehicle state/tyre/command mapping they covered is exercised by 141 Dart vehicle tests
  (61 controller, 35 screen, 12 models, 33 hero).
- `VehicleI18nParityTest` asserted key parity for vehicle strings across the Android catalogs.
  Those strings moved: 92 `vehicle_*` keys now live in the ARB catalogs under
  `validateArbCatalogs` (862 keys, full parity), and the 29 surviving Android keys are under
  `validateAndroidStrings` (16 locales, full parity). The guarantee is preserved by other means,
  which was verified before deleting.

## A bug I introduced and then misdiagnosed

I moved `wakeServiceHost()` out of `configureFlutterEngine` into `onResume`, because calling
`startActivity` during engine configuration brings another activity to the front mid-setup. That
change is correct and worth keeping.

**But I first blamed it for a black screen, and that was wrong.** The head unit's display had
simply gone to sleep — the car is parked with `powerLevel=OFF`. Proof: the BYD HOME SCREEN
captured black too. I only established that by screenshotting something that is definitely not
mine. Worth remembering: "my screenshot is black" is not evidence about my code until something
else on the same screen proves the display is awake.

Flutter health was then confirmed functionally instead: the app drives `SystemService/GetStatus`
RPCs on its poll cycle with zero flutter errors in logcat.

## Verified on the head unit

Killed all daemons, force-stopped both APKs, installed the stripped service host, opened ONLY the
Flutter app: all three daemons came up, zero FATAL EXCEPTIONs, and
`cmd package query-activities` for MAIN/LAUNCHER returns only `net.bladewatch.flutter`.

`AccMonitor` reports `powerLevel=OFF → sentryMode=true`, so the daemon is in sentry mode rather
than continuous recording — correct for a parked car, not a regression.

## Gates

`./gradlew test koverVerify assembleDebug assembleRelease validateArbCatalogs
validateAndroidStrings` all green; flutter analyze clean; 1403 Dart tests; Dart coverage 99.97%
(7004/7006).

## Note on commit state

Earlier close reasons in this session say "nothing committed". That was true when written, but
the repository now carries three commits covering this session's earlier work which I did not
make. Flagged to the owner. This task's changes are uncommitted in the working tree.

title: Turn the main APK into a UI-less service host
description:
## Context

Turn the main APK into a **UI-less service host**, so the Flutter APK is the only in-car UI. Do this BEFORE deleting any native UI files, so the system is never in a state with no working UI.

Blocked until Epic 3 records the explicit "parity confirmed, safe to delete native UI" verdict.

## End state

| APK | Keeps | Loses |
|---|---|---|
| `net.bladewatch.app` | daemons, camera/surveillance pipeline, HTTP + IPC servers, BYD integration, boot receiver, daemon startup, the `onCreate` bootstrap below | every Fragment, layout, nav graph, `app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml`, and its launcher entry |
| `net.bladewatch.flutter` | the entire in-car UI, and the launcher entry the user taps | — |

## The critical part — bootstrap that must NOT be lost

`app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/MainActivity.kt` is 1,753 lines and is **not only UI**. Its `onCreate` performs essential bootstrap that must still run after the UI is gone:

- `setupStorageDirectories()` — deliberately posted off the `onCreate` critical path via `window.decorView.post {}` because a failure (e.g. a ROM lacking the All-Files-Access settings activity on BYD SL7) must not abort launch. **Keep that deferral.**
- `AdbShellExecutor` construction, then `DeviceIdGenerator.init(adbExecutor)` and `generateDeviceId(this)` — **must happen BEFORE any daemon starts**, because the daemon reads the synced device-id file.
- `BydDataCacheWhitelist.applyAll(this)` on a **background thread** — the existing comment explains `ActivityThread.systemMain()` can block for over a minute waiting for system services, so it must not run on the UI thread. Keep it off the main thread.
- `DaemonStartupManager` and its staggered timing (core ~45s, optional ~60s, health checks from ~90s every 30s).
- The periodic update check, with its `mainHandler` / `updateCheckRunnable` cancelled in `onDestroy()` to avoid leaking across recreate.

## Where does the bootstrap go?

Decide and record the choice in the notes. The bootstrap is currently activity-driven, and the main app will no longer have an activity the user opens. Options, in order of preference:

1. Move it into the existing boot receiver / a foreground service, so it is driven by boot and by `DaemonKeepaliveService` rather than by a user opening an app.
2. Keep a minimal, **non-launcher** `MainActivity` that runs the bootstrap and immediately finishes, started programmatically.

Whichever you choose, it must still run on a cold boot of the head unit with nobody touching the screen — that is the normal case in a car.

## Also in this task

- Remove the main app's launcher `intent-filter` so only the Flutter APK appears on the head unit's app list; make sure the Flutter APK has it.
- The Flutter APK must also survive BYD's background killing — check whether `BydDataCacheWhitelist` needs to whitelist `net.bladewatch.flutter` as well as `net.bladewatch.app`, and handle it if so.
- Confirm the Flutter APK starts on boot if the native app used to (check the boot receiver behaviour), or that the user-facing launch path still works.

## Constraints

- Do NOT remove or reorder any bootstrap step; only change what drives it.
- Do NOT change `DaemonStartupManager` timing.
- Do NOT delete native UI source files in this task — that is `BladeWatch-81g9.2`.
- Do NOT modify `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/PeerCredentials.java`, the IPC servers, or anything under `app/src/test/`.
- Do NOT modify `web/`, the daemon logic, or the protos.
- Do NOT commit.

## Conventions for this refactor

- Dart lives under `flutter_ui/lib/` with `screens/<name>/` holding a pure-Dart `ChangeNotifier` controller, models, and the screen widget. Kotlin lives under `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/` with `package net.bladewatch.app.*`.
- Coverage gates: `flutter test --coverage` (Dart, `lib/gen` excluded) and `./gradlew koverVerify` (Kotlin). Both thresholds ratchet upward and may never be lowered.
- **No golden tests.** Visual parity is verified on the device against `screenshots/native/`.
- Verification happens on the head unit at <CAR_IP>:5555. Always pass `-s <CAR_IP>:5555` to every adb command.

## Tests (regression — required)

This task adds no features, so the bar is regression rather than TDD:

- `./gradlew test` passes with zero skipped tests.
- `cd flutter_ui && flutter test` passes with zero skipped tests.
- `flutter test --coverage` and `./gradlew koverVerify` both run, both figures recorded, **neither lower** than the previous recorded figure.
- If a test had to be deleted because the code under test was deleted, say which, and confirm the behaviour it covered either no longer exists or is now covered by a Dart test.
- Any bug found while verifying gets a **failing test written first**, then the fix — never a fix without a test that would have caught it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `./gradlew assembleDebug`, `./gradlew assembleRelease` and `cd flutter_ui && flutter build apk` all succeed.
- [ ] Clean reinstall of both APKs on <CAR_IP>:5555 per the `CLAUDE.md` sequence.
- [ ] **Cold-boot test**: power-cycle the head unit, touch nothing, and confirm all three core daemons start on their normal staggered schedule.
- [ ] Device ID generation still happens before daemon start (verify in logs).
- [ ] Storage setup still runs and still cannot abort launch.
- [ ] Only the Flutter app appears in the head unit's launcher.
- [ ] The Flutter app is whitelisted against BYD background-killing, or it is confirmed not to need it.
- [ ] Both packages still share one UID (`dumpsys package ... | grep userId`), and IPC from the Flutter app still passes the peer-UID gate.
- [ ] `./gradlew test` passes.
- [ ] `./gradlew test` and `flutter test` both pass with zero skipped tests.
- [ ] Dart and Kotlin coverage figures recorded, neither lower than the previous figure.
- [ ] Any bug found got a failing test written first, then the fix.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason:
Done, and the cold-boot test earned its place — it exposed two things no unit test or compiler
could see, one of them a crash I had just introduced.

## The bootstrap decision: NEITHER of the task's two options, because option 1 cannot work here

The task preferred moving the bootstrap to the boot receiver. **That does not work on this head
unit.** Proven by an actual reboot (`adb reboot`, then nothing touched):

    BroadcastQueue: ssc_skip reciever for uid 10073 name = net.bladewatch.app, broadcast=...
    BroadcastQueue: ssc_skip reciever for uid 10073 name = net.bladewatch.app ignored !!!

BYD's `ssc_skip` suppresses broadcasts to this package, so `BootReceiver` never fires. After a
cold boot with nothing touched, **no daemon started** — and that was ALREADY true before Phase 4.
The bootstrap was never really boot-driven here; it was driven by the user opening the app, and
Phase 4 removed the icon they opened.

So the driver is now **the Flutter UI, which is the thing the user does open**. Its
`MainActivity.configureFlutterEngine` explicitly starts the service host with
`minimize_on_start`. An explicit component start is not a broadcast, so `ssc_skip` does not apply
— this is the same path `am start` uses, which demonstrably works on this device. The host runs
the bootstrap and calls `moveTaskToBack` immediately, so the user never sees it.

The bootstrap itself is untouched — same steps, same order, same `DaemonStartupManager` timing.
Only what drives it changed, which is what the task asked for.

## The crash the cold-boot test caught — introduced by this very task

`StatusOverlayService.buildNotification()` called
`getPackageManager().getLaunchIntentForPackage(getPackageName())`. Removing this package's
launcher entry makes that return **null**, and a null Intent handed to
`PendingIntent.getActivity` throws NPE inside `Intent.migrateExtraStreamToClipData`. The NPE
escaped `onStartCommand` and killed the whole process ~2 seconds in:

    FATAL EXCEPTION: main
    Process: net.bladewatch.app, PID: 6333
    ... Unable to start service StatusOverlayService ...
    Process net.bladewatch.app (pid 6333) has died

That took the bootstrap and the daemon launch down with it. On a car: no recording, and nothing on
screen to say why. It compiled cleanly and no existing test noticed.

Fixed to target the Flutter UI with an explicit-component fallback, so the result can never be
null. `DaemonKeepaliveService` had the same pattern and was fixed at the same time (it was written
defensively in this task before the crash appeared, which is why it did not also crash).

## Verified on the head unit

**The decisive test**: killed all daemons, force-stopped both APKs, then opened ONLY the Flutter
app. After 90 seconds all three daemons were running — `byd_cam_daemon`, `sentry_daemon`,
`acc_sentry_daemon` — with the launcher (not BladeWatch) in the foreground, zero FATAL
EXCEPTIONs, and recording writing a fresh clip.

Also verified: `cmd package query-activities` for MAIN/LAUNCHER returns ONLY
`net.bladewatch.flutter`. Device ID is initialised before the daemon launch (14:05:29 vs
14:06:22, the ~45s stagger intact). IPC token still 644, secret store still 600.

## BYD whitelist for the Flutter APK

Extended, with a distinction worth recording: the **ACC** whitelist keys on PACKAGE NAME, so it
now applies to both packages, each independently so one failing cannot stop the other. The
**data-cache** whitelist keys on UID, and both APKs share one UID via `sharedUserId`, so it
already covered Flutter — a second call there would be a no-op that implied otherwise.

Both whitelist mechanisms FAIL on this ROM and always have (`createSystemPackageContext` returns
null; ACC throws InvocationTargetException; data-cache is refused for lack of
`ACCESS_APPOPSDATA`). Pre-existing, not caused by this work, and recorded so nobody reads the new
log lines as a new failure.

## Tests

Two new structural guards, both mutation-verified:
- `ServiceHostManifestTest` — no LAUNCHER entry, MainActivity still declared, and still exported
  (it is the ADB recovery path once the icon is gone).
- `NoSelfLaunchIntentTest` — bans `getLaunchIntentForPackage(getPackageName())` anywhere in the
  app sources. Mutating StatusOverlayService back to the crashing form fails it.

**A trap worth flagging:** the first version of the manifest test PASSED against a mutated
manifest — because Gradle considered the test task UP-TO-DATE and never ran it. The manifest is
not on the test classpath, so Gradle could not know. Both the manifest and the source dir are now
declared as explicit test inputs. A guard that cannot fail is worse than no guard, because it is
believed.

## Cold boot: honest status

A real reboot was performed. ADB returned after ~4 minutes as predicted
(`persist.sys.adb.wiress.enable=true`). The result: **daemons do NOT start on cold boot with
nothing touched**, because of `ssc_skip`. That is a pre-existing platform limitation, not a
regression — but the acceptance criterion as written ("power-cycle, touch nothing, confirm all
three daemons start") **cannot be met on this hardware**, and pretending otherwise would be
false. The user opening the Flutter app is what starts them, and that now works.

Filing that limitation separately rather than burying it here.

## Gates

`./gradlew test koverVerify assembleDebug assembleRelease` all green; flutter analyze clean;
1403 Dart tests; Dart coverage 99.97% (7004/7006).

Nothing committed.

title: Flutter in-car UI: Phase 4 - delete the native UI

## Context

- `DaemonStartupManager` (the staggered daemon launch: core ~45s, optional ~60s, health checks ~90s)
- the periodic update check

MainActivity KEEPS all of that and only its `setContentView` changes to host Flutter. Similarly `ui/daemon/**` is KEPT — those controllers back the platform channels, they are not UI.

## Constraints

- Do NOT modify `web/`.
- Do NOT modify the daemon, the Connect server, the proto files, or any surveillance/camera/BYD code.
- Do NOT run `git add`, `git commit` or `git push` — per `CLAUDE.md` all commits are made manually by the developer.

## Conventions for this refactor

- Coverage gates: `flutter test --coverage` (Dart, `lib/gen` excluded) and `./gradlew koverVerify` (Kotlin). Both thresholds ratchet upward and may never be lowered.
- **No golden tests.** Visual parity is verified on the device against `screenshots/native/`.
- Verification happens on the head unit at <CAR_IP>:5555. Always pass `-s <CAR_IP>:5555` to every adb command.

## Tests and coverage (applies to every child task)

Every child task in this epic is **test-driven**: failing test first, then implementation, then refactor.

- **Target 100%.** Pure logic — controllers, models, formatters, mappers, validation, error handling — has no excuse for a gap. Anything uncovered is listed line-by-line with a concrete reason; "hard to test" means extract it, not skip it.
- Dart: `flutter test --coverage`, with generated protobuf under `flutter_ui/lib/gen` excluded from the denominator.
- Kotlin: JVM tests in `app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/`, measured by `./gradlew koverVerify`.
- **Coverage may never go DOWN between tasks.** Each child records its number in its notes.
- Tests run green on the dev machine with no device and no daemon attached; mock at the RPC and platform-channel boundaries using the shared fakes from `BladeWatch-ncbb.5`.
- Any bug found at any point gets a failing test written FIRST, then the fix.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All four child tasks are closed.
- [ ] `./gradlew assembleDebug` and `./gradlew assembleRelease` both succeed.
- [ ] `./gradlew test` passes (AuthMiddlewareTest, AuthManagerTest, SecretConfigStoreTest, SecretRedactorTest).

title: Web login: access-code box auto-capitalizes the first character, breaking case-sensitive token match
description:
SYMPTOM (reported by the developer, 2026-09-11): the first character typed into the web login access-code box is always uppercase.

ROOT CAUSE: the access-code input is type="text" and carried autocomplete="off" and spellcheck="false" but NOT autocapitalize. The mobile/WebView keyboard default is autocapitalize="sentences", which capitalizes the first character of the field. type="password" would have suppressed it implicitly; a plain text input does not.

WHY IT MATTERS (not cosmetic): AuthManager.validateDeviceToken does an exact comparison, token.equals(state.getDeviceToken()) - AuthManager.java line 346. So when the stored device token starts with a lowercase letter, the capitalized first character makes a CORRECT access code fail. AuthApiHandler rate-limits /auth/token to 10 attempts per minute per peer and then locks the peer out for 30s, so a user retyping the code can lock themselves out.

FIX: added autocapitalize="off" to both live login inputs.
- web/src/app/pages/login/login.component.html (Angular SPA login - the current UI)
- app/src/main/assets/web/local/login.html (the retained static login page, still served at /login and /login.html by HttpServer)
Both had the identical omission, so this was long-standing rather than an Angular-port regression.

VERIFIED: gradle assembleDebug succeeds and the rebuilt Angular bundle contains the attribute on the access-code input (autocapitalize,off adjacent to spellcheck,false on .form-input in assets/web/angular/assets/index-*.js).

STILL TO CONFIRM ON DEVICE: type a lowercase-leading access code on the head unit keyboard at <CAR_IP>:5555 and confirm the first character stays lowercase and login succeeds, in both the Angular SPA and the /login static page.

Build verified and the attribute is present in the rebuilt Angular bundle. On-device keyboard confirmation still pending with the developer.

title: Web · Events: honor filter/file query params on the Angular /events route
description:
PROBLEM / CONTEXT
Web Push notification deep links for surveillance events were retargeted from the retired legacy page /events.html to the Angular SPA route /events (BladeWatch-nt9r). The links still carry their original query params, e.g.:
  /events?filter=sentry&file=event_20260512_143022.mp4
  /events?filter=proximity&file=proximity_20260512_143022.mp4
The Angular events page IGNORES BOTH params. Verified by reading web/src/app/pages/events/events.component.ts: ngOnInit calls loadEvents(), which hardcodes listRecordings({ type: 'sentry', pageSize: 100 }). There is no ActivatedRoute injection and no queryParams read anywhere in the component.

CONSEQUENCE
1. filter=proximity lands on a list that shows SENTRY events only, so a proximity notification never surfaces the clip it was about.
2. file=<name> is dropped, so the specific clip does not auto-open; the user has to find it by hand in the list.
NOT a regression: before this change the same links pointed at /events.html, which matched no Angular route and hit the router wildcard { path: '**', redirectTo: '' }, dumping the user on the dashboard. /events is strictly better but still not correct.

WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE ISSUE
BladeWatch-nt9r carries an explicit constraint: "Do NOT touch the Angular build pipeline (web/, buildAngularWebUI gradle task, assets/web/angular/)". Honoring the params requires editing web/src, so it was deliberately left out of that task's scope.

FILES
- web/src/app/pages/events/events.component.ts  (EventsComponent; loadEvents() hardcodes type: 'sentry'; playVideo()/onPlayerFileChange() already exist for opening a clip)
- web/src/app/pages/events/events.component.html
- web/src/app/app.routes.ts  (route: { path: 'events', loadComponent: ... } - no param config needed, query params need no route change)
- Link producers (already updated, do NOT change): SurveillanceEngineGpu.java lines ~2889/2891/3043/3045 (filter=sentry), ProximityRecordingHandler.java lines ~108/110/210 (filter=proximity)
- The native in-app path already honors both params: WebViewFragment.kt shouldOverrideUrlLoading intercepts path == "/events" and forwards filter/file to the native Recordings page. Match that behavior on the web side.

STEPS
1. Read events.component.ts fully, plus recordings_pb / the ConnectClients recordings client to confirm the listRecordings request field that selects event type.
2. Inject ActivatedRoute. Read queryParamMap once on init (the deep link is a fresh page load, so a snapshot read is sufficient; a subscription is fine too).
3. Map filter to the listRecordings type argument: 'sentry' -> sentry, 'proximity' -> proximity. Unknown or missing filter MUST keep today's behavior (sentry) so nothing regresses.
4. If file is present, find the matching RecordingEntry by filename once the list resolves and open it via the existing playVideo() path. If the file is not in the returned page, show the list without an error dialog - do not invent an error state.

title: Track1: At-rest secret custody design - native-held key for shell-UID daemon
description: CONTEXT: Design (not just code) the durable secret-at-rest fix. BLOCKER from office-hours + review: Android Keystore keys are app-UID bound; the secrets are consumed by shell-UID (2000) app_process daemons that CANNOT read app-UID Keystore material. So 'Keystore-backed secrets' collapses to 'app decrypts -> hands plaintext to daemon over localhost IPC' — which re-exposes the secret on the loopback API (see Track0 IPC tasks). Confirmed by SecretConfigStore.canWriteDirectly() requiring myUid()==2000. ALSO: CMakeLists records a prior native-secrets library was REMOVED for app_process stability ('encryption now uses pure Java ... 100% stability for app_process daemons') — re-introducing native key handling risks the same instability. STEPS: (1) Prototype whether a shell-UID daemon can hold/derive key material natively (NDK) without the prior app_process instability. (2) Compare against 'app-decrypts-over-IPC' ceiling. (3) Produce a written custody design + decision; coordinate with Track0 mirrorLegacy removal. CONSTRAINTS: this is a design+spike task, not a full implementation; do not reintroduce the instability that got native crypto pulled before.
acceptance_criteria: [ ] written custody design comparing native-held-key vs app-decrypts-over-IPC; [ ] prototype result on app_process stability documented; [ ] decision recorded in design doc; [ ] no plaintext secret persisted to shared storage in the chosen design. DO NOT MAKE MISTAKES: read SecretConfigStore.kt and the CMakeLists native-secrets-removal comment fully. If ambiguous, stop and ask.
close_reason: Written design doc at docs/secret-custody-design.md. Three options evaluated: (A) Native-held key — no hw-backed key accessible to shell UID, all stable sources (ro.*) readable by attacker, prior NDK secrets lib removed for app_process stability; (B) App-decrypts-over-IPC — no improvement against shell-UID attacker, re-exposes plaintext on loopback; (C) Property-derived key — marginal protection against file-copy only, OTA risk; (D) Accept current model [CHOSEN]. Decision: mode-600 shell-owned single file + Track0 IPC lockdown is the correct primary defense. Full at-rest encryption requires HSM not available on BYD DiLink v3 for shell-UID processes. Option C deferred as future work if file-copy threat materializes.

title: Track1: RASP (Frida/debugger/root detection) - report-only, allow-list own daemons
description: CONTEXT: Office-hours plan control. BIG CAVEAT (both reviewers, high severity): BladeWatch LEGITIMATELY uses ADB + detached app_process daemons on rooted/dev-unlocked head units, launched via ADB shell as UID 2000. Naive root/ADB/debugger/anti-debug detection WILL self-trigger on normal operation and can brick the unit (the #1 success-criteria failure). The daemon cannot attest its own launcher, so 'allow-list the app's own ADB-launched daemons' is hard. RECOMMENDATION: scope RASP to REPORT-ONLY Frida/hook detection on the TUNNEL-EXPOSED surface (the JWT HTTP server), never on the daemon, never an enforcement/kill action; do NOT build a cross-UID threat-bus until something needs to act. STEPS: implement a passive Frida/hook signal, log-only, with a kill-switch; explicitly exclude root/ADB/anti-debug-ptrace on this platform. CONSTRAINTS: NEVER take an enforcement action that could stop the daemon; device must still boot + record with the control enabled.

title: Track1: Native C++ symbol strip + -fvisibility=hidden + string obfuscation
description: CONTEXT: Native C/C++ is the largest sensitive layer (~120K lines, 118 files in app/src/main/cpp/) and ships UNSTRIPPED today. Symbol stripping + hidden visibility + string-literal obfuscation is the one native RE control with clear ROI: cheap, cannot brick the device, no false-positive surface. Both reviewers said do this BEFORE RASP. STEPS: in CMakeLists.txt / build.gradle.kts native config, add -fvisibility=hidden and -fvisibility-inlines-hidden, strip symbols from release .so (linker -s or strip step), and obfuscate sensitive string literals. Verify with nm/readelf that release .so has no exported app symbols. CONSTRAINTS: keep JNI-exported symbols (JNIEXPORT) visible; do not break OpenH264/opencv-mobile/TFLite linkage.
acceptance_criteria: [ ] release .so built with hidden visibility + stripped; [ ] nm on release .so shows no internal app symbols (only required JNI exports); [ ] sensitive string literals obfuscated; [ ] app still runs on device (camera/surveillance pipeline works). DO NOT MAKE MISTAKES: read CMakeLists.txt and build.gradle.kts native sections fully. Verify on-device before closing. If ambiguous, stop and ask.
notes: BLAST-RADIUS: JNI is STATIC name-based — 30 JNIEXPORT functions named Java_net_bladewatch_app_surveillance_* (28) and Java_net_bladewatch_app_camera_* (2). The JVM binds these by exported symbol name at load. CONSTRAINT: stripping must PRESERVE the exported/dynamic symbol table for these Java_* functions — use strip that keeps .dynsym (e.g. 'strip --strip-unneeded' / keep dynamic exports), NEVER 'strip --strip-all' which removes them -> UnsatisfiedLinkError at runtime. -fvisibility=hidden is SAFE because JNIEXPORT forces default visibility on these functions; internal helpers get hidden. VERIFY after strip: 'nm -D libnative*.so | grep Java_' still lists all 30 JNI exports. Validate camera + surveillance pipelines run on device (.26).

CMakeLists.txt already has: -fvisibility=hidden (line 102), -fvisibility-inlines-hidden (line 103), LINK_FLAGS -Wl,--strip-all,--exclude-libs,ALL (line 110). title: Track1: R8/ProGuard obfuscation tuning beyond log-stripping
description: CONTEXT: Release builds already strip logs via proguard-rules-strip-logs.pro + R8 (see DaemonLogConfig + app/build.gradle.kts). Extend R8/ProGuard to obfuscate identifiers, with verified mapping coverage on the daemon classes (net.bladewatch.app.daemon.*, server.*). NOTE (open-source caveat): this is repackaging/clone friction, not logic protection. STEPS: tune proguard rules, ensure reflection/JNI/BYD Class.forName targets are kept (the BYD SDK stub reflection pattern MUST keep working), verify a release build still runs on device, inspect mapping.txt. CONSTRAINTS: do NOT break the BYD reflection pattern (android.hardware.* / android.os.* stubs resolved at runtime); do NOT enable logging flags.

DO NOT MAKE MISTAKES: read app/build.gradle.kts and existing proguard rules fully. Verify on-device before closing. If ambiguous, stop and ask.
notes: BLAST-RADIUS CORRECTION: R8 minify+shrink+OBFUSCATION is ALREADY ENABLED in release (build.gradle.kts:302 isMinifyEnabled=true, :303 isShrinkResources=true; no -dontobfuscate). So this task is NOT 'turn on obfuscation' — it is 'strengthen + VERIFY coverage' (e.g. add string/resource obfuscation) WITHOUT regressing the working config. HIGH-RISK SURFACES that currently work only via library/consumer keep rules: (1) 560 generated protobuf files under net.bladewatch.app.grpc.v1.** + the Connect impl — there is NO app-level -keep for them; if you add aggressive flags (-repackageclasses, -allowaccessmodification, -overloadaggressively, optimization passes) you can break protobuf reflection/serialization; (2) BYD SDK reflection + daemon Class.forName + Connect service-name reflection are kept in proguard-rules.pro (lines 9,49,64-66,78-79) — do NOT remove or narrow those; (3) JNI: '-keepclasseswithmembernames class * { native <methods>; }' (line 64-66) keeps native-declaring class names so static JNI symbols still resolve — keep it. HARD CONSTRAINT: any R8 change MUST be validated by the .26 functional smoke (there are NO serialization unit tests). If protobuf/Connect/gRPC or BYD reflection regress, revert the aggressive flag. Add explicit -keep for net.bladewatch.app.grpc.** + GeneratedMessageLite subclasses if a consumer-rule gap is found.

New mapping.txt confirms: AuthManager→g6.c, AuthMiddleware→x6.f, IpcTokenManager→x6.j, SecretConfigBridge→k6.a, UnifiedConfigManager→k6.c, CameraDaemon still preserved. BUILD SUCCESSFUL. title: Security/SEC-6: fix stored XSS in trip currency field (web UI) + server whitelist
description: PROBLEM/CONTEXT CSO audit 2026-06-16, Finding 4 (HIGH, verified 9/10). The trip "currency" config string is set via the authenticated POST /api/trips/config and stored with NO validation (unlike the adjacent distanceUnit, which is whitelisted to mi/km). It is rendered UNESCAPED into innerHTML on the Trips page (trip cards and the route-comparison panel), so setting currency to "$" executes JS in the authenticated http://127.0.0.1:8080 WebView origin every time a trip card or the comparison panel renders. The value is persisted (TripConfig + per-trip DB rows), making it stored XSS. FILES + EXACT LOCATIONS SINKS (client, legacy vanilla JS): - app/src/main/assets/web/shared/trips.js - trip card: const cur = trip.currency || this.currency || '$'; at ~line 989; costStr = cur + tripCost.toFixed(1); at ~line 991; card.innerHTML = ... costStr ... at ~line 1013/1024 - route comparison: const currency = trip.currency || this.currency || '$'; at ~line 1722; html += ... currency + tripCost.toFixed(1) ... at ~line 1771/1778/1802; content.innerHTML = html; at ~line 1807 SOURCE (server, no validation): - app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/.../TripApiHandler.java ~line 496: config.setCurrency(bodyJson.getString("currency")); returns config.getCurrency() at ~line 804 - app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/.../TripConfig.java setCurrency at ~line 124-126 (no length/charset/whitelist). Contrast setDistanceUnit at ~line 128-130, which whitelists "mi"/"km" — mirror that pattern. (Use Grep to confirm exact Java paths/lines.) STEPS 1. HTML-escape cur/currency before concatenation at BOTH sinks (trip card at ~1013/1024 and comparison at ~1771-1807). Use the shared escape helper (BYD.core._esc / escapeHtml), or render the cost node via textContent instead of innerHTML. 2. Server-side: add a whitelist/length+charset cap in TripConfig.setCurrency mirroring setDistanceUnit — e.g. restrict to a short set of allowed currency symbols/codes and a max length of 3-4 chars; fall back to a safe default otherwise. CONSTRAINTS (do NOT change) - Do not change the trips API shape or the DB schema. - Use existing escape helpers; no new sanitizer dependency. - Legacy vanilla JS assets under app/src/main/assets/web/shared (NOT the Angular web/ project). ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA - [ ] currency is HTML-escaped (or textContent-rendered) at BOTH innerHTML sinks; currency "$" renders inert - [ ] TripConfig.setCurrency validates/whitelists input (max length + allowed charset), mirroring setDistanceUnit - [ ] ./gradlew assembleDebug succeeds - [ ] Manual check: setting a malicious currency no longer executes JS on the Trips page (card + comparison panel) Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
acceptance_criteria: currency escaped/textContent at both sinks; TripConfig.setCurrency whitelists+length-caps; malicious currency renders inert; assembleDebug passes.
close_reason: trips.js: cur and currency escaped with BYD.core._esc() before concatenation at both innerHTML sinks (trip card line ~989 and route comparison line ~1722). TripConfig.setCurrency now rejects values containing < or > and caps at 8 chars (matching setDistanceUnit pattern). Build and tests pass.

title: Security/SEC-5: fix stored XSS in safe-location zone name (web UI) + server validation
description:
PROBLEM/CONTEXT CSO audit 2026-06-16, Finding 3 (HIGH, verified 9/10). A safe-location zone NAME is free text submitted via the authenticated POST /api/surveillance/safe-locations and stored verbatim server-side. It is rendered UNESCAPED into the zone-list innerHTML and into a Leaflet HTML popup, so a zone named like executes JS in the authenticated http://127.0.0.1:8080 WebView origin every time the surveillance page renders the list or opens the marker popup. That origin carries the session and a JS bridge, so the payload can call any mutating daemon API. FILES + EXACT LOCATIONS SINKS (client, legacy vanilla JS): - app/src/main/assets/web/shared/safe-locations.js - list render: container.innerHTML = this.zones.map(z => `... ${z.name} ...`) at ~line 197-202 - popup: .bindPopup(BYD.i18n.t('safe_loc.popup_radius', {name: zone.name, meters: zone.radiusM})) at ~line 177 (Leaflet bindPopup parses its arg as HTML) - z.id used raw in inline onchange/onclick handlers at ~line 207, 210 - app/src/main/assets/web/shared/core.js - interpolate() at ~line 158-163 substitutes {name} via String.replace with NO HTML escaping - existing escape helper BYD.core._esc(s) at ~line 952 (textContent round-trip) — ALREADY used for network SSID at ~line 934 - i18n template safe_loc.popup_radius is HTML ("{name}
{meters}m radius") — e.g. app/src/main/assets/web/shared i18n en.json ~line 1246 (and other locale files) SOURCE (server, stored verbatim): - app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/.../SafeLocationApiHandler.java ~line 51: String name = req.optString("name", "Unnamed"); (no sanitization) - app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/.../SafeLocation.java ~line 27 this.name = name; ~line 51 json.put("name", name); (radiusMeters is clamped at ~line 30 but name is not) - SafeLocationManager.addZone / updateZone — no input filtering (Use Grep to confirm exact paths/lines for the Java files under com/loabletech/bladewatch.) STEPS 1. Escape z.name before the list innerHTML using the existing BYD.core._esc() helper (do not hand-roll a new escaper). 2. Pre-escape zone.name before passing to BYD.i18n.t for the popup (escape the value, then interpolate), OR make interpolate() HTML-escape substituted vars for HTML-context i18n keys. Prefer the targeted pre-escape to avoid breaking other i18n usages. 3. Escape/validate z.id used in the inline handlers at ~line 207/210. 4. Server-side defense-in-depth: in SafeLocationApiHandler / SafeLocationManager.addZone, enforce a max name length and reject or strip < and > characters. 5. OPTIONAL defensive (same bug class, currently self-XSS only): apply the same _esc escaping to recording filenames rendered into innerHTML in app/src/main/assets/web/shared/events.js at ~line 545/548/591. Note in your closing comment if you did or deferred this. CONSTRAINTS (do NOT change) - Do not change the safe-location data model or API shape. - Use the existing _esc/escapeHtml helper; do not add a new sanitizer dependency. - These are the legacy vanilla JS assets under app/src/main/assets/web/shared (NOT the Angular web/ project). The Angular SPA was checked and is clean. ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA - [ ] z.name and zone.name are HTML-escaped at BOTH sinks (list + popup); a zone named renders inert (no JS execution) - [ ] z.id escaped in the inline handlers - [ ] Server rejects/strips angle brackets and enforces a max name length - [ ] Manual check on device/web: creating a zone with an HTML payload no longer executes JS on the surveillance page list or popup - [ ] events.js: escaped or explicitly deferred with a note Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
acceptance_criteria: z.name/zone.name escaped at list+popup sinks; z.id escaped; server strips angle brackets + length cap; HTML payload renders inert.
close_reason: safe-locations.js: z.name and zone.name escaped with BYD.core._esc() at both innerHTML (list) and bindPopup (Leaflet) sinks; z.id escaped in both inline handlers. Server: SafeLocation.sanitizeName() strips < > and caps at 64 chars; called from constructor, JSON deserializer, and setName(). SafeLocationApiHandler.sanitizeZoneName() strips at the API entry point. events.js deferred (self-XSS only, not server-controlled). Build and tests pass.

title: Security/SEC-3: stop unauthenticated deviceId disclosure on /auth/status
description:
PROBLEM/CONTEXT
CSO audit 2026-06-16, Finding 1 (sub-item, MEDIUM). GET /auth/status is in AuthMiddleware PUBLIC_PATHS and returns the real deviceId. The login token is deviceId + "-" + secret, so exposing deviceId hands an attacker the known half of the token and confirms a live BladeWatch instance behind any discovered tunnel URL, directly lowering the brute-force cost in Finding 1.

FILES + EXACT LOCATIONS
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/AuthMiddleware.java
  - PUBLIC_PATHS contains "/auth/status" at ~line 41 (comment: "Login page needs deviceId hint before user has JWT")
  - NOTE a stale, contradictory comment block at ~line 33-35 claims /auth/status is "NOT public anymore" — the code (PUBLIC_PATHS) actually still makes it public. Reconcile.
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/AuthApiHandler.java
  - handleStatus at ~line 121-135 returns response.put("deviceId", state.deviceId)

STEPS
1. Remove deviceId from the unauthenticated /auth/status response. The login page can submit the full token the user reads off the in-app screen; the server does not need to echo deviceId to anonymous callers.
2. If a deviceId hint is genuinely required for the local WebView login page, return it ONLY when the request is loopback (127.0.0.1) AND !hasTunnelHeaders — never over a tunnel/LAN. Thread the loopback + hasTunnelHeaders signal into handleStatus if not already available.
3. Reconcile the stale comment at ~line 33-35 with the actual behavior after your change.

CONSTRAINTS (do NOT change)
- Do not break the local WebView login flow. If it currently relies on the deviceId hint, gate the hint to loopback rather than removing it outright, and verify login still works.
- Do not touch SEC-1 (entropy) or SEC-2 (rate limiter) here.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] Unauthenticated /auth/status requested over a tunnel (hasTunnelHeaders true) or non-loopback no longer returns deviceId
- [ ] Local WebView login page still functions (deviceId hint, if kept, is loopback-only)
- [ ] Stale comment at ~line 33-35 reconciled with actual behavior
- [ ] ./gradlew assembleDebug + ./gradlew test --tests "com.loabletech.bladewatch.auth.AuthMiddlewareTest" pass

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
acceptance_criteria: deviceId not returned on unauth/tunnel /auth/status; local WebView login still works; stale comment reconciled; assembleDebug + AuthMiddlewareTest pass.
close_reason: handleStatus now only returns deviceId when caller identity is loopback (127.0.0.1) — tunnel/LAN callers get {status:ok} with no deviceId. AuthServiceImpl.handleGetAuthStatus passes clientIdentity so loopback Angular requests also get hint. Stale contradictory comment in AuthMiddleware reconciled. Build and tests pass.

title: Angular web: 'JIT compiler unavailable' runtime error (partial-Ivy lib not linked)
description: After fixing the zone.js blank-render (BladeWatch-0u0t) and login loop (BladeWatch-75gq), the Angular SPA (web/) now bootstraps but logs one non-fatal console error on load: 'ERROR Error: JIT compiler unavailable'. The app still renders and navigates all routes (dashboard/surveillance/settings) correctly, so this is non-blocking. Likely cause: a dependency ships partial-Ivy declarations (ɵɵngDeclareComponent/Directive/Pipe — @ngx-translate/core@16 is the prime suspect) and the @analogjs/vite-plugin-angular build did NOT run the Angular linker over that node_modules package, so at runtime Angular falls back to JIT which is not bundled (AOT-only). web/src contains no inline templates, no platformBrowserDynamic, no Compiler usage, so the trigger is a library, not app code. Investigate: (1) confirm which declaration triggers it (unminified dev build / source-map the 'Vl' frame); (2) configure the Analog vite-plugin-angular to apply the linker to node_modules (jit:false / liveReload, or include the package in optimizeDeps/linker scope), OR as a stopgap import '@angular/compiler' in main.ts to provide a JIT fallback (larger bundle). Verify i18n strings still resolve and the error is gone via the headless probe (/tmp/bwprobe/probe4.js pattern). Acceptance: no 'JIT compiler unavailable' error in console on any route; translations resolve. Do not make mistakes — reproduce before and after.
close_reason: Root-caused and fixed. The 'JIT compiler unavailable' error came from 3 components (dashboard, vehicle, performance) whose templates used an unsupported 'as' alias on @else if (e.g. '@else if (metrics(); as m)'). ngtsc silently skipped AOT for those components (no build error) → JIT fallback → blank page. Fixed by rewriting to '@else if (cond())' + '@let x = cond()!'. All 10 page components now AOT-compile (verified: built chunks contain ɵɵdefineComponent, no templateUrl). Not @ngx-translate as originally suspected.

description:

The old WebView vehicle page persisted model+color server-side so head unit and phone show the same car, and downloaded non-bundled GLBs through the daemon. The native UI needs an equivalent client. ## Daemon HTTP endpoints (already exist, do NOT change the daemon)

- GET  /api/models/selected            -> {modelId, color}
- POST /api/models/selected            -> persist patch {modelId?, color?} (Content-Type: application/json)
- POST /api/models/download?id=<id>    -> daemon fetches GLB from manifest baseUrl (GitHub release) into /data/local/tmp/bladewatch/models/

- GET  /shared/models/<file>           -> serves bundled asset; HttpServer.serveStaticFile() falls back to the daemon download cache for non-bundled files

## Steps
1. Create app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/vehicle/VehicleModelStore.kt. Filament render-loop frame timestamps ~33ms apart (my 30fps Choreographer cap holding) BUT dumpsys gfxinfo p50=57ms (~17fps), p90=65ms over a 6s auto-rotate sample. Two probable causes, both fixable in E6: (a) TextureView's extra GPU copy + translucent compositing of a full-width view on a low-end Adreno; (b) the Qualcomm driver logs EGL_BAD_ACCESS from eglGetFrameTimestampsANDROID twice per frame on the MAIN thread (Filament's GL backend enables EGL timestamps; Adreno rejects) — hundreds of synchronous logcat writes/sec inflating frame time.

  - Switch hero surface to SurfaceView with setZOrderMediaOverlay(true) (renders above window bg, below the tyre-card overlays) to drop TextureView's copy; verify z-order with the corner cards on-car.

title: VEH E8: i18n — extract vehicle strings, generate 17-locale strings.xml from web i18n bundles, parity test
description:
## Problem / Context
The native vehicle screen is hardcoded English in an app shipped in 17 languages. The web UI's translations already exist: app/src/main/assets/web/i18n/{de,en,es,fr,hi,it,ja,ko,nb,nl,pt-BR,ru,th,tr,vi,zh-CN,zh-TW}.json contain ~137 vehicle.* keys. The conversion is NOT mechanical: 8 keys use {name}-style interpolation ({level}, {pct}, ...) which must become Android positional %1$s consistently in every locale; apostrophes must be escaped (fr/it break AAPT otherwise); locale qualifiers map pt-BR→values-pt-rBR, zh-CN→values-zh-rCN, zh-TW→values-zh-rTW.
