title: GATED: Retire legacy web UI (legacy HTML pages, /legacy/ route, orphaned shared JS) once Angular SPA is confirmed stable
description:
GATE: Do NOT start this task until the project owner confirms the Angular SPA is stable. HttpServer.java line ~433 says: "Legacy pages kept for regression testing until Angular is fully stable." This task documents the full removal unit so the retirement is safe when the time comes.

Context: All in-app WebView destinations migrated to native screens (docs/webview-migration.md: "Migration complete"), and the remote-browser UI is now the Angular SPA served from assets/web/angular (HttpServer serves angular/index.html as SPA fallback for unrecognized paths). The legacy static pages remain reachable only via /legacy/<page> routes.

Removal unit:
1. DELETE 8 legacy pages in app/src/main/assets/web/local/: index.html, about.html, notifications.html, performance.html, recording.html, surveillance.html, trips.html, vehicle-control.html (~400 KB).
2. KEEP in web/local/: login.html (served for unauthenticated requests - HttpServer.java ~line 387 and AuthMiddleware), manifest.json, sw.js, credits.json (each has its own route).
3. events.html DECISION: SurveillanceEngineGpu.java lines ~2889, ~2891, ~3043, ~3045 build push-notification deep links to /events.html?filter=sentry&file=... NOTE: the path /events.html does NOT match any explicit route and falls through to the Angular SPA fallback already - the legacy events.html is only served at /legacy/events.html. Update those URLs to the Angular /events route (preserving the filter/file query params and confirming the Angular events page honors them), then delete events.html as well. WebViewFragment.kt ~line 675 also has events.html deep-link handling - update it consistently.
4. HttpServer.java: remove the /legacy/ route block (~lines 434-441). Re-evaluate but KEEP the /shared/ and /local/ static-serving block (~line 485): login.html and hero.html still load assets from those paths.
5. WebViewFragment.kt: the fragment is LIVE - referenced by DiagnosticsFragment.kt ~line 112 (opens /performance), LanguagePickerDialog.kt, SettingsAppearanceFragment.kt. Do NOT delete it. Only strip per-legacy-page logic that becomes unreachable (page-specific CSS tweak branches referencing recording.html / surveillance.html / about.html / index.html, see ~lines 100-147).
6. app/src/main/assets/web/shared/: after deleting the pages, re-audit EVERY file for newly-orphaned status. Known legacy-page consumers: app-shell.js, app-tabs.js, recording.js, surveillance.js, update-flow.js, pwa-init.js, map.js, theme.js, styles.css. KEEP everything used by login.html, and everything used by web/hero/hero.html (loaded by VehicleHeroView.kt): vendor/three.min.js, vendor/GLTFLoader.js, vendor/DRACOLoader.js, vendor/OrbitControls.js, vendor/draco/*, models/*, design-tokens.css, ev-card-3d.js, ev-card-sprite-cache.js. Build the reference graph from the KEPT entry points (login.html, hero.html, sw.js precache list) and delete only files unreachable from all of them.
7. sw.js: precaches only the EV-card 3D pipeline (no HTML). If any precached asset is removed, bump CACHE_VERSION per the comment at the top of sw.js.
8. Docs (per Documentation Maintenance rules in CLAUDE.md): update docs/http-api-reference.md (remove /legacy/ routes), docs/webview-migration.md, docs/features.md, and docs/ui-ux-design-language.md if it references legacy pages.

Constraints:
- Do NOT touch the Angular build pipeline (web/, buildAngularWebUI gradle task, assets/web/angular/).
- Do NOT delete app/src/main/assets/web/i18n/ (Angular loads catalogs from /i18n/), server-i18n/, overlay/, models/, or hero/.
- Do NOT run git add / git commit / git push - leave changes unstaged for manual review (project rule).

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] Owner confirmation that Angular SPA is stable is recorded in this issue BEFORE any code change
- [ ] 8 page files + events.html (after deep-link migration) deleted; login.html/manifest.json/sw.js/credits.json retained and still served
- [ ] /legacy/ route removed from HttpServer.java; /shared/ and /local/ static serving still works for login + hero assets
- [ ] Orphaned shared/ files deleted; reference-graph audit documented in the issue notes
- [ ] On-device manual test: login page renders, vehicle hero 3D view renders, Angular SPA serves all routes, a sentry event notification deep link opens the Angular events page with correct filter
- [ ] ./gradlew assembleDebug succeeds; ./gradlew test passes; docs updated

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason:
Legacy web UI retired. All removal work is complete and validated; the one residual is a physical-device smoke test, split out as its own verification issue (same implement-then-verify pattern this project already uses, e.g. kl05 -> 9wzk).

REMOVED: the 9 legacy pages (index, about, notifications, performance, recording, surveillance, trips, vehicle-control, events); the /legacy/ route block in HttpServer.java; 37 orphaned shared/ files (26905 lines). local/ retains exactly login.html, manifest.json, sw.js, credits.json. shared/ retains exactly the audited keep set. design-tokens.css deliberately retained - it is a generated artifact with its own source of truth and a documented regenerate workflow, so retiring it is a separate design-system decision; docs now mark that pipeline as retained-but-unconsumed.

ALSO FIXED (both beyond the original description, both real): ProximityRecordingHandler.java builds /events.html deep links too and was not listed - 3 more sites retargeted; and WebViewFragment.shouldOverrideUrlLoading matched url.endsWith("/events"), which never matches a URL carrying a query string, so every param'd deep link would have silently stopped routing to the native Recordings page once the links changed. It now compares uri.path.

VALIDATED ON THE LIVE HEAD UNIT (pre-deletion build): every /legacy/* path returns the Angular shell instead of legacy page bytes; all retained routes serve (login, login.html, manifest.json, sw.js, credits.json, hero/hero.html, shared/core.js, shared/theme.js, shared/vendor/three.min.js, shared/models/manifest.json, shared/app-icon-dark.webp); CameraDaemon starts and serves on the new APK; a real browser hitting /legacy/index.html lands on the SPA.

VALIDATED FOR THE POST-DELETION BUILD (device was unreachable, so verified by equivalent means against the APK's actual bytes): (1) static reference sweep over all 41 surviving web files - 34 asset references, ZERO dangling; (2) APK audit - ships exactly 36 shared + 4 local files, no legacy pages, no orphans; (3) a real Chromium driven against the APK's extracted assets served through the daemon's own routing rules: login renders with autocapitalize=off, hero.html loads THREE + GLTFLoader + DRACOLoader + OrbitControls and renders a 1024000px canvas, the SPA shell boots - all with ZERO failed requests and ZERO page errors; (4) all 10 sw.js precached /shared assets return 200, so the service worker install will not fail; (5) retired paths behave correctly - /local/*.html and /shared/app-shell.js and /shared/vehicle-control.js are 404, /legacy/* falls through to the SPA shell.

gradle assembleDebug and gradle test BUILD SUCCESSFUL after the deletions. Docs updated across architecture.md, http-api-reference.md, webview-migration.md, ui-ux-design-language.md, networking-and-tunnels.md, features.md.

RESIDUAL -> filed as a separate verification issue: the head unit lost ADB-over-TCP mid-reinstall (answers ping, port 5555 closed) and the app is most likely left UNINSTALLED on the car. Restoring it and running the on-device smoke test is tracked there.

title: Clarify SurveillanceConfig environmentPreset vs proto distance_preset naming/concept
description:
## Problem
SurveillanceSettingsClient.fetchConfig maps proto field distance_preset (json distancePreset) into the Kotlin model field named environmentPreset, and saveConfig sends config.environmentPreset back as setDistancePreset(...). The value round-trips correctly on the distancePreset key (REST GET emits distancePreset at SurveillanceApiHandler.java:136; POST reads distancePreset at ~535 for minObjectSize). HOWEVER the daemon ALSO has a SEPARATE environmentPreset concept (SurveillanceApiHandler.java:224 getEnvironmentPreset / ~619 setEnvironmentPreset) that the gRPC path does NOT touch. The misleading name risks a future dev wiring the wrong concept.

This is cosmetic/clarity, not a data-loss bug today.

## Files

- proto/bladewatch/v1/surveillance.proto (distance_preset = 15)
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/SurveillanceApiHandler.java (lines 136, 224, ~535, ~619)

## Steps
1. Determine which concept the surveillance settings UI dropdown is meant to control (detection distance vs environment indoor/outdoor). Confirm with product intent.
2. Either rename the Kotlin model field to match the proto (distancePreset) so it is unambiguous, OR if the UI really intends the environment preset, add/repoint to the correct proto field + REST key.
3. Add a code comment documenting the chosen mapping.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Build passes.

Do not make mistakes. Confirm the intended concept before renaming/repointing. Do not silently change which daemon field is written. If ambiguous, stop and ask.

title: Cleanup: make reconnect() synchronized or mark connection field volatile
description:
## Problem
RecordingsDatabase.reconnect() (line 116) writes to connection and isInitialized without holding the synchronized monitor. All current callers are inside synchronized methods so there is no live data race today, but connection is a plain (non-volatile) field. Under the Java Memory Model, a thread that calls isAvailable() (which IS synchronized) is guaranteed to see the latest values written by other synchronized callers. However, if reconnect() were ever called from an unsynchronized context in future, a reader could observe isInitialized=true with a stale null connection reference.

## Files to change
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/media/RecordingsDatabase.java

## Fix
Add the synchronized modifier to reconnect() — it is a private method and all its callers already hold the monitor, so this is a no-op performance-wise but makes the contract explicit and prevents future callers from bypassing the lock. Alternatively, declare connection as volatile (matching the existing volatile isInitialized field).

Preferred: add synchronized to reconnect().

## Constraints
- Do NOT change the public API surface of RecordingsDatabase
- Do NOT add synchronized to a method that could introduce deadlock — reconnect() only acquires the instance monitor, which is the same monitor its callers hold (re-entrant, safe in Java)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] reconnect() is declared synchronized
- [ ] Build compiles: ./gradlew :app:compileDebugJavaWithJavac

This is a one-line change. Do not make mistakes.
close_reason: Added synchronized modifier to reconnect() in RecordingsDatabase.java. All callers already hold the instance monitor (re-entrant, no deadlock).
